prd_items.subject: Split and attest a fail-closed capability-derived Linux broker supervisor/worker jail

prd_items.description:
ROLE AND ORDER
Representation-first implementation row. It is the first of the two broker hardening rows and has no dependency on broker-process-jailing; broker-process-jailing MUST depend on this row because the jail FD allowlist, Landlock rules, network namespace choice, rlimits, and seccomp arguments must be derived from the finalized capability set. Keep this row pending until an EMIT owner implements and witnesses the whole contract.

CURRENT-STATE WITNESS (corrects the roadmap premise)
* litebox_broker_userland/src/main.rs::linux_main::main creates a temporary Unix listener, constructs PolicyEngine::with_host_guaranteed_rights(ObjectRights::all()), spawns exactly the configured runner, and validates the accepted peer PID.
* litebox_broker_transport_linux_userland/src/unix_socket/host.rs::validate_peer_process uses Linux SO_PEERCRED; UnixStreamHostSetupChannel::from_host_guaranteed converts that deployment proof into PeerCredential::HostGuaranteed.
* litebox_broker_host/src/lib.rs::setup_connection maps that to CallerCredential::HostGuaranteed. BrokerHostAssociation::execute_request/handle_request then dispatch event/pipe operations. handle_request deliberately returns UnsupportedOperation for every SocketRequest.
* litebox_broker_core/src/policy.rs::PolicyEngine::principal_object_rights supplies one coarse ObjectRights bitset per CallerCredential. litebox_broker_core/src/session.rs::ObjectRights contains only WAIT and WRITE and the same bitset is stamped onto every newly-created object reference.
* litebox_broker_protocol/src/message.rs and socket.rs already encode typed IPv4/TCP create/connect/send/receive/shutdown/status requests, but litebox_broker_local has no socket adapter, BrokerControl in litebox/src/broker/mod.rs has no socket methods, and ObjectEntry has no socket object.
* There is no broker filesystem request, local adapter, host handler, core object, or policy decision today. The runner constructs its guest filesystem locally from in-memory/tar layers in litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/lib.rs. This row is therefore a greenfield broker filesystem capability surface plus completion/redesign of the reserved TCP surface, not a refactor of an existing broker filesystem path.

AUTHORITATIVE PRECEDENT
* WASI filesystem 0.2.8 types.wit: all paths are relative to a base directory descriptor; absolute paths, .. or symlink traversal outside that base fail not-permitted; descriptor flags separate read, write, and mutate-directory; open-at derives a descriptor and cannot grant mutation through a read-only base.
* WASI sockets 0.2.8 network.wit/tcp.wit: network is an opaque resource; start-bind/start-connect require a borrowed network resource; access-denied is a first-class failure.
* Wasmtime main crates/wasi/src/ctx.rs and sockets/mod.rs: no preopens and all socket addresses denied by default; preopened_dir binds host and guest paths with FsPerms; socket_addr_check receives (SocketAddr, SocketAddrUse), defaults false, and maps denial to PermissionDenied. SocketAddrUse distinguishes TcpBind/TcpListen/TcpAccept/TcpConnect and UDP uses.

REPRESENTATION CONTRACT
1. Replace PolicyProfile's deployment-wide ObjectRights grant with one immutable, versioned, deny-unknown-fields BrokerPolicyV1 loaded and fully validated before the runner is launched:
   BrokerPolicyV1 { schema_version: 1, principal: PrincipalPolicyV1, limits: AuthorityLimitsV1 }.
   The initial production topology has exactly one principal because the broker launches and PID-binds exactly one runner. PrincipalPolicyV1 contains: a stable principal label, explicit event/pipe creation grants, directory_preopens: Vec<DirectoryGrantV1>, and networks: Vec<NetworkGrantV1>. No omitted grant is implied.
2. CapabilityLabel and rule IDs are operator-visible ASCII `[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`, unique within their namespace, and contain no path, credential, hostname, or secret. Reject duplicate labels/rule IDs, unknown fields, zero/overflowing limits, non-UTF-8 manifest strings, non-absolute host/guest roots, non-normalized guest roots, duplicate or ancestor/descendant-overlapping guest roots, more than 64 preopens, more than 64 network grants, or more than 1024 destination rules per network grant. AuthorityLimitsV1 explicitly and positively bounds max_live_handles, max_open_directories (including initial preopens), max_open_files, max_open_sockets, and max_total_file_bytes_in_flight; max_open_directories is at most 64 and at least the preopen count, and checked arithmetic proves every configured object/FD ceiling fits the later deterministic FD ranges and RLIMIT_NOFILE.
3. DirectoryGrantV1 is `{ label, host_path, guest_path, rights }`. The supervisor opens host_path exactly once before any jail is entered as a directory FD with O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC; it never sends host_path to the runner. guest_path is the absolute, normalized mount name exported to the runner. Directory rights are the closed least-privilege labels STAT, READ_DIR, OPEN_READ, OPEN_WRITE, CREATE_FILE, CREATE_DIR, REMOVE_FILE, REMOVE_DIR, RENAME_SOURCE, RENAME_TARGET, and READ_LINK. File rights are the closed labels STAT, READ, WRITE, SET_SIZE, and SYNC. A derived file/directory handle carries only the requested subset authorized by its parent; rights can be attenuated but never amplified.
4. Every broker reference stores a tagged ObjectAuthority, not an untyped shared bitset: Event(EventRights), PipeReader(PipeRights), PipeWriter(PipeRights), Directory(DirectoryRights), File(FileRights), Network(NetworkRights), Socket(SocketRights). Event rights are WAIT/ADD/CONSUME; reader endpoints are WAIT/READ; writer endpoints are WAIT/WRITE. Network v1 has TCP_CONNECT only. A connected socket has WAIT/STATUS/SEND/RECEIVE/SHUTDOWN. The kind tag makes using directory bits as socket bits unrepresentable. Every reference also stores session_id and CapabilityLabel; handles remain broker-minted and session-scoped.
5. Negotiation exports a bounded list of broker-minted initial capability descriptors `{handle, kind, label, guest_path?, rights}` only after peer authentication. The runner cannot supply an initial handle. ConnectSocketRequest gains an explicit network_capability handle. Every path operation starts from an explicit directory handle. Broker protocol version is bumped atomically across protocol/wire/local/host; old peers receive UnsupportedVersion before shared-memory activation.
6. Filesystem v1 wire/local/host/core surface is explicit and closed: Directory requests OpenAt, StatAt, ReadDirectory, CreateDirectoryAt, RemoveDirectoryAt, UnlinkFileAt, RenameAt, and ReadlinkAt; File requests ReadAt, WriteAt, Stat, SetSize, and Sync. OpenAt carries path flags, CREATE/EXCLUSIVE/TRUNCATE/DIRECTORY flags, and requested tagged rights. Data uses the existing bounded shared-buffer leases. Hard-link and symlink creation are intentionally UnsupportedOperation in v1; they are not silently passed through.
7. Broker-relative paths are UTF-8, at most 4096 bytes, use `/`, and contain no empty, `.` or `..` component and no leading `/`; the base itself is addressed by its existing handle, not by `.`. Final symlink following is opt-in. Every descendant resolution uses Linux openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, O_NOFOLLOW when final-follow is absent, and the original/derived directory FD; lexical canonicalization is never an authorization decision. Internal symlinks may resolve only while the kernel proves the result remains beneath the preopen. No fallback path walker is permitted.
8. NetworkGrantV1 is `{ label, uses, rules }`; v1 accepts only TCP_CONNECT and numeric IPv4 SocketAddressV4. DestinationRuleV1 is an ordered `{ id, action: allow|deny, cidr, inclusive_port_ranges }`; first match wins and the implicit terminal rule is deny. CIDRs and port ranges are canonicalized and validated at load time. DNS, IPv6, bind, listen, accept, UDP, raw sockets, and reconnect are explicitly unsupported in v1 and fail before a host syscall.
9. The per-destination seam is the total, in-process SocketPolicy hook `authorize(SocketPolicyContext) -> SocketPolicyDecision`, where context carries principal label, network capability label, NetworkUse::TcpConnect, protocol/family, and the exact canonical numeric destination; decision is Allow{rule_id} or Deny{rule_id_or_default, reason}. Production installs the immutable manifest evaluator; default construction installs DenyAll. The hook runs after handle/kind/rights validation and immediately before the one nonblocking host connect syscall. A denial performs no socket syscall, leaves the socket Unconnected, and returns ErrorCode::PolicyDenied. SocketError is reserved for host/network outcomes; remove the duplicate SocketError::PolicyDenied meaning. A hook panic is caught before connect and fatally fails that association with Internal, so no allow can be synthesized from policy failure.
10. On allowed connect, the socket object records the authorizing network capability identity and exact remote endpoint before exposing Connected/Connecting. Subsequent send/receive authority comes only from that connected socket; it cannot change destination. If DNS is ever added, the invariant already fixes its shape: name lookup is a separate denied-by-default capability and every resolved numeric address must be checked after resolution and before connect; a hostname check alone can never authorize an IP.
11. litebox_broker_local gains directory/file/socket typed adapters; litebox/src/broker/mod.rs::BrokerControl and BrokerLocalControl gain the matching bounded calls. The runner mounts one broker-backed filesystem at each exported guest_path and routes broker-backed TCP sockets through the negotiated Network capability. Host paths and policy internals never cross the local boundary.

PRECONDITIONS
* The accepted connection has already passed validate_peer_process against the exact Child PID and setup_connection has produced HostGuaranteed; an unauthenticated/unknown credential receives no capabilities.
* BrokerPolicyV1 is a regular, no-symlink operator input whose file and parent components are owned by root or the invoking deployment identity and are not group/world writable. All preopen roots are opened successfully before runner launch.
* Linux openat2 is available whenever directory_preopens is non-empty. Missing openat2 is a startup UnsupportedPlatform failure, never a racy userspace fallback.
* Capability and FD limits are internally consistent and fit BrokerCoreLimits and the later jail's computed RLIMIT_NOFILE.

INVARIANTS
* Default is zero ambient filesystem/network authority. Authority exists only as a session-owned, kind-tagged broker handle descended from a manifest grant.
* Principal authentication, capability selection, rights checks, path confinement, and destination decision all precede the host side effect. Denial is side-effect-free.
* Handle guessing, reuse after close, cross-session use, and wrong-kind use reveal no other session state and cannot reach a host object.
* Rights are monotone decreasing across derivation; close/session teardown releases the host FD/socket and all quota charges exactly once.
* An absolute path, malformed path, symlink/magic-link escape, or destination without an Allow match cannot reach an ambient host path/network syscall.
* Existing event/pipe behavior is available only when the manifest explicitly grants its object class; there is no compatibility `ObjectRights::all()` bypass.
* Every request and response remains bounded by manifest limits, wire bounds, shared-buffer bounds, and checked arithmetic.

FAILURE BEHAVIOR
* CLI/schema/ownership/duplicate/limit/preopen validation fails before runner spawn, emits one structured `policy_load_failed` reason, and exits nonzero; no permissive policy is substituted.
* Unknown, stale, foreign-session, or wrong-kind handles return UnknownObject. A known same-session handle missing the required tagged right returns InvalidRights. Explicit path/destination policy denial returns PolicyDenied. Malformed or oversized wire/path input aborts the association as MalformedRequest. Host filesystem and network failures use closed FilesystemError and SocketError enums, never raw errno passthrough.
* Failed open/create/connect never installs a handle, consumes quota, truncates a file, or changes socket state. Partial data operations report the exact completed byte count under existing shared-buffer lease rules.
* Policy hook panic/internal invariant failure occurs before the host action and aborts the association; the userland supervisor then treats broker loss as fatal to its runner.

OBSERVABILITY
* A dedicated inherited audit FD emits newline-delimited JSON schema `litebox.broker.audit.v1`; stderr is the human fallback. Startup records policy SHA-256, counts/limits, principal/capability labels, and opened preopen identities without host paths. Every authority-creating decision (initial export, OpenAt/create/rename/remove, socket connect) records monotonic decision_id, instance/session/request IDs, principal label, capability label, operation, allow/deny, rule ID/reason, duration, and protocol error. Relative paths are not logged; record length plus HMAC-SHA-256 under a fresh 256-bit per-instance key sampled with getrandom before runner launch, carried only in the sealed bootstrap, never emitted, and zeroized at teardown. Numeric network endpoint is logged because it is the authorization subject. Never log payload bytes, host paths, credentials, or manifest contents.
* Periodic/final audit snapshots expose allow_total, deny_total by reason, policy_error_total, live_handles, open_files, open_sockets, and quota high-water marks. A clean session-final snapshot must return all live/open counters to baseline. Audit write failure fails the association in production mode rather than running unobserved.

PLATFORM SUPPORT
* Production wiring is Linux x86_64, matching litebox_runner_linux_userland's cfg. Protocol/core representations remain no_std/portable. On non-Linux, or on Linux without required openat2 when preopens exist, startup returns UnsupportedPlatform and never silently runs with ambient access.
* v1 supports broker-backed numeric IPv4 TCP client streams and the listed filesystem operations only; every other family/protocol/operation is a closed UnsupportedOperation before host action.

POSTCONDITIONS
* A successfully negotiated session exposes exactly the manifest's initial labeled capabilities and no host path; every derived object can be traced to one initial grant and has no stronger rights.
* Real guest filesystem/TCP operations traverse local -> wire -> host -> policy -> confined host object and return stable broker errors; event/pipe compatibility also traverses explicit grants.
* Session/process teardown leaves no live broker reference, FD/socket, shared-buffer lease, or quota charge.

LIVE PRODUCTION ACCEPTANCE (no synthetic test files)
On a real Linux x86_64 host, launch the release litebox-broker-userland and release litebox_runner_linux_userland through their production Unix/memfd/control-ring path with one BrokerPolicyV1. The manifest grants: event/pipe; a read-only preopen mounted at `/cap/ro`; a read-write preopen mounted at `/cap/rw`; and TCP_CONNECT only to one loopback server address/port.
1. A real guest reads an allowed file, writes/creates only under `/cap/rw`, and receives permission denial for write under `/cap/ro`, an absolute path, `..`, a same-name path outside a grant, and internal symlinks escaping the root. The outside sentinel remains byte-identical.
2. The guest completes connect/send/receive against the allowlisted loopback listener. An adjacent port and a non-allowlisted address return policy denial, and listener/packet counters prove no connect syscall/SYN reached either denied endpoint.
3. A stale/guessed/cross-session/wrong-kind handle returns UnknownObject; requesting a stronger derived right returns InvalidRights; broker/runner remain healthy after recoverable denials.
4. Existing event and pipe operations still complete only with their explicit manifest grants; removing either grant makes creation PolicyDenied.
5. Audit JSONL is machine-parseable, ties every allow/deny to policy hash, labels, request and rule/reason, contains no host path/payload, and final live/open counters return to baseline. `/proc/<broker-pid>/fd` returns to its startup census after session teardown.
Acceptance is the observed production binary/transport/guest behavior and host sentinel/network state, not a unit or synthetic test suite.

CRITICAL CURRENT FILES/SYMBOLS
litebox_broker_userland/src/main.rs::{linux_main::main,serve_runner,accept_runner_stream,dispatch_requests,run_worker}; litebox_broker_transport_linux_userland/src/unix_socket/host.rs::{validate_peer_process,peer_process_id,UnixStreamHostSetupChannel::from_host_guaranteed}; litebox_broker_host/src/lib.rs::{setup_connection,BrokerHostAssociation::execute_request,handle_request}; litebox_broker_core/src/policy.rs::{PolicyProfile,PolicyEngine,PolicyEngine::principal_object_rights}; litebox_broker_core/src/session.rs::{CallerCredential,ObjectRights,ObjectReference,ObjectEntry,BrokerSession::create_object_reference,BrokerSession::authorize_use_object}; litebox_broker_core/src/lib.rs::{BrokerCore,BrokerCoreLimits}; litebox_broker_protocol/src/message.rs::{BrokerOperation,SocketRequest,BrokerResult}; litebox_broker_protocol/src/socket.rs::{CreateSocketRequest,ConnectSocketRequest,SocketConnectionStatus,SocketError}; litebox_broker_local/src/lib.rs::BrokerLocal; litebox/src/broker/mod.rs::{BrokerControl,BrokerLocalControl}; litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/{lib.rs::run,broker.rs::connect}.

SOURCES

prd_items.description: User-requested (2026-08-10), split from the combined 'interactive keyboard input' request since this half is Windows-only and cannot be hardware-verified on this session's Apple Silicon macOS machine (no Windows host available). Explored: litebox_shim_windows/src/syscalls/condrv.rs (the ConDrv/console-driver IOCTL handler) only recognizes the LaunchServer handshake IOCTL (lines 303-362) and returns NOT_SUPPORTED for everything else, including any real input-delivery or cursor-position-report (CPR) IOCTLs. A TODO(condrv-shared-console) at litebox_shim_windows/src/lib.rs:619-621 already flags moving console ownership to shared/broker state as unfinished. No hits anywhere in the repo for 'cooked', 'CPR', 'ConPTY', or CreatePseudoConsole -- this is a clean-slate implementation, not a targeted bug fix. Needs a real Windows host to implement and verify against real console API behavior (ReadConsoleInput, cooked vs raw mode line editing, ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT/ENABLE_LINE_INPUT flags, and CPR escape-sequence replies for cursor-position queries) -- deferred from this pass, same reasoning already applied to the Windows CI job investigation and the Windows-only items in this same request batch.
prd_items.subject: Windows console input (cooked-mode handling, cursor-position-report replies) has zero real implementation -- ConDrv IOCTL handler only recognizes the launch handshake

prd_items.description: User-requested (2026-08-10). Explored: litebox/src/net/mod.rs's Network<Platform> (a real userspace smoltcp TCP/IP stack) requires the platform to implement IPInterfaceProvider's send_ip_packet/receive_ip_packet. Linux implements this via a real TUN device (litebox_platform_linux_userland/src/lib.rs:1268-1310) with host-level NAT/masquerade happening externally via host iptables. Windows's implementation is a hard stub: litebox_platform_windows_userland/src/lib.rs:1378-1395, both send_ip_packet and receive_ip_packet are unimplemented!(). No existing TODO comments about Administrator privileges or drivers exist anywhere -- this is a clean-slate feature, not a partially-started one. litebox_broker_* crates are about broker object identity/handles/pipes/policy, not networking -- no NAT infrastructure exists there either. Building a real userspace NAT gateway needing neither Administrator privileges nor a kernel driver on Windows is a substantial, security-sensitive systems project (likely needs something in the class of a raw AF_INET SOCK_RAW socket approach, or a WinDivert-style technique, or a Windows-provided userspace networking primitive -- needs real Windows-specific research, not assumption) that cannot be built or verified without a real Windows host, which this session does not have access to. Tracked as its own large architectural row rather than attempted blind.
prd_items.subject: Windows guest networking is a hard unimplemented!() stub -- building a real userspace NAT gateway (no Administrator/driver) is a substantial new feature needing a Windows host to build and verify

prd_items.description: User-requested (2026-08-10) as 'a deep, multi-stage fork() correctness fix on Windows' describing bugs in an existing fork() implementation (stale untranslated code-page and argv/data pointers after address-space duplication). REAL STATE, verified by direct exploration before any implementation attempt: fork() is not implemented on ANY platform. litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/process.rs:665's do_clone comment says outright 'exit_signal is ignored because we don't support fork yet'; do_clone only accepts clone()/clone3() with required flags VM|THREAD|SIGHAND|FILES -- i.e. a single shared address space, CLONE_THREAD only, never a true child process. litebox_shim_linux/src/lib.rs:358 ('this process model has no fork'), litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/mm.rs:443, and litebox_common_linux/src/mm.rs:264 all reiterate the same. Grepping fork across litebox_platform_windows_userland and litebox_shim_windows returns zero hits. There is no address-translation/remapping machinery for a forked child's memory anywhere to build on. This is NOT a bug fix -- it is a new, foundational feature: a real multi-process model (new host process per guest fork, on Windows specifically a new host process since Windows can't give two logical guest processes the same addresses in one host process; likely similar treatment needed on Linux/macOS too for a genuinely correct implementation, not just Windows), plus code-page vs argv/data-page pointer translation across the fork boundary, plus wait4/waitid + orphan-process reparenting (also entirely absent today, see linux-poll-fd-leak-futex-requeue for what was scoped OUT of that row for this reason). This is squarely 'Larger architectural work, out of scope for a single pass' per this project's own established framing for Seatbelt/Landlock/vsock/WASI-capability-redesign -- deserves a dedicated design-first session (host process lifecycle across 3 platforms, security boundary implications of a new process-creation primitive, memory-model implications for the existing single-shared-address-space assumptions baked into mm.rs/proc.rs/darwin.rs) rather than a single batch-agent implementation attempt. Flagging clearly rather than either silently skipping or rushing a partial, likely-unsafe implementation of new process-isolation machinery.
prd_items.subject: fork() does not exist ANYWHERE in litebox today (not Linux, not macOS, not Windows) -- 'fix' requires designing and building true multi-process support from scratch, a large architectural project

prd_items.description: Found live on real M3 Pro hardware while demoing the mac port (packaged a real public.ecr.aws/docker/library/alpine:latest image, ran it via litebox_runner_linux_on_macos_userland). Root cause chain, fully verified: litebox_shim_linux::default_fs nests two layered::FileSystem instances -- outer (upper=in_mem_fs writable scratch, lower=inner, semantics=LowerLayerWritableFiles) wrapping inner (upper=dev_stdio '/dev'+'/proc' virtual resolver, lower=tar_ro the OCI image, semantics=LowerLayerReadOnly). Any chmod/chown/utimensat/write-a-new-file targeting a base-image file needs layered::FileSystem::migrate_file_up to copy it into the writable upper layer first. THIS PASS fixed three real, live-reproduced hard panics in that path (commit pending): (1) migrate_file_up's deliberate unreachable!() guard for LowerLayerWritableFiles semantics, (2) an unimplemented!() when mkdir_migrating_ancestor_dirs cleanly reported it couldn't create a directory, (3) an equivalent .unwrap() in open()'s O_CREAT-with-missing-ancestor path. All three now propagate a clean ChmodError::ReadOnlyFileSystem / ChownError::ReadOnlyFileSystem / UtimeError::ReadOnlyFileSystem / OpenError::NoWritePerms instead of crashing the guest process outright -- verified via a new regression test (litebox/src/fs/tests.rs::layered_chmod_chown_utimensat_on_lower_only_file_does_not_panic) and live re-execution of the exact original crash repro. REMAINING, NOT fixed this pass: the operations still functionally FAIL (clean error, not success) for any top-level directory other than /tmp. Root cause: in_mem::FileSystem's permission model is a single fixed current_user (uid 1000) for the guest's entire lifetime (litebox/src/fs/in_mem.rs:61-64), checked on every mkdir/open against the target's real Unix parent-directory permissions -- and root '/' defaults to mode 0755 owned by uid 0 (litebox/src/fs/in_mem.rs 'RootDir::new'), so uid 1000 cannot create a new top-level entry there. litebox_runner_linux_on_macos_userland/src/lib.rs:98-107 works around this ONLY for /tmp, via in_mem::FileSystem::with_root_privileges (a &mut self, setup-time-only escape hatch -- confirmed via grep to have zero other production call sites) explicitly pre-creating /tmp as world-writable before the guest ever runs. Every OTHER base-image top-level directory (/etc, /usr, /var, /bin, /lib, /root, /home, ...) has no such carve-out, so a guest's first chmod/chown/utimensat/new-file-write under any of them cleanly fails instead of succeeding. This is architecturally identical to how a real Linux kernel's overlayfs performs copy-up with kernel privilege regardless of the calling process's own permissions on the upper filesystem -- litebox's migrate_file_up (and open()'s equivalent ancestor-creation path) needs the same kind of internal/elevated-privilege execution, which does not currently exist as a runtime (non-&mut-self) capability anywhere in the FileSystem trait or in_mem backend. Needs careful security-model design (a guest must not be able to reach or trigger this privilege bypass for anything other than the exact copy-up bookkeeping it is meant for), a new FileSystem-trait-level or layered.rs-local mechanism, and live verification across at least litebox_shim_linux (this repro) plus litebox_shim_windows and litebox_runner_snp, which share the exact same nested-layering topology (grep-confirmed) and are presumed to have the identical gap, unverified on this pass (no Windows/SNP host available). Recommend a dedicated implementer + adversarial-security-verifier pass given the privilege-boundary stakes.
prd_items.subject: layered::FileSystem's copy-up migration is subject to the guest's own uid permission check, so chmod/chown/utimensat/new-file-writes fail (cleanly, not crash) on any base-image directory except the specially pre-seeded /tmp

CORRECTED AND RE-WITNESSED SCOPE. The original stale/cache/file-wide `layered.rs` premise is false, while two narrower diagnostics defects remain in loaded gm 0.1.1281 (source cab7985b1af9101ceefe3aab6c04b8d2c47fab7d).

CURRENT DIFF / LIVE GATE: The loaded predicate runs `git diff --unified=0 HEAD` and inspects only added tuples. `unreachable!()` is not a needle; Rust needles are only `.unwrap()`, `.expect(`, and `panic!(`. A bounded reconstruction of HEAD via GM `git_show -L` slices plus `/usr/bin/git diff --no-index --unified=0` against the current file found four real added matches in litebox/src/fs/layered.rs: line 1623 `.expect("every upper open completion holds the namespace");`, line 1681 `.expect("O_CREAT holds the namespace through publication"),`, line 2482 `let (parent, leaf) = new.rsplit_once('/').unwrap();`, and line 3146 `.expect("directory generation space exhausted");`. An isolated direct transition using the installed gm.wasm, body `{"to":"DECIDE","session_id":"990416-gm-gate-layered-live"}`, freshly denied with exactly those four watcher findings: dispatch 1788294229560-0-9146790446293299, fingerprint c37c1b9ca02de3ee. Thus the present denial is legitimate and current-diff-driven, not stale, cached, whole-file, or session-local.

REAL DEFECT 1 -- RUST TEST SCOPE: Historical aaa-final watcher events 1786398106635 and 1786398195030 named only newly added litebox/src/fs/tests.rs unwrap/expect lines, not layered.rs. They were fresh findings, but transitions.rs::is_test_scoped_path recognizes `.test.`/`.spec.` and `/test[s]/` directory segments, not conventional basename `tests.rs`, and it never honors `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. This contradicts the predicate description's test-only-configured Rust module exemption.

REAL DEFECT 2 -- REPEAT IDENTITY: gates.rs stores repeat state under only `<target>::gate-deny` and emits prose claiming `this exact gate denial`. A bounded isolated witness kept phase/target/body constant but changed the exact finding set: dispatch 1788294505387-2-54929c96c966b2bc reported only `layered.rs:123: let alpha = synthetic_value.unwrap();`; dispatch 1788294520068-3-cd155df8b118638b reported only `layered.rs:987: let beta = synthetic_other.expect("distinct finding set");`. Both had fingerprint 4b019bc768bf291c, yet `.gate-deviation-repeats.json` became `{"decide::gate-deny":2}`. The counter therefore conflates different line sets/diffs (and source confirms it also omits predicate, fingerprint, and session identity); this is repeat-classification state, not verdict caching.

UPSTREAM CONTRACT: (1) recognize conventional Rust test module files, at minimum basename test.rs/tests.rs and *_test.rs, preferably with cfg(test)-aware module classification; (2) key escalation by target plus stable canonical residual/predicate-and-finding identity within a bounded session/stop window, resetting only that identity on success, or change the prose/behavior to state honestly that it is aggregate target-gate friction. Implement and live-witness upstream; do not add LiteBox tests or mutate LiteBox source/config/shared-daemon/external state for this row. prd_items.description:
From the 2026-08-10 adversarial workflow. The assigned bug (allocate_jit_pages FixedAddressBehavior::Replace silently returning a kernel-chosen address instead of the caller's exact requested address, regression from commit 1e9b4c2fd5) was correctly diagnosed and a fix written, and BOTH adversarial verifiers independently reproduced the bug and confirmed the dispatch fix is discriminating (reverting only the must_be_exact change makes the new test fail with a wrong address; restoring it passes). BUT the work is NOT merged, for two reasons, both of which need resolving first.

FINDING 1, arguably more important than the assigned bug and independently confirmed by both verifiers with their own from-scratch C probes: mach_vm_remap(copy=FALSE) returns KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE (kr=2) for EVERY MAP_JIT source -- live destination, free destination, and mach_vm_allocate(VM_FLAGS_FIXED) reservation alike -- while a non-JIT source control returns kr=0. remap_to_fixed is the single mechanism behind every exact-placement path on this platform, so it was dead for JIT mappings. copy=TRUE fixes it and yields a genuine JIT mapping: a verifier wrote real aarch64 code (movz w0,#4242; ret) into a MAP_JIT source, remapped with copy=TRUE, munmap'd the source, and EXECUTED the destination getting 4242, then confirmed a write faults under pthread_jit_write_protect_np(true) and succeeds under (false).

FINDING 2, a NEW defect the candidate fix introduces, found by a verifier and absent from the implementer's own residual-risk list: allocate_jit_pages(Replace) over a FREE destination returns Ok(suggested_range.start) with NOTHING MAPPED THERE. Because Replace now skips reserve_fixed, the internal mmap(NULL, ..., MAP_JIT) deterministically reuses the just-freed hole and returns exactly suggested_range.start; remap_to_fixed then trivially 'succeeds' with src == dest, and the unconditional munmap(kernel_chosen, len) afterwards unmaps the very range being returned. This directly contradicts the doc comment the same diff adds ('Replace and NoReplace always return exactly suggested_range.start or an error'). It is currently latent ONLY because of a cross-crate invariant in a DIFFERENT crate -- litebox/src/mm/linux.rs:501-504 downgrades Replace to NoReplace when the range does not overlap an existing VMA -- which is neither documented at nor enforced by allocate_jit_pages.

ALSO NOTED: production reachability of the Replace path is unproven. A verifier instrumented a release runner and recorded ZERO allocate_jit_pages calls for busybox uname/ls/free and for node; reachability rests on reading Vmem::reset_pages (litebox/src/mm/linux.rs:440), which neither agent executed from a guest. And a pre-existing adjacent hazard: allocate_jit_pages(NoReplace) on a free destination can fail spuriously with AddressInUse because reserve_fixed collides with the temporary MAP_JIT mapping allocate_jit_pages itself just created.

NEXT STEP: take the copy=TRUE fix and the dispatch fix, but first make Replace-over-a-free-destination either reserve properly or return an honest error, and either enforce or document the mm/linux.rs invariant at the allocate_jit_pages boundary. Worktree with the candidate diff: .claude/worktrees/wf_52206494-718-2.
prd_items.subject: mach_vm_remap(copy=FALSE) fails for every MAP_JIT source, so remap_to_fixed -- the single mechanism behind every exact-placement path on macOS -- was entirely dead; the candidate fix also introduces a dangling-address path

prd_items.description:
From the 2026-08-10 adversarial workflow. An implementer produced a copy-up privilege fix for layered-fs-copy-up-needs-elevated-privilege that genuinely closes the functional gap AND holds the privilege boundary -- all three verifiers independently confirmed both of those, including with their own hand-built adversarial ustar fixtures (root-owned 0644/0600/04755, guest-owned 0644/0444) rather than the implementer's. Errno fidelity even improves (chmod of another user's file EROFS->EPERM, write to root-owned file EIO->EACCES) and no ownership laundering occurs (copy-up preserves both mode AND owner). NOT MERGED because the correctness verifier REFUTED it on new crashes, each reproduced against clean HEAD as a control:

1. unreachable!() at litebox/src/fs/layered.rs:424 (the 0..=2 arm of match Arc::strong_count(&entry) in migrate_file_up's descriptor-migration loop). Trigger: sh -c 'exec 9>>/etc/hosts; echo NEW >&9', also plain 'busybox echo hi >> /etc/hosts 2>&1', also two sequential appends to the same base-image file. 10/10 runner aborts (exit 101) with the diff, 0/10 on clean HEAD (clean EIO, exit 0).
2. assertion failed: Arc::ptr_eq(&old_entry, &entry) at layered.rs:437, same defect family. Trigger: sh -c 'exec 9>>/etc/hosts; exec 8>&9; echo NEW >&9'.
3. open() with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC on ANY existing base-image directory (sh -c '> /etc', also /usr, /dev, /proc) aborts at litebox_common_linux/src/errno/mod.rs:135 (exit 101) where clean HEAD returned a harmless EACCES. Cause: the new 'Ok(_) => return Err(e)' arm in layered::open propagates OpenError::TruncateError(IsDirectory), which From<OpenError> for Errno cannot map ('_ => unimplemented!()').

PLAUSIBLE, not fully pinned: after the guest's PT_INTERP is copied up, every subsequent execve SIGSEGVs (sh -c 'echo >> /lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1; exec /bin/busybox uname -a' -> exit 11, 8/8; clean HEAD refuses the write with EIO then execs fine). Suspected: in_mem::get_static_backing_data returns None for a copied-up (Cow::Owned) file, bypassing the mmap path.

RESOURCE REGRESSION the implementer's residual-risk list got factually wrong: it claims the copy-up memory cost 'was already true for permitted operations'. Measured on clean HEAD, NO base-image operation copied anything up (peak RSS 421,265,408 vs 421,216,256 baseline for a DENIED append to a 60 MB root-owned file). On the patched build the same DENIED operation costs +65 MB (486,506,496). Denied operations now allocate host heap proportional to target file size -- a guest-reachable memory-amplification vector.

EVIDENCE-SCOPE CAVEAT worth remembering: the implementer's live 'append works' evidence only ever used the plain 'echo X >> file' form, which is the single case where the migration list has length 1 and the buggy loop happens to be safe. Every multi-reference form of the same operation crashes.

ADJACENT PRE-EXISTING (verified present on clean HEAD, so not caused by this attempt, but they gate the headline claim): chmod 0777 /etc, chmod 0700 on a base-image dir, touch /etc, and chmod/touch on a file the guest cannot read all hit unimplemented!() in layered.rs (MigrationError::NotAFile / NoReadPerms) and kill the sandbox with exit 101, at layered.rs:999/998/1110/1109.

NEXT STEP: the design is sound and the privilege boundary is verified -- redo it with the descriptor-migration loop and the O_CREAT|O_TRUNC-on-directory errno mapping handled, add the multi-reference-descriptor cases to the tests, and bound or avoid copy-up on operations that will be denied anyway. Candidate diff: .claude/worktrees/wf_52206494-718-1.
prd_items.subject: First copy-up privilege attempt was REFUTED in review: it fixes the functional gap but introduces at least three new guest-triggerable runner aborts

prd_items.description: Profiled via sample(1)+lldb on a CPU-bound, zero-syscall busybox-awk loop (BEGIN{...for(i=0;i<N;i++){c=(a+b)%1000000007;...}}): 46%% of leaf CPU samples land in a private rwx VM_ALLOCATE region (848KB, right after the host binary's own segments, not recognized by atos/sample as any loaded image) rather than the guest's own faithful-address-range code (0x3ffffff...). Live disassembly at a hot guest PC found a classic AArch64 PLT stub (adrp/ldr/br through a GOT-style table) whose resolved target sometimes lands in that JIT region; one such target disassembled to malloc-shaped bit-twiddling (alignment-class computation), consistent with busybox awk's double-precision arithmetic (its `%` on doubles/fmod, and/or per-value heap allocation) going through this path on every loop iteration. Controlled A/B (identical computation, identical system load, matching output) showed litebox's raw `user` CPU time is ~8x native macOS awk's for the same iteration count -- a real, litebox-attributable CPU cost, not a scheduling/accounting artifact (native showed almost no real-vs-CPU-time inflation under the same load; litebox did). Hypothesis for next investigation: litebox's AOT rewriter may be leaving PLT calls to musl libc functions (fmod, malloc, etc.) as lazily-bound indirect trampolines instead of eagerly resolving/patching call sites at rewrite time (the rewriter already walks the whole binary to replace SVC instructions, so eager PLT binding -- akin to LD_BIND_NOW/-znow static linking -- may be a tractable, general, guest-transparent win). NOT attempted this pass: deep changes to litebox_syscall_rewriter's AOT rewriting are high-risk to guest compatibility and needed more time to verify safely across the guest matrix than this pass had. See docs/benchmarks/ for the reproduction harness, profiler evidence, and measurement methodology this row should build on.
prd_items.subject: AOT-rewritten guest code spends ~46%% of CPU in a private JIT-mapped region doing PLT-indirected calls, ~8x native user-CPU for identical computation

prd_items.description: Surveyed and drafted an implementation of AnEntrypoint/litebox commit 46349353 (follow intermediate-position symlinks during read-only tar-backed filesystem walks, e.g. Alpine's usrmerge /lib -> usr/lib) -- a real gap: this shim's path resolver doesn't currently follow a symlink that appears as a non-final path component. Draft touches 8 files (litebox/src/fs/{backend,composer,layered,mod,resolver,tar_ro}.rs, litebox_common_linux/src/lib.rs) with a shared walk_path_following_symlinks helper, hop-restart-from-root design, and 5 new tests -- all passing, clippy/fmt clean, cross-compile clean. NOT landed: independent adversarial verification found a confirmed, reproduced bug -- in resolver.rs's walk_path_following_symlinks, the absolute-target branch (target.strip_prefix('/')) filters out '.' but not '..', unlike the relative-target branch which correctly pops on '..'. An absolute symlink target containing '..' (e.g. a -> /b/../c) fails to resolve with NoSuchFileOrDirectory instead of resolving correctly. Doesn't affect the stated Alpine usrmerge use case (relative targets only, verified working), but is a real, easily-triggered gap in general absolute-symlink-target handling. This touches core filesystem code used everywhere (backend/composer/layered/resolver/tar_ro), so deferred rather than landed with a known, unaddressed edge-case bug. Fix: mirror the '..'/'.'-popping handling the relative branch already does correctly, in the absolute-target branch too, then re-verify with the reproducing case (a -> /b/../c) added as a regression test. The draft diff is not preserved anywhere durable (was only in an ephemeral workflow worktree) -- would need to be redone from scratch, referencing AnEntrypoint/litebox commit 46349353ed63ac3c8d376b5ecd9318c779fed2b1 for the original design.

prd_items.description: Found during the ba60bb4792 pass: every ELF in the packaged node:alpine tar carries the LITEBOX0 AOT trailer except usr/lib/libgcc_s.so.1 (tail-byte verified independently by both verifiers). Before the new e_machine gate, this caused the x86-only runtime patcher to decode libgcc's AArch64 bytes as x86 on every launch (latent corruption, now refused with a single warning: machine=183 len=212992). libgcc currently runs with raw un-caught SVCs -- benign only as long as no libgcc code path issues a syscall. Investigate why the packager's rewriter fails/skips this file (its stderr should say 'failed to rewrite ... including as-is') and fix the underlying rewrite failure so the whole image is covered.

Structural fix: reserve [GUEST_ADDR_MIN, GUEST_ADDR_MAX) at startup with a single VM_FLAGS_FIXED PROT_NONE mapping and carve all guest mappings from it, making late host allocations structurally unable to intrude; retire reserved_pages. Four independent reference implementations -- gVisor systrap, qemu linux-user, box64, Darling sigexc -- all resume by mutating the host ucontext in-handler and letting the kernel's sigreturn commit all 31 GPRs, sp, pc, pstate, TLS, and FPSIMD atomically. prd_items.description: From the ba60bb4792 root cause: litebox has three code-mutation stages (packager AOT rewrite, loader trampoline publication, runtime maybe_patch_exec_segment) whose contracts were undocumented, and the Node PC=0 crash came from exactly one stage silently skipping a header field the others fill. Write the invariant down in docs/ (every path that materializes a pre-patched trampoline must publish every runtime-variable header word; the runtime patcher may never write file-derived bytes over relocated memory), enumerate the header layout in one place, and add a shared helper both loader.rs and mm.rs call so a new header field cannot be added to one path only. Consider a debug assertion at gate-execution time that the offset word is non-default when the process key differs.
prd_items.subject: Document and enforce the AOT/load-time/runtime patch invariant for trampoline headers

prd_items.description: litebox uniquely runs one shim over Linux-userland and macOS backends, so a record/replay harness logging (nr, args-hash, retval, guest pc) per syscall and reporting the first divergence is cheap and mechanical -- gVisor closed its compatibility gap with tens of thousands of such runs. Build as a dev_tools crate replaying an strace corpus from node:alpine on real Linux, plus a ring buffer of the last N syscalls dumped on fault (would have identified the uv_loop_init failing call instantly). Optionally a hermit-style --verify double-run mode to separate host nondeterminism from guest logic. Immediate cheap slice: add return-value logging to the existing LITEBOX_LOG syscall trace.
prd_items.subject: Differential syscall harness: diff litebox's syscall stream against a real Linux run of the same guest

prd_items.description: With JS executing (3c727e583e), child_process.execSync('/bin/sh -c ...') fails with spawnSync ENOSYS (errno -38) from libuv's uv_spawn. libuv spawns via posix_spawn or fork+execvp depending on platformo; under musl this reaches clone/fork + execve. The macOS platform has the delayed-address-space-handoff fork model working for busybox sh (real pipelines fork fine), so the gap is likely a specific clone flag combination or posix_spawn-related syscall libuv uses that the shim rejects with ENOSYS rather than fork itself. Diagnose with the new sysret trace (grep for ENOSYS), implement the missing surface, verify with child_process.execSync + spawn round trips.
prd_items.subject: child_process spawn returns ENOSYS under Node on macOS -- next Node functional gap

prd_items.description: After full V8 JIT landed (661ecea): three deferred hardening items. (1) DCZID_EL0: only CTR_EL0 is emulated in fault_handler; DCZID_EL0 (mrs Xt, S3_3_C0_C0_7 = 0xd53b00e0) also traps on Darwin EL0 and musl/some code reads it for DC ZVA block size -- not yet observed crashing node, but add symmetric emulation (return a safe block-size value) if any guest hits it. (2) JIT_REGIONS is a fixed 64-slot atomic array; V8 uses one big code range + a few, so ample, but a guest that creates >64 distinct JIT regions logs a one-time warn and those overflow regions get no fault-toggling (faults delivered to guest). If a real workload approaches the cap, grow to a dynamic structure or coalesce. (3) Stress: run JIT-heavy Node under concurrent child_process spawns and parallel worker_threads to exercise fault-toggling + fork-gate + per-thread JIT mode together under load; current verification covered them separately. Also worth: node running a real npm/script workload end to end (require of a real module, http server) as a broader JIT+syscall soak.
prd_items.subject: JIT W^X follow-ups: DCZID_EL0 emulation if needed, JIT-registry 64-slot cap, combined JIT+child_process/parallel stress

Postcondition: one release exists, latest is correct, and a repeated verification cannot create or overwrite a divergent artifact.

prd_items.description: Precondition: local npm configuration may contain an authenticated account. Invariant: credentials are never printed, copied, committed, or sent anywhere except registry.npmjs.org through npm. Postcondition: npm whoami succeeds for an account authorized to publish @openclew/litebox, or the credential acquisition path is concretely executed before publication.
prd_items.subject: Verify npm registry identity and publish authority

prd_items.description: Precondition: publication has returned success. Invariant: verification reads the public registry rather than the working tree or a local npm cache. Postcondition: name, version, latest dist-tag, full eight-file payload, bin mapping, source pin, shasum, and integrity all match the pre-publication package.
prd_items.subject: Verify published registry metadata and tarball content

prd_items.description: Precondition: npm registry shows @openclew/litebox latest 0.1.0 and the intended package API remains backward-compatible. Invariant: published npm versions are immutable and no existing version is overwritten. Postcondition: package.json carries the next unused patch version and CLI --version reports it.
prd_items.subject: Assign an unused semver patch version

prd_items.description: Precondition: release metadata is updated and npm tooling is available without dependency installation. Invariant: package files remain limited to bin, lib, and README.md with no repository secrets, caches, binaries, user changes, or unrelated dashboard content. Postcondition: a real npm pack dry run identifies the expected eight files, executable bin mapping, integrity, size, and version.
prd_items.subject: Audit the exact npm tarball before publication

prd_items.description: Precondition: only npm/package.json and npm/lib/platform.js are intended release modifications in addition to the preserved user-owned files. Invariant: litebox/src/net/mod.rs and litebox_runner_linux_on_macos_userland/src/lib.rs remain byte-identical, unstaged, and uncommitted. Postcondition: release metadata is committed and pushed to origin/main while those two local modifications remain present.
prd_items.subject: Commit and push npm release metadata without user edits

prd_items.description: Precondition: commit 876e41c093728c831e524c56c2decb4a784dbade is pushed and downloadable from GitHub. Invariant: one npm version deterministically selects one immutable full commit SHA and cache paths remain revision-scoped. Postcondition: PINNED_REV names that full commit, so a default npx run cannot fetch the stale 497433858b0f8c52ea335df3576afb3e23e3a2e3 tree.
prd_items.subject: Pin the npm package to the Node-enabled source revision

prd_items.description: Precondition: the newly published CLI can package the real node:alpine image from its pinned source revision. Invariant: output is written synchronously to survive the known unrelated Node teardown failure, and no local checkout or prebuilt runner supplies the result. Postcondition: a published-package npx invocation reports lo and eth0 with 127.0.0.1/8 and 10.0.0.2/24, proving AF_NETLINK shipped.
prd_items.subject: Run Node os.networkInterfaces through the published npx path

prd_items.description: Precondition: existing litebox and npm caches may contain revision 497433858b0f8c52ea335df3576afb3e23e3a2e3 artifacts. Invariant: source, target, binaries, and images are selected under the full new revision and clean verification uses isolated cache roots. Postcondition: observed paths and output prove no stale source, runner, packager, image, or npm package masked the release.
prd_items.subject: Exclude stale local caches from release acceptance

prd_items.description: Precondition: the pinned revision includes the landed macOS fork/child_process and x18/Node fixes and their real behavior is re-witnessed. Invariant: documentation states only capabilities observed through the new published npx artifact, does not promote unverified host rows, and preserves all existing command syntax. Postcondition: npm/README.md and CLI help no longer tell users fork is absent or Node cannot run; they describe the now-working interactive/direct Node paths and any still-observed teardown limitation accurately.
prd_items.subject: Remove stale fork and Node crash warnings from the npm CLI and README

prd_items.description: Precondition: the new version is public and a fresh temporary npm cache/directory is available. Invariant: no LITEBOX_SRC, prior litebox cache, local package path, or old npm tarball may satisfy the invocation. Postcondition: the same npx @openclew/litebox commands resolve the published version and --version, --help, --where, and unknown-option behavior are observed directly.
prd_items.subject: Prove clean npx resolution preserves the existing CLI

prd_items.description: Precondition: --rev is untrusted CLI input used in both the GitHub source URL and revision-scoped cache path. Invariant: only a 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA can become a source/cache revision, so separators, traversal, refs, encodings, and empty values cannot escape or alias cache state. Postcondition: invalid revisions fail before any filesystem or network effect, while the pinned and explicit full-SHA paths retain the established npx behavior.
prd_items.subject: Contain custom revision selection to immutable commit SHAs

prd_items.description: Precondition: the npx CLI inherits a real host terminal and the pinned macOS runner can receive guest terminal syscalls and keyboard bytes. Invariant: stdin/stdout/stderr remain attached bidirectionally with terminal mode, window size, signals, EOF, and exit status preserved across interactive shells and REPLs. Postcondition: the published npx package live-runs keyboard-driven Node REPL and shell sessions plus representative pwd, ssh, rsync, gzip, and neofetch commands, fixing every reachable syscall or packaging gap rather than documenting failures.
prd_items.subject: Support real interactive and REPL programs through npx LiteBox

prd_items.description: Precondition: the deterministic image contains rsync and the filesystem supports its metadata operations. Invariant: source bytes, destination bytes, modes/times, partial-transfer cleanup, child/pipe behavior, and SSH authority remain correct across retries. Postcondition: local rsync copies a tree byte-for-byte and rsync over the controlled SSH endpoint transfers a file, while an interrupted/corrupt transfer produces a named failure without a false success.
prd_items.subject: Prove rsync local and SSH-backed transfer

prd_items.description: Precondition: the guest image contains BusyBox or another shell and the pinned runner includes fork/exec/wait. Invariant: shell and child share the controlling terminal without losing keyboard bytes, process lifecycle, current directory, or exit status. Postcondition: an npx shell accepts typed `pwd`, `echo`, external commands, a pipe, and exit, rendering each result interactively.
prd_items.subject: Run an interactive shell with external commands

prd_items.description: Precondition: the digest-pinned tools image contains Bash and stock Neofetch 7.1.0 at /usr/bin/neofetch with SHA-256 3dc33493e54029fb1528251552093a9f9a2894fcf94f9c3a6f809136a42348c7. Invariant: uname reports Linux-compatible identity; /proc-derived values are coherent and privacy-safe; stdout mode emits no ANSI; fields not in the minimal contract are explicitly disabled rather than fabricated. Postcondition: live `neofetch --stdout` exits zero and emits exactly nonempty OS, Kernel, and Memory fields with no escape bytes, missing-command diagnostics, hangs, or host-secret leakage.
prd_items.subject: Run stock Neofetch with a precise minimal compatibility contract

prd_items.description: Precondition: every example has been live-run through the published artifact. Invariant: README and CLI help use the same package name/options, distinguish `node` from `node -i`, name required images, and expose no stale unsupported claim. Postcondition: copy-paste commands cover Node REPL, shell/pwd, ssh, rsync, gzip, and neofetch plus noninteractive alternatives and known observed limitations.
prd_items.subject: Document executable interactive examples

prd_items.description: Precondition: the selected guest image contains Node and npx has a real terminal. Invariant: guest fd 0 remains readable and tty-aware while stdout/stderr stay attached; typed input is neither buffered away nor interpreted by the host. Postcondition: `node -i` displays a prompt, evaluates typed arithmetic and multi-line JavaScript, handles backspace/history, and exits through Ctrl-D with the correct status under the published npx command.
prd_items.subject: Run a real Node.js REPL with keyboard input

prd_items.description: Precondition: default Alpine and Node Alpine do not necessarily include ssh, rsync, and neofetch. Invariant: every documented acceptance command names an immutable or digest-pinned OCI image whose architecture matches the host; npx does not silently install mutable packages at runtime. Postcondition: Node, shell/pwd/gzip, ssh/rsync, and neofetch each have a reproducible image command, with a single purpose-built image preferred if it avoids fragmented UX.
prd_items.subject: Provide deterministic images containing requested programs

prd_items.description: Precondition: REPLs and network clients may emit output while waiting for input. Invariant: no unbounded queue, busy loop, lost wakeup, starvation, or lock held across a blocking terminal read; one reader owns stdin. Postcondition: sustained mixed keyboard/output activity remains responsive and bounded, including cancellation during a blocked read.
prd_items.subject: Bound simultaneous terminal input and output

prd_items.description: Precondition: a foreground guest process owns the terminal. Invariant: Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D, Ctrl-Z policy, SIGWINCH, process groups, and foreground ownership cannot target the runner incorrectly or leave terminal state corrupted. Postcondition: interrupt, EOF, suspend policy, resize, and clean exit are live-observed for shell and Node REPL, with the host terminal restored after normal exit and guest crash.
prd_items.subject: Preserve interactive control keys and resize signals

prd_items.description: Precondition: the shell has a valid root and current working directory. Invariant: chdir/getcwd state remains per guest process and survives child execution without host path leakage. Postcondition: typed `pwd`, `cd /tmp`, and `pwd` produce `/` then `/tmp` in an interactive npx shell.
prd_items.subject: Prove pwd and directory state interactively

prd_items.description: Precondition: host stdin/stdout may be a TTY or a pipe. Invariant: guest isatty, termios reads/writes, canonical/raw/echo flags, and window dimensions reflect the host terminal without exposing host-only memory layouts. Postcondition: terminal-aware REPLs and utilities can query/change/restore modes and dimensions through real ioctls with Linux-compatible results.
prd_items.subject: Complete terminal mode and identity semantics

prd_items.description: Precondition: a deterministic guest image contains a real OpenSSH client and a controlled reachable SSH endpoint is available without public credential exposure. Invariant: DNS/address resolution, outbound TCP, entropy, host-key checking, terminal prompts, key permissions, and Ctrl-C fail closed; secrets never enter package files or logs. Postcondition: npx runs `ssh -V`, handles a real host-key/auth interaction through keyboard input, executes a remote `pwd`, and exits cleanly against the controlled endpoint.
prd_items.subject: Prove interactive OpenSSH client behavior

prd_items.description: Precondition: a guest may enable raw/no-echo mode then exit, signal, abort, or lose its network peer. Invariant: terminal restoration runs exactly once and cannot be skipped by guest status translation. Postcondition: host echo/canonical mode and cursor usability match the pre-run state after normal exit, Ctrl-C, Node teardown failure, SSH failure, and forced guest termination.
prd_items.subject: Restore host terminal state after every exit path

prd_items.description: Precondition: a caller that is not already a process-group leader invokes setsid. Invariant: PID/session/PGID relationships remain globally unique and controlling-terminal eligibility follows Linux rules across fork/exec/wait. Postcondition: setsid returns the new session id, leader/error boundaries match Linux, and terminal/job-control programs no longer hit ENOSYS.
prd_items.subject: Implement setsid session and process-group creation

prd_items.description: Precondition: an inherited, duplicated, reopened /dev/std*, or /dev/tty descriptor addresses a terminal and receives TCGETS, TCSETS, TCSETSW, or TCSETSF with Linux termios data. Invariant: one shared terminal object losslessly translates relevant input, output, local, control flags and control bytes (including ISIG, ICANON, ECHO, IEXTEN, ICRNL, IXON/IXOFF, OPOST, VMIN, VTIME, VINTR, VQUIT, VEOF, VSUSP); unsupported combinations and host tcgetattr/tcsetattr failures return named Linux errno; NOW, DRAIN, and FLUSH timing semantics remain distinct; original host state is restored exactly once. Postcondition: a deliberately non-default host-termios sentinel round-trips byte-for-byte and live stty, Node raw mode/editing, shell control keys, and SSH no-echo prompts work through every terminal alias without EINVAL, ENOTTY, or leaked host mode.
prd_items.subject: Apply complete Linux termios state through every terminal descriptor

prd_items.description: Precondition: an interactive shell launches a foreground child and the host terminal generates Ctrl-C/Ctrl-Z. Invariant: foreground process-group identity is guest-global and signal routing targets the foreground group exactly once, not merely the runner thread or parent shell. Postcondition: Ctrl-C interrupts `sleep`, its exit reflects SIGINT, the shell trap/status are Linux-compatible, and the terminal remains usable.
prd_items.subject: Deliver terminal control signals to the foreground guest job

prd_items.description: Precondition: a process calls kill/tgkill against an existing child or process-group member. Invariant: PID lookup spans the guest task registry with lifecycle-safe ownership, cannot target a recycled/dead task, and applies permission/signal-zero semantics before delivery. Postcondition: `kill -TERM $child` reaches the sleeping child, wait reports signal termination, and nonexistent targets alone return ESRCH.
prd_items.subject: Route kill signals to live child tasks by guest PID

prd_items.description: Precondition: stdin or stdout may not be a TTY. Invariant: the CLI does not force a PTY or raw mode when streams are pipes/files and preserves exit codes and signal mapping. Postcondition: direct commands, piped gzip, redirected Node output, closed stdin, and CI-style npx invocation remain deterministic alongside new interactive support.
prd_items.subject: Keep noninteractive pipelines compatible

prd_items.description: Precondition: the guest image exposes gzip and writable /tmp. Invariant: pipes, file descriptors, metadata, binary bytes, and compression failures remain Linux-compatible and bounded. Postcondition: typed or direct npx commands compress and decompress empty, text, and binary payloads byte-for-byte, and corrupt input returns a named nonzero failure.
prd_items.subject: Prove gzip streaming and file round-trip

prd_items.description: Precondition: a session has a controlling terminal, one foreground process group, and a background job attempts read(2) from that terminal. Invariant: only the foreground process group may consume terminal input; background reads receive SIGTTIN according to Linux job-control rules, with orphaned-group exceptions handled explicitly. Postcondition: typed foreground input cannot be consumed by `(read x; ...) &`, the background job stops instead of printing the secret, and `fg` resumes it to consume input only after foreground ownership transfers.
prd_items.subject: Stop background process groups from stealing terminal input

prd_items.description: Precondition: returning ownership to a parent requires restoring every saved mapping and protection. Invariant: partial restoration can never resume guest code against a mismatched address space; all mapping failures retain the original cause and trigger complete rollback or process failure. Postcondition: the observed 268435456-byte RWX restoration failure is eliminated or terminates the affected process before memory access, and repeated Node spawns preserve mapped sentinels with no warning.
prd_items.subject: Make fork address-space restoration fail closed

prd_items.description: Precondition: kill/tgkill receives signal 0 for self, live child/group, dead, or unauthorized target. Invariant: signal 0 performs lookup and authority checks without enqueuing a signal or changing lifecycle state. Postcondition: live permitted targets return 0, dead targets return ESRCH, unauthorized targets return EPERM, and self no longer returns EINVAL.
prd_items.subject: Implement kill signal-zero existence and permission checks

prd_items.description: Precondition: multiple fork-family processes share the macOS-hosted guest address space and at least two are runnable. Invariant: exclusive address-space ownership is time-bounded or cooperatively preemptible at deterministic safe points, so a nonblocking child cannot starve its parent or siblings. Postcondition: a CPU-bound background child and interactive foreground shell both make bounded progress, keyboard latency remains bounded, and pipelines retain correctness.
prd_items.subject: Prevent CPU-only fork children from monopolizing guest execution

prd_items.description: Precondition: npx spawns the runner with inherited stdio and the host delivers SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGWINCH to Node or its process group. Invariant: the wrapper neither dies before the guest handles a control signal nor double-delivers it; resize and termination signals reach the runner, and exit mapping remains shell-compatible. Postcondition: Ctrl-C interrupts a foreground guest promptly through npx instead of killing the wrapper after delay, SIGWINCH updates dimensions, and wrapper cleanup runs once.
prd_items.subject: Forward host terminal signals from the npm wrapper to the guest runner

prd_items.description: Precondition: a parent exits while descendants remain live. Invariant: child ownership and zombie reaping transfer atomically to a designated guest reaper; the host runner lifetime covers all non-daemon guest processes and no child record is discarded. Postcondition: a delayed orphan prints and exits after its parent, is reaped without a zombie leak, and runner exit waits according to the documented process-lifetime policy.
prd_items.subject: Keep orphaned children alive under an init-style reaper

prd_items.description: Precondition: setsid/session leaders and terminal-opening processes follow Linux eligibility rules. Invariant: SID and controlling-terminal ownership are per session, TIOCSCTTY/TIOCNOTTY enforce authority, and inherited terminal state does not masquerade as a newly acquired controlling tty. Postcondition: setsid boundaries are real, `setsid -c` acquires the intended terminal, detached processes lose it, and SSH/job-control behavior matches Linux.
prd_items.subject: Implement sessions and controlling-terminal ownership

prd_items.description: Precondition: a live process receives SIGSTOP/SIGTSTP/SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU or SIGCONT. Invariant: STOP-class signals suspend without destroying task/address-space state; SIGCONT resumes once; WUNTRACED/WCONTINUED report transitions without consuming exit status. Postcondition: Ctrl-Z, background-terminal enforcement, bg/fg, wait, and jobs distinguish running/stopped/continued/exited rather than treating SIGSTOP as status 147 termination.
prd_items.subject: Implement stopped and continued child lifecycle

prd_items.description: Precondition: a program opens /dev/ptmx and performs TIOCGPTN/unlock/grant then opens the slave. Invariant: master/slave byte flow, termios, window size, session/foreground group, hangup, permissions, and close semantics are isolated per PTY. Postcondition: a real PTY allocation succeeds instead of ENOTTY, enabling terminal multiplexers and SSH commands that request a fresh pseudo-terminal.
prd_items.subject: Provide Unix98 pseudoterminal allocation and lifecycle

prd_items.description: Precondition: multiple guest processes may coexist or transition through zombie/stopped states. Invariant: /proc snapshots derive from the same lifecycle registry as signals/wait and expose stable per-PID identity without collapsing to the currently scheduled task. Postcondition: ps and /proc enumerate shell, foreground child, background child, status/PGID/SID, and lifecycle transitions coherently.
prd_items.subject: Publish the real guest process tree through procfs

prd_items.description: Precondition: fork-family tasks, exec, wait, signals, procfs, and a controlling terminal currently observe overlapping process state. Invariant: one lifecycle-safe registry owns PID, PPID, SID, PGID, parent/children, foreground group, running/stopped/zombie state, signal target, and address-space owner, with no last-writer shadow copies. Postcondition: every process-control and terminal path derives coherent identity and lifecycle from that registry, and stale/recycled targets are unrepresentable.
prd_items.subject: Make one registry authoritative for guest process identity and lifecycle

prd_items.description: Precondition: multiple guest processes can coexist after fork. Invariant: each process has one PGID within one SID; setpgid/getpgid enforce Linux leader, membership, exec, and existence rules without changing unrelated processes or terminal foreground ownership. Postcondition: shell pipelines and background jobs form distinct groups and group-directed signal/wait selectors address exactly their members.
prd_items.subject: Implement per-process Linux process groups

prd_items.description: Precondition: a process may or may not belong to a session with a controlling terminal. Invariant: /dev/tty resolves dynamically through the caller session, never aliases inherited fd 0 blindly, preserves terminal metadata on reopen/dup, and returns ENXIO when detached. Postcondition: shells, Node/libuv, SSH prompts, and terminal utilities can reopen their controlling terminal with correct tty and readiness behavior.
prd_items.subject: Expose the controlling terminal at /dev/tty

prd_items.description: Precondition: guest stdin/stdout may carry arbitrary binary bytes rather than UTF-8 text. Invariant: npx, runner, stdin pump, virtual devices, and host writes perform no decoding, newline conversion outside active termios, truncation, or unbounded buffering. Postcondition: all 256 byte values and large binary streams round-trip byte-for-byte through TTY-disabled pipes with matching hashes and statuses.
prd_items.subject: Preserve every byte through terminal and pipeline transports

prd_items.description: Precondition: a parent has children in multiple process groups and children may stop, continue, exit, or die by signal. Invariant: wait4 pid selectors >0, 0, -1, and <-1 filter exactly as Linux specifies; WNOHANG, WUNTRACED, and WCONTINUED report each eligible transition once without consuming unrelated status. Postcondition: shell job waits cannot reap another group and jobs/fg/bg receive coherent stopped, continued, and terminal statuses.
prd_items.subject: Implement group-filtered wait and lifecycle events

prd_items.description: Precondition: canonical host TTY read may return zero for an empty-line VEOF while the terminal remains open. Invariant: only real host descriptor closure marks the stdin pump permanently EOF; configured VEOF terminates the current canonical read and later input remains readable. Postcondition: Ctrl-D exits a Node REPL or completes one shell read as expected, while a subsequent reader can accept typed input unless the host stream actually closed.
prd_items.subject: Distinguish terminal VEOF from permanent input closure

prd_items.description: Precondition: read(fd, buf, 0) is issued while host stdin is open and empty. Invariant: count zero never waits on the pump, consumes no byte, changes no EOF/readiness state, and succeeds for every valid readable descriptor. Postcondition: zero-length reads return 0 immediately under TTY, pipe, and file redirection.
prd_items.subject: Make zero-length stdio reads return immediately

prd_items.description: Precondition: a guest requests more than the shim kernel-buffer cap from stdin or another nonseekable descriptor. Invariant: the dispatcher chunks sequentially without lseek, panic, data duplication, or allocation beyond an explicit bound while preserving partial-read and EINTR rules. Postcondition: a real one-megabyte stdin read completes or returns a Linux errno without aborting the runner.
prd_items.subject: Chunk large reads from nonseekable stdio safely

prd_items.description: Precondition: guest stdout or stderr writes after the host reader closes. Invariant: host closed-pipe errors become Linux EPIPE; an unblocked, default-disposition SIGPIPE is delivered exactly once, while ignored/caught SIGPIPE leaves write returning EPIPE. Postcondition: pipelines terminate with Linux-compatible signal/status behavior instead of EIO and preserve partial-write semantics.
prd_items.subject: Translate closed host output to EPIPE and SIGPIPE

prd_items.description: Precondition: host pipes may fill, drain, close, or remain blocked while guest poll/select/epoll and signals race. Invariant: readiness reflects actual capacity/data/EOF, O_NONBLOCK never blocks, EINTR/cancellation reaches blocked reads and writes, and queues remain bounded with no busy loop or lost wakeup. Postcondition: fill/drain probes observe correct transitions and Ctrl-C/termination promptly releases every blocked host I/O path.
prd_items.subject: Make host stdio readiness and cancellation truthful

prd_items.description: Precondition: guest duplicates fd 0/1/2 or reopens /dev/stdin, /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr, or /dev/tty. Invariant: descriptor-local flags and shared open-file-description state follow Linux rules while stream identity, isatty, direction, pump readiness, and fstat type remain attached to the underlying object. Postcondition: Node setRawMode and stty work on original, duplicated, and reopened terminal descriptors, and poll never misclassifies reopened stdin as writable output.
prd_items.subject: Preserve terminal and readiness metadata across dup and reopen

prd_items.description: Precondition: host terminal dimensions change while a guest session owns the controlling TTY. Invariant: updated dimensions are queryable and SIGWINCH is routed once to the current guest foreground process group without targeting wrapper-only threads or stopped jobs incorrectly. Postcondition: shell, Node REPL, and resize-sensitive clients receive repeated resizes and TIOCGWINSZ reports the corresponding rows and columns.
prd_items.subject: Deliver terminal resize notifications to the foreground job

prd_items.description: Precondition: stdin, stdout, and stderr may have mixed TTY/pipe redirections. Invariant: TIOCGWINSZ succeeds for any terminal-backed guest fd using its own host terminal association and does not depend on stdout being a TTY; nonterminals return ENOTTY rather than a fabricated size. Postcondition: TTY stdin with piped stdout retains real dimensions while a pipe-only invocation is non-TTY.
prd_items.subject: Query window size from the terminal descriptor actually addressed

prd_items.description: Precondition: SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGTSTP, SIGWINCH, or wake signals may land on guest, stdin-pump, network, timer, or helper host threads. Invariant: signal disposition and masking ensure every supported host signal enters one async-signal-safe owner and wakes guest dispatch exactly once; no thread can drop or double-deliver it. Postcondition: repeated signals during compute, blocked input/output, and network activity reach the intended guest group promptly and deterministically.
prd_items.subject: Make host signal capture race-free across runner threads

prd_items.description: Precondition: a guest process terminates because of a Linux signal while the host runner itself exits normally. Invariant: process wait status retains exit-versus-signal type across shim, runner, Node wrapper, and shell boundaries without low-byte truncation or conflation with host signal death. Postcondition: SIGINT, SIGTERM, and SIGSEGV produce the documented 130, 143, and 139 npx statuses while ordinary exits remain unchanged.
prd_items.subject: Report guest signal death with shell-compatible status

prd_items.description: Precondition: interactive programs need terminal and user-directory variables while the host environment may contain credentials and host-only paths. Invariant: the wrapper constructs an allowlist with validated TERM, HOME, PATH, locale, and related terminal variables, passes explicit runner --env values, never uses --forward-env, and excludes secrets by default. Postcondition: Node, shells, SSH, rsync, and neofetch receive coherent guest values while synthetic host credentials and host paths remain absent.
prd_items.subject: Forward only a safe explicit guest environment

prd_items.description: Precondition: --rev, --image, and --shell may be missing, empty, option-shaped, separator-shaped, malformed, or valid. Invariant: parsing returns a named rejection before cache/network/build effects for every invalid operand and preserves all tokens after the first literal -- byte-for-byte as guest argv. Postcondition: a live boundary matrix rejects invalid values consistently and accepts the established valid npx commands.
prd_items.subject: Make every value-taking CLI option total before side effects

prd_items.description: Precondition: help, version, diagnostics, or child completion may occur while stdout/stderr is backpressured. Invariant: the wrapper never calls immediate process.exit while authored bytes are pending; it sets exitCode or waits for stream completion without hanging on permanently closed destinations. Postcondition: diagnostics larger than pipe capacity arrive exactly and retain the intended status.
prd_items.subject: Drain wrapper output before terminating Node

prd_items.description: Precondition: --quiet is selected with an empty revision cache. Invariant: routine wrapper, Cargo, source, codesign, and image-packaging progress is suppressed while actionable errors remain visible and preserve failure status. Postcondition: first-build stderr contains no progress chatter in quiet mode and a deliberate build failure still emits its complete diagnostic.
prd_items.subject: Honor quiet mode across first-run build and packaging

prd_items.description: Precondition: npm/npx may receive interrupt, termination, hangup, quit, stop/continue, spawn failure, or parent exit while a runner and guest descendants exist. Invariant: one wrapper supervisor owns forwarding, process-group policy, wait/reap, terminal cleanup, and final status; no signal can orphan the runner or produce two terminal restorations. Postcondition: every normal and abnormal wrapper exit leaves no runner descendant and reports one deterministic shell status.
prd_items.subject: Supervise the runner as one owned process lifetime

prd_items.description: Precondition: concurrent or interrupted npx invocations may download, extract, build, codesign, package, or publish the same revision/image. Invariant: per-artifact writer locks, unique temporary paths, fsync/rename ordering, and stale-writer recovery expose either one complete matching artifact or no final artifact; runner and packager become visible as a coherent pair. Postcondition: racing and killed invocations converge on one usable cache without partial files, cross-writer deletion, or rebuild loops.
prd_items.subject: Serialize and atomically publish revision cache artifacts

prd_items.description: Precondition: source, build, image, or packaged-tar cache paths may exist while stale, truncated, corrupt, tampered, dirty-source-derived, or mislabeled by a requested revision. Invariant: a retained manifest binds npm version, requested revision, actual source commit/tree hash and cleanliness, source archive digest, Cargo.lock/toolchain/build arguments/host tuple, runner and packager hashes and signatures, OCI index plus selected manifest/config/layer digests, packager options, and final tar digest; LITEBOX_SRC content is keyed by actual tree identity; every reuse rehashes required artifacts and fails closed on mismatch. Postcondition: clean, dirty-local, label-spoof, byte-corruption, stale-manifest, wrong-platform-image, and missing-artifact probes can never execute content under an unrelated trusted cache key and rebuild only through a private atomic staging path.
prd_items.subject: Cryptographically bind every reusable cache artifact to its actual inputs

prd_items.description: Precondition: remote archives, manifests, blobs, redirects, and decompression may be slow, huge, malformed, nested, or adversarial.
