Invariant: connection/read deadlines, byte ceilings, member/path validation, decompressed-size and file-count budgets, and cancellation apply before allocation/extraction while OCI descriptor digests remain verified. Postcondition: truncated data, bad checksums, traversal, expansion bombs, and stalled servers fail by named errors without exhausting disk, memory, or cache integrity.
prd_items.subject: Bound source and image acquisition resources

prd_items.description: Precondition: a default npx invocation needs a reproducible multi-architecture image. Invariant: package metadata names an OCI index digest and records the selected platform manifest digest; cache identity binds resolved content rather than a mutable tag string. Postcondition: repeated clean invocations package byte-identical intended rootfs content and registry tag movement cannot change a published npm version.
prd_items.subject: Pin the default guest image to immutable OCI content

prd_items.description: Precondition: requested Node, BusyBox shell/pwd, gzip, OpenSSH, rsync, and neofetch must exist without runtime package installation. Invariant: one purpose-built multi-arch image pins base and package inputs, vendors neofetch with verified source/license, includes SBOM/licenses/provenance, has no credentials, and is published by immutable index digest. Postcondition: documented absolute paths exist and executable rewriting/package validation succeeds for arm64 and x86_64 manifests.
prd_items.subject: Ship a reproducible tools image with provenance

prd_items.description: Precondition: SSH and rsync-over-SSH need outbound TCP while the macOS runner currently requires separately provisioned utun state. Invariant: npx accepts an explicit validated network configuration, owns setup/cleanup or connects to a documented existing interface, scopes routing/NAT authority, and keeps offline mode as the default. Postcondition: a controlled SSH endpoint is reachable through the published CLI and failure/interrupt removes temporary host network state.
prd_items.subject: Expose a usable least-privilege external networking path

prd_items.description: Precondition: rsync destinations, known_hosts, SSH keys, and user files must survive beyond one ephemeral overlay run. Invariant: an explicit host-directory mount maps one authorized root with path traversal, symlink, uid/mode, rename, fsync, and interruption boundaries enforced; unrelated host paths remain unreachable. Postcondition: local and SSH-backed rsync persists exact destination bytes/metadata across invocations and interrupted temporary files follow documented cleanup semantics.
prd_items.subject: Expose durable guest storage for transfers and credentials

prd_items.description: Precondition: interactive SSH may read keys, agent sockets, passwords, passphrases, known_hosts, and changed host keys. Invariant: credentials enter only through explicit mounts/fds or terminal input, never argv/log/cache/image; no-echo mode restores reliably, strict host-key verification fails closed, and persistence is limited to the authorized guest home. Postcondition: synthetic credentials complete a controlled auth flow, host-key mismatch is rejected, logs/artifacts contain no secret, and Ctrl-C leaves terminal and files safe.
prd_items.subject: Protect SSH credentials and host-key state

prd_items.description: Precondition: package platform mapping currently names combinations whose runner stubs or argument contracts cannot launch. Invariant: each advertised OS/architecture has a real runner accepting the same CLI contract and live interactive/non-TTY evidence, or the parser rejects it before build with an exact supported-host list. Postcondition: macOS arm64, Linux x64, Windows x64, and every listed architecture either run the published artifact correctly or are no longer represented as supported.
prd_items.subject: Make npm host claims match executable runner support

prd_items.description: Precondition: interactive guest output can contain ANSI, OSC, DCS, APC, PM, alternate-screen, clipboard, hyperlink, mouse, paste, and device-query sequences. Invariant: the product explicitly chooses transparent trusted-guest mode or an opt-in filtered safety mode without corrupting ordinary REPL/TUI bytes; documentation names the boundary and cleanup restores host modes. Postcondition: a disposable terminal-emulator matrix witnesses the chosen behavior and untrusted output cannot gain undocumented host-terminal effects.
prd_items.subject: Define terminal control-sequence trust behavior

prd_items.description: Precondition: poll/select/epoll observes an open regular file at any offset. Invariant: readiness follows Linux regular-file semantics independent of terminal/output metadata, EOF reads return zero without a readiness hang, and mixed fd sets retain each descriptor event. Postcondition: BusyBox `read x </etc/os-release`, Node file streams, gzip, rsync, and shell redirections complete instead of blocking forever in ppoll.
prd_items.subject: Report regular files immediately readable and writable

prd_items.description: Precondition: exec has committed past old-image teardown and a later mapping, interpreter, TLS, or loader operation fails. Invariant: no guest-controlled failure reaches expect, panic, or partially resumes the prior image; resources and child status converge to one Linux signal/errno policy with the original cause retained. Postcondition: induced failures at every post-commit stage terminate only the affected guest process, wake waiters, and keep the runner coherent.
prd_items.subject: Make every post-teardown exec failure a process result

prd_items.description: Precondition: multiple writers/readers use scalar and vectored I/O, O_NONBLOCK, O_DIRECT packet mode, splice-family operations, and F_SETPIPE_SZ near bounds. Invariant: PIPE_BUF atomicity applies to full logical writes, packet boundaries and truncation obey Linux, capacity changes are bounded, and readiness/EOF/HUP remain race-free. Postcondition: real concurrent helper binaries witness native-equivalent bytes, ordering guarantees, statuses, and resource limits needed by shells, Node, gzip, SSH, and rsync.
prd_items.subject: Complete Linux pipe atomicity, packet mode, and resizing

prd_items.description: Precondition: the packager emits a tar consumed by tar_no_std and executable rewriting may alter members. Invariant: archive headers, padding, end markers, links, modes, sizes, and rewritten ELF payloads are valid and deterministic; no reader warning is ignored as benign without member-by-member proof. Postcondition: the runner opens the package with no invalid-block warning and an independent tar inventory/hash comparison proves every intended file and executable is intact.
prd_items.subject: Eliminate archive warnings and prove complete rewritten images

prd_items.description: Precondition: TLS-using guests run on real Apple Silicon with a host-selected pthread TSD slot and rewritten guest code. Invariant: packager, loader, trampoline header, context switch, and runtime offset use one load-time value and reject incompatible artifacts before guest entry. Postcondition: the published runner emits no TPIDR_EL0/TSD-slot mismatch warning and Node threads, SSH crypto, and other TLS-heavy programs run repeatedly without stale offset behavior.
prd_items.subject: Eliminate guest thread-pointer slot mismatches in release artifacts

prd_items.description: Precondition: Linux guest software branches on uname sysname and LiteBox may still expose its own brand elsewhere. Invariant: utsname fields follow Linux ABI expectations, with sysname exactly Linux and LiteBox identity placed only in compatible release/version/nodename fields that do not cause software to reject the OS. Postcondition: `uname -s` prints Linux and stock Neofetch, OpenSSH, rsync, Node, and shell feature detection no longer abort on an unknown kernel family.
prd_items.subject: Report Linux-compatible uname identity

prd_items.description: Precondition: process and system tools read /proc/version, uptime, meminfo, cpuinfo, mounts, stat, self, and per-PID status, stat, cmdline, comm, exe, fd, and fdinfo while processes fork, exec, stop, continue, exit, and reparent. Invariant: every value and symlink is a coherent view of the authoritative process, descriptor, mount, and system registries; PID/PPID/PGID/SID and descriptor flags remain process-specific; no last-writer-wins record, host-only path, or secret is exposed. Postcondition: live multi-hop shell ancestry, ps, Node, SSH, rsync, and minimal Neofetch reads stay coherent across lifecycle transitions and return Linux-compatible content instead of ENOENT or fabricated identity.
prd_items.subject: Derive complete procfs compatibility views from authoritative guest state

prd_items.description: Precondition: terminal diagnostics may query model, CPUs, frequencies, thermal, DRM, and power paths while the sandbox must not leak unintended host identity. Invariant: an explicit policy either supplies coherent synthetic /sys nodes with bounded values or intentionally omits named enrichment classes; no field contradicts procfs/uname or reveals host identifiers without opt-in. Postcondition: the documented Neofetch fidelity level is reproducible and optional Host/CPU/Resolution/Battery fields behave by policy rather than arbitrary ENOENT.
prd_items.subject: Define a privacy-safe synthetic sysfs hardware view

prd_items.description: Precondition: the runner starts as uid/gid 1000 and interactive programs require passwd lookup, HOME, USER, SHELL, config, cache, and key paths. Invariant: the selected image and environment agree on one non-root identity, its writable home and shell, restrictive default modes, and no mapping to host account databases. Postcondition: id -un, getpwuid, shell startup, Node history, SSH known_hosts/config, rsync, and Neofetch all use the documented guest identity successfully.
prd_items.subject: Provide a coherent writable guest user and home

prd_items.description: Precondition: guest fd 0/1/2 may currently be a filesystem file, pipe endpoint, terminal device, or (rarely) socket-backed descriptor; the shim's Devices backend currently maps /dev/std* names to fixed host stdio devices regardless of current guest fd redirection (litebox/src/fs/devices.rs open_file_at), losing StdioStream/StdioStatusFlags metadata and bypassing redirection, causing ENOTTY/FIONBIO/readiness regressions (litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/file.rs stdin_read_would_block, litebox_shim_linux/src/lib.rs stdio init). Per man7 open(2)/proc_pid_fd(5), opening /dev/stdin (a symlink to /proc/self/fd/0) is a normal path-based open through procfs, which creates a NEW open-file description: independent offset and status flags for a regular file, a new endpoint on the same pipe object for a FIFO, a fresh per-open handle sharing termios/state for a TTY, and ENXIO for a bare socket fd. dup/dup3 is a materially different operation (shares offset+status flags, cannot honor a new access mode) and must not be used as a silent stand-in. Invariant: for every reachable current fd-0/1/2 subsystem, the reopen path dispatches to that subsystem's real open semantics; O_CLOEXEC affects only the new descriptor; entry metadata (StdioStream) is attached to the freshly created open-file description, not copied from a dup; readiness of the new descriptor tracks the underlying shared object identically to a native reopen. Postcondition: opening /dev/stdin|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr against a file-backed, pipe-backed, or terminal-backed current fd 0/1/2 produces a descriptor with correct independent-or-shared state per object type and correct ioctl/FIONBIO/poll behavior; against a socket-backed fd it fails ENXIO; FD_CLOEXEC on the new descriptor is independent of the source.
prd_items.subject: Reopen /dev/stdin,/dev/stdout,/dev/stderr with subsystem-aware Linux-compatible semantics, not a dup approximation
prd_items.witness_evidence: litebox/src/fs/devices.rs open_file_at (fixed Device::from_name mapping); litebox_shim_linux/src/stdio.rs test_stdio_flags_with_dup (proves dup shares status flags, fresh open via /proc/self/fd/0 does not); man7.org open(2)/dup(2)/proc_pid_fd(5) reopen-vs-dup contract

prd_items.description: Precondition: the host stdin provider returns data, zero, EINTR, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, a retryable platform error, or true endpoint closure while guest readers may be blocking or nonblocking. Invariant: only a witnessed terminal or pipe endpoint closure becomes permanent EOF; EINTR returns promptly to guest signal handling, EAGAIN remains temporary unavailability, and all other host errors map to a specific Linux errno without poisoning future reads. Postcondition: live nonblocking, interrupted, recovered-error, and actual-close probes distinguish EAGAIN, cancellation, error, and EOF, with later input still consumable after every nonterminal condition.
prd_items.subject: Preserve host stdin errors without manufacturing permanent EOF

prd_items.description: Precondition: a host-backed input stream may contain buffered bytes when its producer closes and may be observed by poll, select, epoll, or a blocking read through original or reopened descriptors. Invariant: readiness is derived from one shared stream state; buffered bytes report readable before final HUP, drained permanent closure reports readable plus HUP as Linux requires, canonical VEOF is a one-read event rather than HUP, and every registered waiter is awakened exactly when its observable state changes. Postcondition: live data-then-close, empty-close, VEOF-then-more-input, duplicate/reopen, and concurrent-waiter probes observe identical bytes and Linux-compatible IN/HUP transitions without hangs or lost wakeups.
prd_items.subject: Represent stdio data, EOF, and HUP as distinct readiness states

prd_items.description: Precondition: a guest calls epoll_pwait with a null or valid non-null Linux signal-mask pointer while signals and fd readiness may race. Invariant: a non-null mask is validated and installed atomically for exactly the wait interval, unmaskable signals remain unblocked, pending delivery and EINTR follow Linux ordering, and the prior mask is restored on readiness, timeout, signal, or error. Postcondition: live ready-before-signal, signal-before-ready, simultaneous, timeout, invalid-pointer, invalid-size, and repeated-interruption probes return Linux-compatible events/status without panic, lost signals, or leaked mask state.
prd_items.subject: Implement atomic temporary signal masks for epoll_pwait

prd_items.description: Precondition: OCI extraction yields executable ELF members and one or more rewrites may succeed, fail, produce an invalid trailer, or target an unsupported architecture. Invariant: original executable bytes are never silently substituted after a rewrite failure; every required executable is validated for guest architecture and rewrite stamp before any final tar becomes visible; diagnostics identify the exact path without exposing host secrets. Postcondition: a live image with one deliberately unrewritable required ELF exits nonzero and publishes no final tar, while a valid image inventory proves every required executable is rewritten and runnable.
prd_items.subject: Fail packaging when any required executable cannot be rewritten

prd_items.description: Precondition: image layers contain relative or absolute symlinks, hardlinks, whiteouts, replacements, and executable launchers such as /usr/local/bin/npm pointing into /usr/local/lib/node_modules. Invariant: layer order, link target bytes, path normalization, modes, ownership, and overwrite semantics match OCI extraction without flattening a link into misplaced regular-file content or permitting root escape. Postcondition: independent tar inventory and live guest readlink/exec probes preserve all selected link chains, including a working Node npm launcher, and malformed cycles or escaping targets fail with a named packaging error.
prd_items.subject: Preserve OCI symlinks and executable launcher topology exactly

prd_items.description: Precondition: the minimal OS/Kernel/Memory Neofetch contract is live and a full/default Neofetch claim is requested. Invariant: Host, Uptime, Packages, Shell, Resolution, DE/WM, themes, Terminal, CPU, GPU, disk, battery, users, locale, and network fields each have an explicit guest-derived, privacy-safe value or an explicitly absent representation; no host hardware identity is guessed or leaked. Postcondition: stock default Neofetch output is field-by-field documented and live-witnessed against the selected policy, or product documentation continues to claim only the minimal contract.
prd_items.subject: Define and implement every optional Neofetch system field before claiming full output

prd_items.description: Precondition: inherited stdio may be a TTY with deliberately non-default flags/control bytes, three different terminals, or redirected non-TTY descriptors. Invariant: each terminal object snapshots the addressed host fd once, guest TCGETS initially reflects that exact translatable state, non-TTY descriptors remain ENOTTY, and no fixed synthetic defaults or hard-coded stdout fd replace observed state. Postcondition: live sentinel configurations across stdin, stdout, stderr, dup, /dev/std*, and /dev/tty round-trip expected Linux fields and restore the exact original host blob after every normal and abnormal exit path.
prd_items.subject: Seed guest terminal attributes from the actual addressed host terminal

prd_items.description: Precondition: a clean source build selects a host tuple and digest-pinned OCI platform and produces runner, packager, and packaged tar artifacts. Invariant: one versioned canonical manifest records npm version/tarball integrity, requested and actual clean source identity, Cargo.lock/toolchain/build arguments, host tuple, binary hashes/signatures, OCI index/selected manifest/config/layer digests, packager options, tar inventory/hash, and macOS signing entitlements; the manifest itself is hashable and atomically published with its artifacts. Postcondition: clean-cache npx acceptance can start from registry metadata and prove every executed byte back to immutable source and OCI descriptors, while any changed input yields a different cache identity and manifest.
prd_items.subject: Emit and retain one verifiable manifest for every release artifact

prd_items.description: Precondition: LinuxShimBuilder receives any None/Some combination of guest interface and gateway IPv4 overrides and constructs Network exactly once. Invariant: the configured interface address is stored once in the Network-owned device, drives smoltcp CIDR selection, own-address loopback classification, socket local identity, and netlink/getifaddrs output; the configured gateway mutates the existing default route in place; no hard-coded 10.0.0.2/10.0.0.1 copy may contradict runtime state. Postcondition: live default, interface-only, gateway-only, and both-override runner invocations observe the selected interface via guest ip/getifaddrs, connect to their own selected address through loopback, and route outbound traffic through the selected gateway without touching either protected file.
prd_items.subject: Propagate configured guest network identity through data plane and introspection

prd_items.description: Precondition: a guest opens NETLINK_ROUTE and requests RTM_GETROUTE after Network construction with default or overridden gateway state. Invariant: route messages derive from the same Network route state used for packet egress, preserve sequence/multipart framing and IPv4 prefix/gateway attributes, and never fall back to canned defaults. Postcondition: live BusyBox `ip route` reports the exact default gateway for default, gateway-only, and both-override invocations, while malformed or unsupported requests terminate with Linux-compatible netlink responses rather than hanging.
prd_items.subject: Report configured default routes through rtnetlink

prd_items.description: Precondition: a caller supplies optional interface/gateway IPv4 values including unspecified, loopback, multicast, limited broadcast, subnet network/broadcast, identical interface/gateway, or a gateway outside the fixed /24. Invariant: validation is total and side-effect-free, names the rejected operand/reason, accepts only a usable unicast interface plus reachable unicast gateway under the selected prefix, and never converts invalid input into a partially configured smoltcp/netlink/device state. Postcondition: every invalid equivalence class exits nonzero before guest execution and every valid default/interface-only/gateway-only/both combination remains coherent across packet routing, own-address loopback, getsockname, and netlink output.
prd_items.subject: Reject unusable guest and gateway IPv4 overrides before network construction

prd_items.description: Precondition: litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/epoll.rs's EpollDescriptor::try_from resolves a guest raw fd to a typed subsystem descriptor and epoll registers a weak reference keyed on (guest raw fd, TypedFd pointer); litebox/src/fd/mod.rs's Descriptors::duplicate creates a new TypedFd/token sharing the same underlying Arc<RwLock<DescriptorEntry>> but with a distinct token pointer, so closing the originally-registered duplicate can invalidate the epoll registration's weak reference while another live duplicate of the same open-file description still exists -- violating Linux's rule that an epoll registration survives until every duplicate referencing that open-file description is closed. Invariant: epoll registration identity and liveness track the shared DescriptorEntry (the open-file description), not any single duplicate's token pointer; readiness delivery and registration validity are unaffected by which duplicate fd number closes first. Postcondition: registering fd A for epoll, dup'ing A to B, closing A, then continuing to receive/deliver events sourced from B's shared object behaves identically to native Linux epoll_ctl semantics, live-proven with a real epoll_wait sequence across a dup+close.
prd_items.subject: Fix epoll registration lifetime so it tracks the shared open-file description, not the exact duplicated typed-fd token
prd_items.witness_evidence: litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/epoll.rs EpollDescriptor::try_from and weak (raw fd, TypedFd) registration key; litebox/src/fd/mod.rs Descriptors::duplicate (shared Arc<RwLock<DescriptorEntry>>, distinct token); epoll(7) open-file-description lifetime contract

prd_items.description: Precondition: litebox_common_linux/src/lib.rs's IoctlArg enum and ioctl decoder only recognize TCGETS/TCSETS; TCSETSW(0x5403)/TCSETSF(0x5404) constants and variants are absent; litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/file.rs's TCSETS handler always calls platform.set_terminal_raw_mode with no NOW/DRAIN/FLUSH distinction; litebox_platform_macos_userland/src/lib.rs always issues host tcsetattr with TCSANOW. Invariant: a typed TerminalSetAction{Now,Drain,Flush} threads from the decoded ioctl command through the shim into the platform boundary; Drain and Flush additionally guarantee prior writes are flushed to the terminal before the attribute change is applied (matching POSIX tcsetattr semantics), and Flush additionally discards unread input, including bytes already buffered in the macOS StdinPump ring/producer thread, not only the host tty's own input queue. Postcondition: TCSETSW maps to host TCSADRAIN, TCSETSF maps to host TCSADRAIN plus an explicit StdinPump discard of any currently buffered unread bytes (coordinated with the producer thread so no race reintroduces discarded bytes), and both return the same success/error semantics as TCSETS otherwise; TCGETS/TCSETS/TCSETSW/TCSETSF are all live-provable against a real PTY.
prd_items.subject: Implement TCSETSW and TCSETSF with typed NOW/DRAIN/FLUSH terminal-set actions
prd_items.witness_evidence: litebox_common_linux/src/lib.rs IoctlArg enum (TCGETS/TCSETS only); litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/file.rs TCSETS handler; litebox_platform_macos_userland/src/lib.rs set_terminal_raw_mode (hardcoded TCSANOW); litebox/src/platform/stdin_pump.rs (no discard API); POSIX tcsetattr TCSADRAIN/TCSAFLUSH semantics

prd_items.description: Precondition: a fresh SPECIFY instruction has been dispatched and recall still fails with SQLite rc=5/database-is-locked, as witnessed in .gm/exec-spool/out/recall-npm-release-1787095221-1787139400000000001.json and the matching instruction reports the same locked code-index database. Invariant: never delete a dot-lock or restart the shared daemon while any live process owns the database; preserve all .gm data and other sessions; diagnose lock ownership before mutation and keep one writer per state surface. Postcondition: recall and code-index overview complete successfully on two consecutive fresh dispatches, or a controlled replacement retrieval path exposes the same durable memory corpus while the underlying gm defect is repaired, with no data loss and no long-gap denial.
prd_items.subject: Restore gm recall/code-index availability without risking live database writers
prd_items.witness_evidence: recall-npm-release-1787095221-1787139400000000001.json: semantic retrieval unavailable, exec rc=5 database is locked; instruction-npm-release-1787095221-1787139500000000001.json: codeinsight prepare rc=5 database is locked

prd_items.description: litebox_runner_linux_on_macos_userland gains the orchestration: read the snapshot file and base tar BEFORE enable_seatbelt_sandbox() (the profile denies file opens), build the shim through the restore path instead of load_program, rebuild the host-side machinery (stdin pump, net worker, timer threads, signal handlers/altstack), then run_thread with the restored context. Clock policy: guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC is host CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW (lib.rs:1418-1424) and jumps forward by the restore downtime; boot_time feeds sysinfo uptime and absolute sleep deadlines (syscalls/process.rs:2192-2230). Record wall+monotonic at checkpoint, compute downtime at restore, re-arm outstanding itimers with remaining-time semantics, and document the forward jump for v1 (relative-timeout guests unaffected); a shim-level monotonic offset applied at the clock_gettime choke point is the follow-up if real guests misbehave. Refuse restore on hwcap/page-size/tar-hash mismatch from the container header.
prd_items.subject: Runner flags (--checkpoint-after-load/--snapshot-out/--restore-from), seatbelt ordering, and monotonic-downtime compensation

prd_items.description: litebox/src/fs/in_mem.rs gains tree (de)serialization: RootDir.entries is a HashMap<normalized-path, Entry> of pure data (FileX.data Cow, DirX.children, SymLinkX.target, perms, atime/mtime/ctime, unique_id -- in_mem.rs:1223-1364), plus current_working_dir and unique_id_freshness so post-restore creates cannot collide with restored inodes. Restore builds the tree, then the fd-table row relinks open Descriptor::File entries to nodes by unique_id and reinstates position/append_mode/read-allowed flags. The tar_ro base is never serialized -- the runner re-supplies the identical tar (enforced by the container's tar hash) -- and /proc is rebuilt from restored task state, so the writable upper is the only FS state that exists. Cow<'static,[u8]> shared with the tar must be re-borrowed from the fresh tar on restore, not deep-copied into the snapshot.
prd_items.subject: Serialize the in_mem writable upper FS (tree, perms, timestamps, unique_ids) and open-file positions

prd_items.description: The south-side restore half. Take macos-guest-address-space-reservation (one enforced VM_FLAGS_FIXED PROT_NONE reservation over [GUEST_ADDR_MIN, GUEST_ADDR_MAX) at startup) as a hard dependency -- it makes the entire guest window structurally free in a fresh runner, turning fixed-address restore from usually-works into guaranteed, and retiring the reserved_pages one-time snapshot whose failure mode (late host allocations intruding into the guest range, 200k measured) is exactly what would randomly corrupt a restore. Sequence: allocate every VMA with FixedAddressBehavior::NoReplace, write page blobs RW, flip permissions via update_permissions (which already migrates refused mprotect(+EXEC) to fresh MAP_JIT mappings, docs/macos.md:105-120), re-register JIT regions for fault-driven W^X toggling (lib.rs:3067-3078), sys_icache_invalidate exec ranges, then RE-PUBLISH every trampoline header word from the guest_images registry (syscall-entry stub address and TSD slot offset are host .text/runtime values that ASLR and pthread_key_create change across processes -- guest.rs:91-108, lib.rs:1738-1762; this is the macos-trampoline-header-invariant row's invariant, enforced) plus any sigreturn-trampoline addresses. Handlers/altstack/TSD slots are re-installed before the first resume.
prd_items.subject: Restore guest pages at identical VAs on macOS: PROT_NONE reservation dependency, MAP_JIT recreation, trampoline-header republish

prd_items.description: Everything the MVP rows deliberately refuse. Per-thread contexts live on each thread's own host stack (GuestThreadState published via TSD, guest.rs:1440-1456), so a multi-thread checkpoint must quiesce every thread through the tier-1 interrupt path and enumerate them (no central task registry exists today -- ProcessTable tracks processes, not threads). Threads parked mid-syscall (WaitState WAITING, litebox/src/event/wait.rs:45-55) hold their PtRegs at the syscall-entry point and their host stack inside shim.syscall(ctx); resuming them needs Linux's restart model -- roll pc back to the SVC gate and re-issue, or fabricate EINTR -- applied per blocking syscall class (futex, epoll, read, wait4), plus serialization of FutexManager wait queues and the event system's wakers. Forked guests add SharedAddressSpace token state and parked MemoryImages (syscalls/process.rs:268-330). Design the task-registry and restart protocol first; estimate after tier-1 lands, informed by which blocking classes real pre-warmed workloads actually sit in.
prd_items.subject: Multi-threaded + forked guests and mid-syscall checkpointing (ERESTART-style resume), the deferred hard half

prd_items.description: The north-side half of the snapshot, as a new litebox_shim_linux/src/snapshot.rs plus (de)hydration helpers in syscalls/{process,signal,file}.rs. Task: pid/ppid/tid, Credentials, comm, FsState (umask + cwd), SignalState (handlers/mask/both pending queues/altstack/saved-sigsuspend-mask -- all plain data, syscalls/signal/mod.rs:30-56), FilesState. The fd table is the design constraint: open file descriptions live in LiteBox's global Descriptors table (litebox/src/litebox.rs:102-103) with per-descriptor state like the in_mem Descriptor::File position (litebox/src/fs/in_mem.rs:1414-1421) stored per-entry, so the dump must walk raw_descriptor_store, tag each entry by subsystem TypeId, and relink by unique_id on restore. gVisor's policy, adopted verbatim: checkpoint REFUSES loudly when any fd outside {stdio, in_mem regular files/dirs} exists (no sockets, pipes, epoll, eventfd, unix in v1) rather than silently dropping state. GlobalState scalars: pgid, termios, brk (PageManager), next_thread_id, boot_time plus recorded wall/monotonic checkpoint timestamps; ProcessTable must be empty beyond the initial process or the checkpoint refuses (fork/threads are the later row).
prd_items.subject: Serialize/restore shim Task + GlobalState (creds, cwd, signals, fd table restricted to stdio + in_mem files, termios, pgid, brk, clocks)

prd_items.description: The cheapest 80% of the pre-warmed-guest win. After LinuxShim::load_program returns (litebox_shim_linux/src/lib.rs:358-435) and EnterShim::init has filled the entry PtRegs, the guest has never executed, so the entire state -- fresh shim objects, fully loaded and already-rewritten/patched memory (trampoline headers published), entry PtRegs -- is consistent by construction with no interrupt, no syscall-boundary discipline, no in-flight anything. Dump = all VMAs + page contents + fresh Task/GlobalState scalars + empty fd table beyond stdio. Restore skips tar parsing, ELF loading, AOT verification and trampoline publication entirely: allocate_pages at the recorded fixed addresses, copy blobs, restore shim objects, run_thread with the saved PtRegs. This is the Firecracker boot-template flow and needs none of the quiesce machinery of tier-1; land it first as the proving ground for the container format and the restore path (MAP_JIT recreation, JIT-region re-registration, trampoline-header republish all get exercised here first).
prd_items.subject: Tier-0 snapshot at the post-load_program/pre-first-instruction point (fast cold-start with zero quiesce work)

prd_items.description: Mid-run checkpoints capture at the exact point run_thread's loop decides to resume (litebox_platform_macos_userland/src/guest.rs:1486-1549), where the full register file is already materialized: GPRs in the caller-owned PtRegs, FP/SIMD in GuestThreadState.guest_fp (reachable via ThreadProvider::get_fp_state, lib.rs:2617-2623), guest_sp recorded by enter_shim (litebox_shim_linux/src/lib.rs:247-251 -- its comment already names this snapshot use). Capturing at the resume decision rather than at syscall entry means x0 already holds the result and no ERESTART-style syscall-restart machinery is ever needed: restore is re-enter_guest_asm with the saved PtRegs. To force a compute-bound guest to a capture point, reuse interrupt_thread (SIGUSR2 -> interrupt_signal_handler -> prepare_interrupt_delivery -> shim.interrupt(ctx) with an exact mcontext+NEON capture, guest.rs:1238-1278). Add a small public platform API that quiesces and hands the triple (PtRegs, FpState, TP) to the shim's snapshot module; refuse capture while a guest signal handler frame is in flight (sigreturn-trampoline host addresses embedded on the guest stack) -- the shim knows when it built a frame in process_signals. Threads blocked mid-syscall (WaitState WAITING) are out of scope here; that is the ERESTART row.
prd_items.subject: Tier-1 quiesce + capture: checkpoint a running single-threaded guest at the guest-exit resume point via the existing SIGUSR2 interrupt path

prd_items.description: Define the on-disk shape every other snapshot row reads and writes, before any of them lands. Hand-rolled alloc-only framing in the tree's existing zerocopy idiom (precedent: litebox_syscall_rewriter's LITEBOX0 TrampolineHeader64) -- magic LBSNAP0, format version, per-section versions, and a header carrying arch, host page size (16 KiB on this host, not assumed), GUEST_ADDR_MIN/MAX, AT_HWCAP/AT_HWCAP2, and the SHA-256 of the base tar so a restore against the wrong image refuses loudly instead of corrupting. Sections: VMAPS (start/end/VmFlags per PageManager::mappings() entry), PAGES (sparse 16 KiB blobs, zero pages elided), THREADS (PtRegs + GuestFpState + guest TP, all already fixed-layout), TASK, FDTABLE, FS_INMEM, GLOBALS. serde is deliberately not introduced (the workspace only has it in an OP-TEE runner). Unknown version/arch/hwcap/page-size/tar-hash mismatch at open time is a hard error, never a best-effort load.
prd_items.subject: Versioned guest-snapshot container format (magic + sectioned, zerocopy-style, no serde)

prd_items.description: Precondition: git worktree list shows ~40+ registered worktrees under .claude/worktrees from prior sessions/workflows, gitignored and untracked so they do not pollute git status. Invariant: only worktrees with live, still-relevant branches remain registered. Postcondition: `git worktree remove` (or prune) clears completed/abandoned worktrees, keeping worktree count proportional to active work.
prd_items.subject: Prune completed/stale git worktrees under .claude/worktrees

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. CONDITIONAL: only if litebox's Linux shim/runner is ever targeted at Windows/WSL2 hosts. From OpenShell study (GPU report, ranked item 7): /dev/dxg is the WSL2 sole GPU device node; /usr/lib/wsl holds CDI-injected driver libs and needs explicit listing to defeat Landlock cross-mount traversal gaps; presence detection via /dev/dxg (openshell-sandbox/src/lib.rs:1487-1489); skip nonexistent native nvidia nodes on WSL2 and vice versa in merge logic. Precondition: a WSL2 host target exists for litebox. Invariant: native-Linux behavior unchanged. Postcondition: GPU guest works under litebox on WSL2, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: WSL2 /dev/dxg + /usr/lib/wsl handling if the Linux shim targets WSL2 hosts (conditional)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (GPU report, ranked item 2; source openshell-sandbox/src/lib.rs:1434-1631): when /dev/nvidiactl or /dev/dxg is present, widen the Landlock baseline -- RO: /run/nvidia-persistenced (EACCES vs ECONNREFUSED changes NVML error semantics), /usr/lib/wsl (WSL2 CDI libs; explicit listing defeats Landlock cross-mount traversal gaps); RW: /dev/nvidiactl, /dev/nvidia-uvm, /dev/nvidia-uvm-tools, /dev/nvidia-modeset, /dev/dxg, and /proc PROMOTED to RW because cuInit() writes /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/comm and fails with error 304 otherwise; must be /proc not /proc/self/task because Landlock rules bind inodes and children have different procfs inodes. Per-GPU /dev/nvidiaN enumeration at runtime (skip bare /dev/nvidia). Precondition: litebox Landlock ruleset live (done, 4f68241). Invariant: enrichment only fires on GPU presence; non-GPU hosts get byte-identical ruleset to today. Postcondition: NVML/CUDA guest init succeeds under the ruleset on GPU hardware, witnessed live; failure modes documented inline (NVML persistenced EACCES, cuInit 304).
prd_items.subject: Presence-triggered GPU baseline paths + /proc RW promotion in the runner Landlock ruleset

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (process-supervision report, ranked item 1; source openshell-supervisor-process/src/main_session.rs, 511 lines): the single most portable artifact -- depends only on owning guest fd 0/1/2 backing objects, which the shim already does. Port: sequenced output ring evicting past 1MiB (OUTPUT_BUFFER_BYTES), replay-then-live cursors for new subscribers, lag error with skipped-count resync (MainOutputLagged), single-owner input lease with read-only degradation, retained master for resize/signal, 2s drain-then-Exit with exit replayed once to post-exit subscribers. Precondition: answer litebox-side unknown -- how guest fds 0/1/2 are currently backed (inherited host stdio vs pipes), which determines integration invasiveness. Invariant: guest write path never blocks on a slow/absent consumer beyond buffer capacity (drop/evict, never stall). Postcondition: attach/detach cycles against a running guest with replay and single-writer stdin, witnessed live via the runner/broker.
prd_items.subject: Runner-level session multiplexer: retained guest stdio, 1MiB sequenced replay, stdin lease, lag+Exit semantics

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (GPU report, ranked item 1): in litebox userland modes GPU support IS (a) fd passthrough of /dev/nvidiactl, /dev/nvidiaN, /dev/nvidia-uvm{,-tools}, /dev/nvidia-modeset through interposed open/openat, and (b) verbatim ioctl relay on those fds -- the NVIDIA ioctl ABI is too large and unstable to emulate. Precondition: answer the open litebox-side unknown first -- does the shim/runner currently pass through host device fds at all, and can ioctl interposition relay arbitrary unknown ioctls on a passthrough fd (determines 'wire existing machinery' vs 'build ioctl relay'). Invariant: passthrough fds are scoped to an explicit allowlist; no other host device nodes become reachable. Postcondition: a CUDA/NVML guest binary (e.g. nvidia-smi equivalent) runs under the Linux userland runner on GPU hardware, witnessed live. Evidence: openshell GPU report sections 2,5.
prd_items.subject: GPU device-node passthrough + ioctl relay in shim_linux / Linux userland runner

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (process-supervision report, ranked item 2): shim emulates the slave side -- isatty, termios-lite, TIOCGWINSZ/TIOCSWINSZ, line-discipline subset -- backed by a runner-held master composing with litebox-session-multiplexer; unlocks interactive guests (node REPL, shells, TUI agents). OpenShell lessons to reuse when wiring clients: shell-without-pty must stay supported (VS Code Remote-SSH misdetect story, ssh.rs:546-559); resize routes to attached session else per-channel PTY; exit-status protocol ordering data -> EOF -> (2s grandchild timeout) -> exit-status -> close. Precondition: litebox-session-multiplexer. Invariant: non-PTY guests see zero behavior change; isatty answers are truthful per-fd. Postcondition: an interactive guest program reading termios/winsize and driving a line discipline works under litebox, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Shim PTY-slave emulation backed by the runner multiplexer (isatty/termios-lite/winsize)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (process-supervision report, ranked item 4; source sandbox/linux/seccomp.rs): formalize litebox's ad-hoc ENOSYS answers into a declarative allow/block table in OpenShell's profile shape -- default-allow with targeted blocks, per-entry threat-model comments, and the errno-selection discipline: ENOSYS where libcs have fallback paths (clone3 -> clone fallback only fires on ENOSYS, seccomp.rs:151-166), EPERM where the operation must hard-fail; argument-conditioned rules via masked-flag matching (execveat+AT_EMPTY_PATH, clone/unshare+CLONE_NEWUSER). NETLINK_ROUTE-only carve-out is the precedent litebox already effectively implemented for os.networkInterfaces. Precondition: none. Invariant: every blocked syscall carries a one-line rationale; errno choice per entry is justified by the libc-fallback test. Postcondition: the table drives shim answers; a guest probe binary witnesses the documented errno per blocked syscall, verified live.
prd_items.subject: Declarative shim syscall-policy table with OpenShell seccomp errno-selection discipline

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (process-supervision report, ranked item 3): address the Node child_process ENOSYS gap NOT with in-guest fork emulation (research-grade; XNU-x18 constraint on macOS; multithreaded guests) but with runner-supervised sibling instances -- shim answers vfork/posix_spawn/clone-for-exec with an RPC to the runner, which launches a NEW litebox instance from the same image with fd wiring (pipes/PTY) bridged back as child stdio; wait/exit-status flows through the broker. Explicitly EXCLUDES full fork. Precondition: three litebox-side unknowns to answer first -- (a) which exact syscalls Node child_process.spawn issues under the guest libc (clone3/clone/vfork/posix_spawn internals; OpenShell's clone3-ENOSYS trick shows the errno answered determines which glibc fallback fires -- verify live per guest-test-binary recipe); (b) whether the shim models multiple guest processes at all (pids, wait4, exit-status propagation) or a broker-level process registry must be built; (c) cold-start cost of a sibling instance (npm spawns many short-lived children; tens-of-ms+ cold start implies an instance pool or pre-warmed template). Invariant: child stdio wiring is explicit per-spawn; no fd leaks across instances. Postcondition: node -e "require('child_process').spawnSync('echo',['hi'])" works under litebox, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: posix_spawn/vfork fast path via broker-orchestrated sibling litebox instances (Node child_process gap)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (process-supervision report, ranked item 5; sources seccomp.rs:59-121 apply_supervisor_prelude, landlock.rs:105-127 two-phase): extend the just-reenabled Landlock work (4f68241) -- (a) after runner bootstrap completes, self-apply a seccomp filter synchronized across ALL threads (TSYNC / apply_filter_all_threads) stripping syscalls the runner only needs during startup (mount family, module load, kexec, bpf, perf_event_open, userfaultfd); (b) if the runner ever gains a privileged setup phase, adopt the PreparedRuleset split: open PathFds as root, restrict_self after drop; (c) bounding-set clear-with-probe-verification if ever started privileged (all four outcome branches handled, process.rs:357-394). Precondition: current Landlock wiring (done). Invariant: steady-state runner syscall surface is a strict subset of bootstrap surface; prelude install failure is fatal (fail-closed), never warn-and-continue. Postcondition: post-prelude, a stripped syscall attempted from the runner fails, witnessed live (e.g. via strace on CI).
prd_items.subject: Runner self-hardening pass: post-bootstrap TSYNC seccomp prelude + two-phase Landlock ordering

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (GPU report, ranked item 4; source openshell-core/src/gpu.rs:40-51,314-344, proto/openshell.proto:826-855): GPU is resource intent, deliberately NOT part of the security policy -- a gpu:{count?} field with semantics: omitted count -> 1, zero -> error, exact-device lists with no duplicates and count==len validation, single exact device compatible with default request, driver-owned default selection. Precondition: none (config surface only). Invariant: GPU request never widens the security policy by itself; enrichment (litebox-gpu-landlock-enrichment) is presence/policy driven. Postcondition: invalid requests (0, duplicate devices, count mismatch) are rejected with actionable errors, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Policy-independent GPU resource-request field with OpenShell-compatible validation semantics

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. DEFERRED until the SNP backend needs GPUs. From OpenShell study (GPU report, ranked item 6): port the openshell-vfio lifecycle for SNP guests -- IOMMU-group companion binding with reverse-order rollback (gpu.rs:84-163), new_id registration refcounted across same-ID GPUs (bind.rs:256-317), unbind/new_id/driver_override/drivers_probe sequence with poll confirm and cleanup_partial_bind (bind.rs:125-200), deregister-new_id-FIRST restore ordering (bind.rs:204-254), RAII PciBindGuard, persisted gpu-bindings.json + reconcile_stale_bindings crash recovery. OpenShell does NOT cover NVIDIA confidential-computing GPU mode + SNP attestation interplay -- that investigation is part of this row. Open unknown: whether the SNP guest kernel image carries the nvidia module (OpenShell punts guest-driver provisioning to 'a compatible sandbox image'). Precondition: SNP backend has a GPU requirement; litebox-snp-boot-channel (attestation-bound channel) preferred first. Invariant: host GPU bindings are always restorable; a crashed litebox never leaves a GPU orphaned on vfio-pci without a reconcile path. Postcondition: CUDA workload inside an SNP guest on passthrough GPU, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: SNP GPU passthrough: port openshell-vfio lifecycle + investigate NVIDIA CC-mode/attestation interplay (deferred)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (GPU report, ranked item 5; sources openshell-core/src/gpu.rs:145-257 CdiGpuDefaultSelector, openshell-driver-vm/src/gpu.rs:26-151 GpuInventory, openshell-vfio/src/reconcile.rs:16-101): normalized inventory, concurrency-safe round-robin default selection with explicit all opt-in gating, per-slot assignment persisted to a state file, startup reconcile that restores/cleans stale bindings and rewrites only failed entries for next-start retry. Precondition: litebox-gpu-resource-request-schema. Invariant: an assigned GPU is held until explicit release or crash-reconcile; double-assignment is structurally impossible (assignment under one lock). Postcondition: broker survives kill -9 mid-assignment and startup reconcile restores a consistent inventory, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Multi-GPU inventory, round-robin selection, persisted assignment + crash reconcile (broker host)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (GPU report, ranked item 3): CDI (Container Device Interface) is the ecosystem interchange format across docker/podman/k8s (openshell-driver-docker CDISpecDirs detection, podman /dev scan producing nvidia.com/gpu=N names); parsing nvidia-container-toolkit CDI specs (/etc/cdi, /var/run/cdi) to derive the device/library allowlist lets litebox inherit driver-version coverage for free instead of hardcoding paths. Precondition: litebox-gpu-device-passthrough scoped (defines where the allowlist is consumed). Invariant: absent/malformed CDI specs degrade to the static baseline list, never to an empty allowlist that silently breaks GPUs nor an allow-everything fallback. Postcondition: on a host with nvidia-container-toolkit, the derived allowlist matches the CDI spec contents, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Consume NVIDIA CDI specs to derive GPU device/library allowlists

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (policy report, ranked item 3; sources opa.rs:659-878 OpaEngine swap discipline, openshell.proto ReportPolicyStatus): co-designed with the pending WASI-capability broker redesign (broker-wasi-capability-redesign row), NOT bolted on after. Adopt wholesale: build-and-validate the candidate fully through the same pipeline as initial load, swap under lock, single AtomicU64 generation bump; generation guards on long-lived broker objects (pipes/sockets) force-close objects authorized under a stale generation; implement the four ack kinds (initial / loaded / unchanged-hash / failed) so a control plane can distinguish 'version bumped, content identical' from 'reload required'; on candidate validation failure enter fail-closed quarantine (empty capability set) or retain-last-valid per configured mode, with rejected-revision dedup. Open question: broker protocol version tolerance for new message types (BROKER_PROTOCOL_VERSION exists; negotiation semantics unverified). Precondition: broker control channel (exists, litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/lib.rs:87-96). Invariant: readers observe only old-set or new-set, never a mix; a bad candidate never displaces last-known-good. Postcondition: a capability change pushed to a running guest takes effect without restart and stale-authorized objects close, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Generation-stamped mutable capability set shared by shim+broker, push+ack over broker control socket

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (policy report, ranked item 2; source denial_aggregator.rs, ~210 lines): capture shim EPERM/EACCES returns with (op, path/destination, guest binary identity) into a bounded buffer; flush over the existing broker control channel; aggregate on the host keyed by (op, dest, subject) with counts, first/last-seen, and capped samples. This is the prerequisite observable for denial-to-proposal and policy work. Open question the row must answer: where in the shim's syscall dispatch the tap sits so it costs ~nothing on the hot path. Precondition: none. Invariant: the tap never blocks the guest (bounded buffer, drop-oldest); no denial data includes secrets. Postcondition: a guest program generating denials produces aggregated host-side records matching the generated (op, dest, subject) tuples, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Shim error-return denial tap -> broker-host aggregation keyed by (op, dest, subject)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (policy report, ranked item 1): introduce a minimal typed policy object (fs ro/rw path lists, compatibility mode, version + content hash from day one -- OpenShell's whole ack protocol keys off policy_hash/config_revision) as an explicit runner input; widen enable_landlock_filesystem_ruleset past READ_FILE-only to ro/rw directory support with per-inode access tailoring (fstat the already-open O_PATH fd: directories keep full rights, files masked to file rights -- avoids invalid dir-rights-on-file rules and pathname TOCTOU, openshell landlock.rs:350-365); classify the availability probe ENOSYS/EOPNOTSUPP/EPERM and log loudly on degradation, replacing the silent return at litebox_platform_linux_userland/src/lib.rs:519-521; add best_effort/hard_requirement compatibility mode; refuse the degenerate zero-valid-paths ruleset (would deny everything, openshell landlock.rs:240-246). Precondition: none beyond current Landlock wiring. Invariant: absent a policy input, behavior is byte-identical to today; hard_requirement failure aborts startup. Postcondition: ro/rw policy drives the ruleset with correct per-inode masks, witnessed live on CI (strace-anchored technique available).
prd_items.subject: Typed SandboxPolicy input + Landlock ro/rw upgrade with per-inode tailoring and loud degradation

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (policy report, ranked item 6): document and exploit that a second landlock_restrict_self can only NARROW -- policy updates that reduce fs access apply at runtime without restart; widening is declared out of scope for Landlock and routed to broker fd-delegation (WASI preopens, broker-wasi-capability-redesign territory). Precondition: litebox-policy-as-data. Invariant: stacked rulesets are monotonically non-increasing in access. Postcondition: a runtime policy update shrinking fs access takes effect on the running runner, witnessed live; a widening update is rejected with a pointer to fd-delegation.
prd_items.subject: Runtime fs tightening via additive Landlock restrict_self stacking; widening routed to broker fd-delegation

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (policy report, ranked item 5; source mechanistic_mapper.rs:59-170): port the zero-LLM mapper shape -- group denials by (dest, subject), emit minimal candidate grants with confidence scores and advisor_proposed provenance, skip always-blocked targets (loopback/link-local/metadata equivalents) to avoid proposal loops, never propose SSRF-equivalent escapes in step one; human approval ONLY (auto-approval, if ever, requires the prover row and stays off by default); merged grants flow through litebox-capability-generation-reload. Precondition: litebox-shim-denial-tap + litebox-capability-provenance-review-tokens. Invariant: every proposal is auditable to the exact denial records that produced it. Postcondition: a guest generating repeated denials yields a deduped, correctly-scoped proposal visible on the host, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Deterministic denial->proposal mapper + manual approval flow feeding the capability store

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (control-plane report, ranked item 1): the direct answer to the SNP vsock boot-channel problem -- the design constraint is identical (host/network untrusted, cannot dial in; guest dials out; one connection carries everything). Transferable topology: (a) one guest-initiated ordered byte stream; (b) a long-lived control stream carrying hello/heartbeat/RelayOpen{channel_id,target}/RelayClose; (c) data streams the guest dials inward then CLAIMS by echoing the channel id (RelayInit first frame). Transport-agnostic: TCP/TLS via VMM net stack or a paravirt console; yamux-style framing acceptable if HTTP/2 is too heavy -- the control/claim protocol is the IP, not HTTP/2. Two SNP adaptations OpenShell doesn't have: bootstrap credential must be BOUND TO ATTESTATION EVIDENCE (key release gated on measurement, or mTLS with attestation-derived keys) since the provisioning path is hostile; pinned CA only -- copy OpenShell's deliberate refusal of native root CAs (grpc_client.rs:181-185). Precondition: none. Invariant: zero inbound connectivity required; all streams guest-initiated. Postcondition: a control session + claimed data relay established from inside an SNP guest over the available transport, witnessed live. Unblocks litebox-remote-attach and litebox-config-lkg for SNP.
prd_items.subject: Outbound-only multiplexed control+data channel from the guest (SNP boot channel)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (policy report, ranked item 4; sources sandbox.proto:167-170 advisor_proposed, architecture/security-policy.md:235-240 review_token): input to the WASI-capability broker redesign. Two cheap idioms that prevent the entire stale-approval bug class: (a) per-object provenance bits (advisor_proposed-style) that NEVER independently satisfy trust -- a proposed grant requires explicit approval to become effective; (b) content-hash review tokens binding a proposed grant to the exact live inputs it was validated against, recomputed at approval -- a changed token forces fresh review. Precondition: broker capability model shape (broker-wasi-capability-redesign). Invariant: no code path treats a proposed grant as granted. Postcondition: mutating any decision input invalidates the token and blocks approval, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Provenance bits + content-hash review tokens in the broker capability model

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. DEFERRED until capability reload + denial-to-proposal exist. From OpenShell study (policy report, ranked item 7; source openshell-prover, queries.rs): two starter queries over the litebox capability graph -- (a) which guest-reachable broker objects can read which host paths (analog of credential_reach_expansion), (b) did this change add a write capability on existing reach (analog of capability_expansion); categorical findings, finding-delta gate against the current-policy baseline, auto-approval only when setting=auto AND empty delta AND empty security notes, default off. Open unknown to read first if adopted: finding_delta implementation in openshell-server/src/grpc/policy.rs (located, not read line-by-line; the suppression rule for capability_expansion tuples already in the reach delta needs a precise reading). Precondition: litebox-capability-generation-reload + litebox-denial-to-proposal. Invariant: a prover failure blocks auto-approval, never manual approval. Postcondition: a capability change introducing new host-path reach is flagged by the prover delta, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Z3 finding categories over the litebox capability graph, gated auto-approval, off by default (deferred)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (control-plane report ranked item 4 + process-supervision report ranked item 6, merged): guest-side PTY server (russh-on-socket or a raw PTY bridge) + RelayOpen/RelayInit claim flow over litebox-snp-boot-channel (or local broker channel); access gated by socket fs permissions with no app-level preface; loopback-only TCP targets; the abstract-socket trick so sandboxed code cannot unlink the relay target; SO_PEERCRED-equivalent scoping of which in-guest principal may open the socket. SSH protocol compatibility itself is OPTIONAL and deferred unless VS Code Remote-SSH interop becomes a goal -- then reuse OpenShell's pipe-vs-PTY lessons verbatim (ssh.rs:546-559). Composes with litebox-session-multiplexer and litebox-shim-pty-slave. Precondition: litebox-snp-boot-channel (for SNP) or broker control channel (local). Invariant: attach never grants capabilities beyond the guest's own policy; read-only observers never hold the stdin lease. Postcondition: attach to a running guest, run a command, detach, re-attach with replay -- witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Guest PTY server + reverse-relay remote attach/exec (absorbs SSH-attach-compat)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (control-plane report, ranked items 2-3; sources persistence/mod.rs put_if/update_message_cas, compute/mod.rs recover_failed_lifecycle/main_process_exited, run.rs report_main_process_exit_until_ack): adopt the minimal core, SKIP the fleet machinery (lease/reconciler/HA are overkill for a local broker). (a) Persist desired state per runner (start/stop intent) BEFORE calling the backend, in a tiny CAS store (id, type, payload, resource_version) -- broker crash recovery becomes deterministic; (b) idempotent backend ops + recover ambiguous outcomes by OBSERVATION, never assumption: probe the backend, fence the write on the exact pre-op version, never retry a CAS conflict owned by a newer writer; (c) instance-ID fencing on exit reports so a restarted runner's stale exit can't clobber the new instance; (d) runner/guest reports exit to broker with until-ack retry (infinite backoff), broker persists before acking; (e) readiness = live control session, strictly better than process-alive checks. Precondition: none. Invariant: every state transition is durable before its backend call; conflicting duplicate exit codes are rejected. Postcondition: broker killed mid-transition recovers to the correct state by observation, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Broker persisted-intent CAS store + recover-by-observation + instance-ID-fenced exit reporting

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (control-plane report, ranked item 6; source proto/compute_driver.proto, 373 lines): the contract points to transfer for litebox's backends (macOS HV, Linux userland, LVBS, SNP, Windows userland): driver-private types with broker-side translation; additive capability fields with ignore-unknown (forward-compat by construction); an explicit broker_manages_lifecycle bit deciding crash/shutdown sweeps; idempotent Stop/Start that RETAIN persistent state; DeleteSandbox -> bool deleted distinguishing 'already absent'; a Watch stream so the broker reconciles from backend events instead of polling; GetCapabilities/GetGatewayListenerRequirements/ValidateSandboxCreate up front. Precondition: none. Invariant: unknown capability fields are ignored, never errors; stop/start are safe to call redundantly. Postcondition: the backend trait expresses all five current backends with the capability snapshot, witnessed by compiling + driving each through the uniform call path.
prd_items.subject: Formalize litebox's backend abstraction in the compute_driver.proto shape

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (control-plane report, ranked item 7; sources openshell-ocsf crate, log_push.rs): adopt the schema and discipline, not necessarily the stack -- (a) a fixed event schema (OCSF classes or a litebox-minimal subset) for mediation decisions: fs/net deny, exec, boot/attestation transitions, so litebox events are SIEM-consumable; (b) cheap emit: thread-local event + tracing target + dual human/JSON projections; (c) egress discipline for a constrained channel: bounded queue, batch, DROP when full -- logging must never block the guest; reconnect backoff; permanent disable on auth failure. Precondition: none (local logging first; litebox-snp-boot-channel for remote egress). Invariant: observability overhead on the guest hot path is bounded and droppable. Postcondition: mediation decisions emit schema-conformant events through both projections, and a full queue drops rather than stalls the guest, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: OCSF-shaped mediation event schema + bounded best-effort egress discipline

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (control-plane report, ranked item 5; sources sandbox.proto:362-397, openshell-sandbox poll loop lib.rs:3541-4123): a single config_revision fingerprint over ALL effective inputs; poll or push delivery; fail-closed DEFAULT (forced when no last-valid exists), retain_last_valid opt-in; FIFO decoupled status ack so a delayed older ack can never regress the host's view and failures never delay enforcement; failure-emission dedup by (revision, hash, failure-class) so a bad config doesn't spam; re-apply posture changes against the REJECTED revision without accepting any of its bytes; LKG credentials/state retained until the swap succeeds. For SNP this doubles as 'how to rotate policy into a CVM I can't reach'. Precondition: litebox-policy-as-data (the config object); litebox-snp-boot-channel for the SNP path. Invariant: unknown/empty failure-mode values parse as fail_closed; a rejected candidate never displaces last-known-good. Postcondition: a bad config pushed to a running guest triggers quarantine-or-retain per mode with exactly one deduped failure event, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Revisioned config delivery with last-known-good + ordered status ack

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. From OpenShell study (agent-skills report, proposal 5.1, highest value): litebox has the multi-surface drift problem (global CLAUDE.md, memory/MEMORY.md + per-topic memory files, .claude/skills, gm PRD rows, CI workflow docs). Port the OpenShell shape: no generator -- a drift-check skill with a tracking table (memory index vs topic files; .claude/skills vs CLAUDE.md mentions; .gm PRD rows vs memory topics; workflows vs CI docs), a maintenance map (change area -> surfaces to review), structured drift report (ADDED/REMOVED/STALE), fix-and-reverify; embedded as a pre-record obligation in the gm flow rather than CI. Skeleton in the report. Precondition: none. Invariant: canonical sources are the directories themselves (ls .claude/skills, memory/*.md), never the index files. Postcondition: the skill detects a planted drift (e.g. a memory topic missing from MEMORY.md) when run, witnessed live.

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. Hard rule: a syscall is 'supported' only when verified live on every backend, or explicitly recorded as backend-gated. Skeleton in the report. Precondition: skill-guest-test-binary. Invariant: the ledger never marks DONE without a live run. Postcondition: the skill exists and its ledger matches the memory files' current state, verified by running it against one known-good and one known-open entry.
prd_items.subject: Adopt node-syscall-coverage skill: failing guest op -> syscall -> interposition site -> live verify -> ledger

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. prd_items.description: Route family: representation. The 'something vulkan based' reading delivered with ZERO new device surface: Mesa lavapipe is a conformant pure-CPU Vulkan driver and llvmpipe the GL equivalent; their OS surface is only anonymous+exec mmap (LLVM JIT), clone threads + futexes, memfd/shm, CPUID/HWCAP -- surface litebox largely already implements (memfd at litebox_broker_transport_linux_userland/src/memfd.rs, JIT pages precedent for V8). Work: guest rootfs recipe packaging Mesa llvmpipe+lavapipe; close syscall gaps surfaced live (expected candidates: memfd_create edge cases, mprotect exec transitions, sched_getaffinity, getrandom); verify with glxgears and vkcube witnessed live, displaying via the fb path. AARCH64-MACOS FIX REQUIRED AND IDENTIFIED (mutable litebox-mesa-jit-x18 resolved): LLVM auto-reserves x18 for Darwin triples, but gallivm's Apple-triple branch in lp_bld_misc.cpp is #if DETECT_OS_APPLE-gated with no #else, unreachable for a Mesa binary compiled as a LINUX guest -- it falls back to the guest's own compile-time Linux LLVM_HOST_TRIPLE, so x18 is NOT reserved and JIT shader code can clobber it on the macOS-arm64 host. Fix: patch lp_build_create_jit_compiler_for_module() in lp_bld_misc.cpp to push('+reserve-x18') into MAttrs when DETECT_ARCH_AARCH64 (same mechanism as -ffixed-x18 on Linux; safe on real Linux/Android too, costs one scratch GPR). Do not shortcut via forcing an apple-darwin triple (pulls in unrelated ABI assumptions). This patch must land in the guest's vendored/built Mesa before x86_64-only support can be widened to aarch64-macOS hosts. Precondition: litebox-fbdev-device + litebox-fbdev-ioctls (display target). Invariant: no guest GPU/device emulation added; support claims are per-backend and live-verified only; the reserve-x18 patch ships with the guest Mesa build, not as a litebox-side workaround. Postcondition: vkcube + glxgears run under the runner on BOTH x86_64 and aarch64-macOS hosts, witnessed live, with the patch verified to prevent x18 corruption and per-backend support matrix recorded.
prd_items.subject: Guest Mesa software rendering: llvmpipe (GL) + lavapipe (Vulkan) rootfs recipe, syscall gaps closed live

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. Contract verified consumer-by-consumer from source (x11vnc linuxfb.c, Qt qlinuxfbscreen.cpp, xf86-video-fbdev + fbdevhw.c, DirectFB2). Exact uapi linux/fb.h structs. Mandatory: FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO (0x4600); FBIOGET_FSCREENINFO (0x4602) with id="litebox", smem_start=0, smem_len=yres_virtual*line_length, type=FB_TYPE_PACKED_PIXELS, visual=FB_VISUAL_TRUECOLOR, line_length=xres_virtual*bpp/8, xpanstep=ypanstep=1, accel=FB_ACCEL_NONE, mmio_len=0; FBIOPUT_VSCREENINFO (0x4601) with CLAMP-AND-ECHO semantics (Xorg warns on silent divergence; this is also the dynamic-resize channel) and backing-store realloc on geometry change; FBIOPAN_DISPLAY (0x4606) recording xoffset/yoffset, visible region = base + yoffset*line_length + xoffset*bpp/8 (yres_virtual=2*yres gives tear-free flips); FBIOBLANK (0x4611) success-no-op. FBIOGETCMAP/FBIOPUTCMAP accept+no-op (truecolor only); everything else ENOTTY. Default mode disclosed: 32bpp XRGB8888 red{16,8} green{8,8} blue{0,8} transp{24,8} -- one format end-to-end (Qt ARGB32, softbuffer u32), zero conversion. Mechanics: constant + IoctlArg variant in litebox_common_linux/src/lib.rs (variants at 927-952, decode at 3154-3175), match arm in sys_ioctl (file.rs:2675-2869) gated on fb fd kind via a major-29 recognizer paralleling is_stdio (file.rs:2662-2673). Precondition: litebox-fbdev-device. Invariant: ioctls on non-fb fds keep current behavior exactly; structs are layout-exact with uapi. Postcondition: x11vnc -rawfb /dev/fb0 launches and derives correct WxHxBPP:masks from FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: fbdev ioctl core set: FBIOGET/FBIOPUT_VSCREENINFO, FBIOGET_FSCREENINFO, FBIOPAN_DISPLAY, FBIOBLANK

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. Optional local presentation path alongside the RFB server, same fb backing store. softbuffer (rust-windowing org) is the correct default -- CPU shared-memory buffer to the OS compositor, tier-1 on macOS AppKit/Wayland/Win32/X11, no GPU dependency (rustdesk's own choice; wgpu is strictly heavier for plain framebuffer presentation and adds a hard GPU-driver dependency to the runner). winit supplies window + local input events, which feed the same evdev injection path as RFB input (litebox-fb-evdev-input). XRGB8888 u32 pixels match the fb format end-to-end, zero conversion. Precondition: litebox-fbdev-device + litebox-fbdev-ioctls. Invariant: the preview window is an observer; closing it never affects the guest. Postcondition: a native window on the macOS dev host live-displays guest-painted fb content, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: Native host preview window for the guest framebuffer via softbuffer+winit (optional sibling of RFB)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. DEFERRED -- build only when there is more than one guest framebuffer to composite, or GPU scaling/HDR/post-processing becomes a measured requirement. wgpu's legitimate niche in litebox is host-side composition: per-guest texture upload + shader compositing, headless-capable (compatible_surface optional on native backends, render-to-texture + copy_texture_to_buffer + map_async readback per docs.rs/wgpu). Explicitly NOT for: the VNC path (RFB wants CPU pixels -- why no maintained stack combines wgpu with an RFB server) and never inside the guest (wgpu is a client API, not a driver). Also explicitly NOT: adopting or writing a Vulkan/GLES-execution-engine-on-wgpu (gfx-portability was an unmaintained prototype; no active project exists -- vaporware to adopt, research-grade to write; Mesa's in-tree KosmicKrisp Vulkan-on-Metal undercuts the portability motive). Precondition: litebox-fb-host-window + a measured multi-fb or post-processing requirement. Invariant: softbuffer stays the default presenter; wgpu is additive. Postcondition: compositing of >=2 guest framebuffers in one window at interactive rates, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: DEFERRED: wgpu GPU compositor for multi-guest framebuffers / accelerated scaling (only if presentation needs outgrow softbuffer)

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. DEFERRED -- build only if measured lavapipe performance is insufficient for target workloads (litebox-guest-mesa-software lands first and provides the measurement). The only forwarding architecture feasible without a guest kernel driver model: a custom guest Vulkan ICD (pure userspace .so the Vulkan loader dlopens per its JSON manifest) serializing Vulkan gfxstream-style over the litebox BROKER CHANNEL (LocalCallChannel BrokerRequest/BrokerResponse over unix socket + notification ring -- litebox_broker_transport/src/channel.rs, litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/broker.rs) to a host renderer process linked against host Vulkan (ash) or rutabaga-style; memfd-backed shared memory for bulk buffers. Structurally gfxstream/rutabaga with the broker in place of virtio-gpu. EXPLICIT NON-GOALS (never build, reason recorded): full Venus (requires guest kernel virtio-gpu driver >=5.16 + KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION), a /dev/dxg clone (WSLg's dxgkrnl is a guest kernel driver over VMBus), any virtio-gpu device model -- all assume a guest kernel + hypervisor litebox userland modes don't have. Precondition: measured lavapipe insufficiency + a broker-channel latency measurement against Vulkan command-submission rates (shared-ring fast path if round-trip latency is too high). Invariant: forwarding is per-guest opt-in; the software-Mesa path remains the default. Postcondition: a guest Vulkan application running on host-GPU-accelerated Vulkan via the ICD, witnessed live.
prd_items.subject: DEFERRED: gfxstream-shape guest Vulkan ICD forwarding over the broker channel to a host renderer

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. Documentation row so these questions never get re-litigated. Record in docs/roadmap.md: (1) the graphics v1 architecture -- /dev/fb0 emulation + runner-side RFB (propolis-shape), input via evdev emulation, software Mesa for GL/Vulkan in-guest; (2) WAYLAND: no mainstream compositor runs on fbdev (wlroots and Weston >=4.0 have no fbdev backend; SDL has none either) -- the in-guest Wayland path is wlroots-headless+pixman+wayvnc (heavy in-guest stack) or weston headless/vnc backends; DRM/KMS emulation (dumb buffers + modeset + GBM + dma-buf + evdev + seats) is a much larger surface, deferred until a Wayland-compositor requirement actually exists; (3) NON-GOALS with reasons: Venus/virtio-gpu, /dev/dxg-style kernel forwarding, Vulkan-on-wgpu execution engine (no guest kernel/driver model in userland modes; no active wgpu-driver project exists); (4) precedent note: no syscall-interposition sandbox (gVisor, WSL1, UML) has any guest framebuffer -- litebox is ahead of its direct peers here; (5) pointer to the deferred litebox-vulkan-icd-forwarding row as the sanctioned GPU-acceleration shape. Precondition: none. Invariant: docs record decisions with reasons, not aspirations. Postcondition: roadmap.md updated and committed; a reader can derive why fbdev-first, why not Venus, why not wgpu-in-guest.
prd_items.subject: Record graphics-stack decisions in docs/roadmap.md: Wayland path, DRM deferral, Venus/dxg/wgpu-engine non-goals

prd_items.description: Route family: representation. The end-to-end proof of the VNC-desktop goal, per live-verify discipline (no test files).
