prd_items.description: Precondition: the exact pinned guest reaches successful org.xfce.Xfconf name acquisition, then dbus-daemon stops servicing GetNameOwner and new ListNames calls; direct foreground xfconfd makes the same query succeed. Upstream D-Bus activation uses a babysitter process and, when releasing it, closes its channel, attempts waitpid(WNOHANG), sends SIGKILL if still live, then performs blocking waitpid. The current LiteBox sys_kill returns ESRCH for every positive remote PID even while kill(pid,0) proves that process is live; a real guest probe observed kill_rc=1 and alive_rc=0. Invariant: kill to one positive live guest PID resolves through ProcessTable, queues the user-originated Siginfo only in that target process shared pending queue, drops the process-table lock before acquiring target locks, interrupts every current target thread so unmaskable SIGKILL cannot remain behind an interruptible wait, and never reads target-owned Cell/RefCell state from the sender; self delivery, signal-zero liveness checks, process isolation, signal masks, pending limits, fork/exec state, tkill/tgkill behavior, and x18 policy remain unchanged. Postcondition: a fixed-x18 packaged fork child blocked in a wait is killed remotely, wait4 reports WTERMSIG(SIGKILL) exactly once, replay against the reaped PID returns ESRCH, D-Bus-activated xfconfd no longer wedges the bus, exact xfconf-query returns zero, ListNames remains responsive, and start-desktop proceeds toward DESKTOP UP. Writable artifacts are litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/process.rs and syscalls/signal/mod.rs plus adjacent inline regressions and the required workflow lesson.
prd_items.subject: Deliver process-directed signals so D-Bus activation can reap its babysitter
prd_items.witness_evidence: Actual release-runner probes: activation path acquired org.xfce.Xfconf then GetNameOwner timed out and a concurrent ListNames never replied; direct /usr/lib/xfce4/xfconf/xfconfd stayed foreground and the same query completed XFCONF_STATUS=0 through Hello, RequestName, GetNameOwner, Properties.GetAll, GetAllProperties, GetProperty and SetProperty. A separate actual guest child probe printed REMOTE_KILL child=1001 kill_rc=1 alive_rc=0 and No such process. Current signal/mod.rs:682-708 explicitly accepts remote kill(pid,0) but returns ESRCH for every remote nonzero signal. Official D-Bus dbus-spawn-unix.c documents the activation babysitter cleanup close, WNOHANG probe, SIGKILL and blocking waitpid sequence.

prd_items.description: Precondition: the actual packaged guest trace shows a successful AF_UNIX stream connect, the D-Bus client sends the NUL plus `AUTH EXTERNAL 30`, and dbus-daemon on the accepted endpoint calls getsockopt(SOL_SOCKET, SO_PEERCRED=17), receives EOPNOTSUPP from UnixSocket::getsockopt, replies `REJECTED EXTERNAL`, and closes; the inotify ENOSYS warning is incidental to this proven authentication failure. Invariant: connected AF_UNIX stream endpoints retain the peer process credential snapshot established by connect or socketpair and SO_PEERCRED returns the Linux `struct ucred` peer pid/effective uid/effective gid, never the current querying task or host credentials; listener/unconnected behavior, short-buffer copy semantics, descriptor ownership, process isolation, and existing Unix stream data/poll behavior remain intact. Postcondition: focused live Linux-ABI probes witness reciprocal peer pid/uid/gid on connect/accept and socketpair plus sentinel behavior before connection, the real packaged guest passes org.freedesktop.DBus.ListNames without weakening EXTERNAL authentication, and the supervised desktop reaches DESKTOP UP.
prd_items.subject: Preserve AF_UNIX peer credentials for D-Bus authentication

prd_items.description: Precondition: the pinned archive reaches musl __unmapself; SYS_munmap succeeds, then the rewritten SYS_exit gate faults exactly at its first STR X16,[SP] because the valid native sequence intentionally removed the current stack. Invariant: the normal writable-stack gate stays the zero-signal fast path; on a lower-EL write Data Abort at the exact six-word SVC-gate signature, the macOS handler copies the 24-byte candidate through bounded mach_vm_read_overwrite, validates the complete pattern, decodes the ADRP/ADD continuation, captures all GPR/NZCV/FPSIMD state from kernel mcontext, restores pre-gate SP, fills orig_x0/syscallno, clears per-thread ownership once, and redirects to a host-stack callback returning GuestExit::Syscall. Any unreadable, nonmatching, malformed, overflowed, partial, stale, or ordinary guest fault follows existing exception delivery unchanged. No guest x18/w18 is introduced, no process-global mutable scratch exists, concurrent threads remain disjoint, and ordinary syscalls retain direct callback performance. Writable artifacts are litebox_platform_macos_userland/src/darwin.rs, src/lib.rs and src/guest.rs, the adjacent arm64 rewriter contract documentation, inline regressions, and the workflow lesson mandated by BBCR. Postcondition: an exact gate-shaped guard-page witness preserves x16/SP/continuation and dispatches one syscall before its deliberate null fault; exact packaged xfconf-query returns zero; full platform suite passes; unchanged pinned archive remains zero-x18; launcher proceeds toward DESKTOP UP.
prd_items.subject: Recover valid syscalls from unwritable guest stacks

prd_items.description: The PROVE to EMIT gate is blocked by six unknown mutables that belong to future RES: exception-model, partial-failure, three duplicated degradation rows, and the final crucible. They were added by competing spool consumers before the entry-SP STATE repair and cannot honestly receive final runtime witnesses before the code repair is emitted. The five new PROVE obligations are resolved. Preserve every future acceptance statement in the pending XFCE PRD, retire only the prematurely staged/duplicate mutable instances with explicit lifecycle evidence, and recreate uniquely named RES-v2 obligations when RES is reached; do not claim the XFConf or desktop witness has passed.
prd_items.subject: Recover premature RES obligations blocking EMIT

prd_items.description: Precondition: the fixed release runner passes the invalid-SP syscall regression and activates org.xfce.Xfconf, then a distinct guest process panics at mm.rs because a pre-patched ET_DYN map cannot derive its load base. Invariant: ElfPatchCache is owned by Process, keyed by that process local fd namespace; CLONE_THREAD shares it, fork receives a value clone matching its inherited mappings/fds, exec clears only the caller process cache before mapping the replacement image, fd close removes only that process entry, and no lock is shared across unrelated processes. Existing PageManager mappings, callback patching, close ordering, and runtime rewriter behavior remain unchanged. Postcondition: concurrent/reused same-number fds in independent processes cannot collide; exact packaged XFConf produces no patch-cache panic and advances to a named next result. Writable artifacts are litebox_shim_linux/src/lib.rs, syscalls/process.rs, syscalls/mm.rs, adjacent inline regressions, and current platform gate-recovery files already emitted for this same launcher witness.
prd_items.subject: Scope runtime ELF patch state to a guest process

prd_items.description: Route family: observability, then execution. Precondition: the preserved release-runner trace correlates MemfdCreate{name, flags:0} and EINVAL on the same pid=1294,tid=1294; 104 of 105 selected memfd calls succeed, later calls in that same process/thread succeed, and the Rust-generated backing pathname is an absolute /tmp/.litebox-memfd-<pid>-<attempt-id> string. Source and live namespace evidence exclude unlink and raw-fd publication, localizing the observed EINVAL to do_open while leaving the raw OpenError and filesystem layer unknown. Invariant: instrumentation is bounded and error-only; it records no guest-provided memfd name contents or secrets; each failing backing-open observation identifies pid, tid, attempt id, generated path, raw OpenError, and exact filesystem layer/stage; no backing descriptor is published until open and unlink both succeed; every failure closes anything acquired and leaves no /tmp/.litebox-memfd-* namespace entry; no blind EINVAL retry masks the cause. Postcondition: first, the actual fixed-x18 archive and release macOS runner produce a queryable raw-error witness without global syscall tracing or LLDB; second, the exact faulting layer is repaired at its source; third, live repeated and concurrent creation proves unique open-unlinked objects, read/write/lseek, ftruncate, file-backed mmap, CLOEXEC, invalid-flags and overlong-name errors, bounded collision handling, cleanup, and no leaked backing paths; fourth, unchecked cleanup panic paths are replaced by propagated errors; fifth, the real launcher reaches X UP and DESKTOP UP with xfce4-panel stable. Resource bound: at most 64 backing-name attempts per call; failure logging occurs only on the terminal backing-open error and is constant-size per failed syscall; diagnostics are removed or retained only as narrowly queryable structured error logging after attribution. Type shape: preserve raw OpenError until the observation boundary, then map exactly once to Errno; represent memfd creation stages explicitly enough that open, unlink, and publication failures cannot be conflated. Sealing is implemented only if live Glycin/XFCE use reaches F_ADD_SEALS/F_GET_SEALS, established by correlated execution evidence rather than assumption.
prd_items.subject: Identify and repair the transient memfd backing-open EINVAL blocking XFCE panel startup

prd_items.description: Precondition: prctl option PR_GET_DUMPABLE is called with all four unused argument slots zero. Invariant: the raw ABI decoder constructs a typed PrctlArg and rejects malformed unused arguments with EINVAL; the handler exposes LiteBox's ordinary non-privileged process model without adding speculative PR_SET_DUMPABLE state; temporary catch-all decoder logging is removed after the typed path exists. Postcondition: the actual fixed-x18 XFCE archive under the release macOS runner no longer reports decoder-level EINVAL for syscall 167 option 3 and advances the Glycin/Bubblewrap fallback toward X UP and DESKTOP UP. Writable artifacts: litebox_common_linux/src/lib.rs, litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/process.rs, litebox_shim_linux/src/lib.rs.
prd_items.subject: Implement PR_GET_DUMPABLE for Glycin's Bubblewrap probe

prd_items.description: The PROVE-to-EMIT gate rejects because 11 pending rows are STATE-kind memfd lifecycle obligations whose required witnesses can only exist after EMIT builds the runner and STATE runs the real launcher. Five new PR_GET_DUMPABLE PROVE obligations were added and resolved in dependency order with typed source and live red-trace evidence, but the unchanged later-phase rows still trigger mutables-all-resolved. Six identical denials are now recorded. BBCR checkpoint: preserve the fully specified PR_GET_DUMPABLE path, do not falsely resolve future-phase lifecycle witnesses, and recover through the earliest legal phase without another bare transition retry.
prd_items.subject: Recover PROVE to EMIT from later-phase mutable gate conflict

prd_items.description: Precondition: the release runner and fixed-x18 XFCE archive reproduce the panel failure while all four PR_GET_DUMPABLE calls return 1. Invariant: diagnosis correlates raw syscall arguments by (pid, tid), preserves the fixed-x18 archive and signing boundary, and removes temporary observability before acceptance. Postcondition: the real panel reaches Bubblewrap's recognized namespace-denial fallback instead of surfacing EINVAL, and start-desktop.sh emits DESKTOP UP.
prd_items.subject: Identify and fix the post-PR_GET_DUMPABLE Bubblewrap spawn EINVAL

prd_items.description: Route family: state, then execution. Supplementary groups are implemented and live-proven: xterm executes setgroups(size=12), setuid, and execve(/bin/sh). The remaining defect is narrower and source-proven. Precondition: the unchanged fixed-x18 /tmp/litebox-xfce-64.tar reaches a managed xterm whose child has called setsid and setpgid(0,0), then successfully calls TIOCSCTTY on its PTY slave. Invariant: terminal foreground ownership stays in the existing shared per-PTY PtyState.foreground_pgid; master, slave, duplicates, and /dev/tty views of one PTY observe the same atomic; TIOCGPGRP/TIOCSPGRP remain unchanged; failed controlling-terminal acquisition does not mutate foreground_pgid. Postcondition: after successful TIOCSCTTY, foreground_pgid is atomically set to the caller current shim process-group ID, matching Linux __proc_set_tty; /bin/sh no longer loops comparing TIOCGPGRP with getpgrp; affected checks and the real runner pass. The release runner is signed only with /tmp/litebox-jit-entitlements.plist; browser pointer focuses xterm, browser keyboard produces visible command output, and a real browser wheel event visibly changes generated scrollback. Final acceptance re-runs decoded x18/w18, forbidden-package, signing-material-boundary, entitlement, artifact-hash, and process audits without exporting private signing material. Sole new repair artifact: litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/file.rs; the already-modified supplementary-group artifacts remain in the acceptance diff.
prd_items.subject: Complete xterm shell job control and browser input acceptance

prd_items.description: Precondition: the required release runner reaches DESKTOP UP and its viewer keyboard path visibly edits Thunar, while the managed xterm has focus but neither echoes nor executes input after the earlier TIOCSCTTY foreground publication repair. Source shows every guest process still shares GlobalState::pgid; any later desktop process setpgid/setsid can therefore change xterm child getpgrp without changing its per-PTY foreground_pgid, recreating the shell job-control mismatch. Invariant: process-group identity belongs to Process, is inherited on fork, shared only by threads, changed by setsid/setpgid only for the named live self/child process, and read by getpgid/TIOCSCTTY from that process; per-PTY foreground ownership, session identity, process-table lock ordering, signal state, and wait behavior remain unchanged. Postcondition: a deterministic cross-process regression proves one process changing group cannot alter another process getpgrp or its PTY foreground match; the exact fixed-x18 XFCE archive under the signed release runner visibly executes a browser-entered command and scrolls terminal output with a browser wheel event. Writable repair artifacts: litebox_shim_linux/src/lib.rs, litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/process.rs, litebox_shim_linux/src/syscalls/file.rs, adjacent inline regressions, and the required workflow lesson.
prd_items.subject: Scope process-group identity to each guest process

prd_items.description: Precondition: the required 1024x768 viewer sends one 3,145,732-byte binary WebSocket message and GM-owned real Chrome loses its CDP result envelope exactly when that message arrives, while the same host listener returns ordinary HTTP responses normally. Invariant: one logical framebuffer update remains one RFC 6455 binary message with the existing four-byte dimensions plus RGBA payload; transport frames are bounded, first frame uses opcode 2, continuation frames use opcode 0, only the final frame sets FIN, writes preserve order, and viewer.html remains unchanged. Postcondition: litebox_rfb/src/web.rs emits bounded fragments, the unchanged embedded viewer receives the reassembled logical message, a fresh GM-owned real browser loads http://127.0.0.1:6080, captures the complete 1024x768 desktop, and visibly proves keyboard command output plus wheel-changed terminal scrollback.
prd_items.subject: Fragment full-frame WebSocket transport for real-browser observability

prd_items.description: Precondition: /tmp/litebox-xfce-64.tar has root /bin/sh in /etc/passwd and start-desktop.sh exports SHELL=/bin/sh, but the required live runner records `xterm: No absolute path found for shell: xterm` and no usable terminal remains. Invariant: the launcher names /bin/sh explicitly through xterm -e, keeps the existing 80x24 geometry/title/log boundary, adds no package, preserves fixed-x18 and forbidden-package constraints, and never relies on host environment or passwd fallback. Postcondition: the rebuilt immutable tar starts a managed xterm whose /bin/sh remains alive, a fresh real browser captures it, browser keyboard executes a visible identifying command, and browser wheel changes visible generated scrollback.
prd_items.subject: Launch the managed xterm with an explicit guest shell

prd_items.description: Precondition: the WebSocket transport and explicit xterm shell repairs are emitted, the immutable tar and signed release runner are rebuilt, and browser keyboard plus wheel acceptance has passed once. Invariant: no lifecycle correction is treated as runtime evidence; RES recreates uniquely named exception-model, partial-failure, degradation, and crucible mutables covering TIOCSCTTY EINVAL/EPERM/EFAULT before mutation, runner termination and listener cleanup, immutable-tar restart, bounded dual-PTY contention, malformed authority/pointer inputs, and absence of stale foreground values, child leaks, hangs, or runner failures. Postcondition: every recreated RES mutable is resolved only by same-turn live evidence, the restarted real browser again shows the terminal, and Task 4/16 remain incomplete until that evidence plus final artifact/security/process audits passes.
prd_items.subject: Rehydrate and discharge PTY resilience obligations after source repair

prd_items.description: All bytes written server-to-client on one WebSocket connection must cross one bounded serialization boundary: a complete fragmented framebuffer message is indivisible relative to pong/control output, no concurrent TcpStream clone may interleave bytes between a frame header and payload or between continuation fragments, and write failures must terminate the owning path without queue growth. Live loopback tests must force concurrent framebuffer and ping/pong traffic, parse the full RFC 6455 stream, and prove exact logical reassembly plus a valid pong before the rebuilt real-browser witness.
prd_items.subject: Serialize every WebSocket server write

prd_items.description: Precondition: shared/standalone spool consumers can claim the same request and the caller receives the losing replay result. Invariant: exactly one claimant may execute each request id; every duplicate observer returns the successful durable result, while stateful callers retain idempotent preconditions and inspect post-state before retry. New witness: exec_js dispatch 1787936957450-500-d3847f77d002e92e extracted fifteen exact Git blobs into a unique /tmp tree; one claimant completed all files, a duplicate claimant replayed from the first file and returned EEXIST as the envelope result. Read-only dispatch 1787936988664-500-95d70ac57a786339 proved all fifteen durable outputs exist and match their expected blob hashes. Postcondition: concurrent consumers execute each request once and return the winning result under transition, process, archive-swap, and file-materialization workloads.
prd_items.subject: Prevent duplicate spool consumers from replaying stateful requests

prd_items.description: The XFCE desktop VNC-web viewer (--vnc-web flag, litebox_rfb framebuffer/websocket server) only exists in litebox_runner_linux_on_macos_userland/src/lib.rs. litebox_runner_linux_userland (the native-Linux, no-macOS-userland-emulation runner) has no --vnc-web flag and cannot serve the desktop framebuffer at all. On real x86_64/aarch64 Linux hosts there is no XNU/x18 corruption (that bug is specific to Apple's kernel clearing the AArch64 x18 register on EL0 return, per docs/roadmap.md), so the litebox_packager/examples/xfce recipe's unconditional call to build-x18-desktop-repo.sh is unneeded work on that host and produces x18-fixed binaries that make no sense outside the macOS/AArch64 guest scenario -- on x86 there is no x18 register at all. Two obligations: (1) add a native-Linux desktop recipe path that skips the x18 rebuild and uses stock Alpine XFCE packages directly; (2) port/share the --vnc-web + litebox_rfb wiring into litebox_runner_linux_userland so the same viewer.html/websocket flow works when litebox runs natively on Linux, not just under macOS userland emulation.
prd_items.subject: Wire --vnc-web into litebox_runner_linux_userland for native x86/arm64 Linux hosts

prd_items.description: litebox_packager/scripts/build-x18-desktop-repo.sh sets RUSTFLAGS=-C target-feature=+reserve-x18 in /etc/abuild.conf and this DOES reach cargo builds for glycin/librsvg's own crate code, but the residual-x18 gate still fails: objdump shows 500+ w18/x18 references in glycin-svg/glycin-heif/glycin-image-rs/glycin-jxl/glycin-thumbnailer, concentrated in code patterns matching Rust's own UTF-8 validation / char decoding state machine (ldrb w18 jump-table dispatch near std-like symbols). Root cause: Alpine's rust/cargo package (main/rust APKBUILD, pkgver 1.96.1) ships a PREBUILT libstd/libcore sysroot that was never compiled with +reserve-x18 -- RUSTFLAGS only affects the crate being built, not the already-compiled std it links against, so every Rust binary in the closure links a stock x18-using std regardless of the crate's own RUSTFLAGS. docs/roadmap.md line ~891 already documents the intent ('Cargo code (Glycin/libglycin/librsvg...) uses +reserve-x18') but the sysroot itself needs the same treatment for the gate to actually pass. Fix requires rebuilding rustc/cargo from source (rustc-$pkgver-src.tar.xz, a multi-hour multi-stage bootstrap) with RUSTFLAGS/target-feature threaded through the std build, or using -Z build-std with a nightly toolchain to recompile std per-crate. Out of scope for a single session; verified live against the actual build container (glycin rebuilt with explicit RUSTFLAGS at the abuild invocation, residual count unchanged at 554 hits in glycin-svg alone).
prd_items.subject: Rebuild Alpine's rust/cargo package with +reserve-x18 so Rust binaries in the desktop closure are truly x18-clean

prd_items.description: The final residual-x18 verification loop (build-x18-desktop-repo.sh ~line 356-379) iterates every */aarch64/*.apk in the local REPODEST and fails the whole build if any contains x18/w18 operands. Rebuilding the gcc origin also produces gcc-gnat, gcc-go, gcc-gdc and their runtime libs (libgnat, libgo, libgphobos, libgccjit) as side-artifacts of the multi-language GCC bootstrap; these are never installed into the XFCE desktop image (verified: grep across build-xfce-image.sh/Containerfile/DEFAULT_PACKAGES finds no reference to gnat/go/gdc/gccjit). Live-measured 41,270 total residual x18/w18 references across the full local repo, the overwhelming majority (>39,000) inside these unshipped GNAT/Go/D compiler packages plus flock/libblkid/util-linux-misc (also not in DEFAULT_PACKAGES). The gate should scan only packages actually referenced by the image build (DEFAULT_PACKAGES-derived closure, or whatever the final image manifest installs), not every apk abuild happened to produce as a side effect of a multi-language compiler bootstrap. Real remaining residual work after excluding unshipped packages: mtdev (21 refs, IS in DEFAULT_PACKAGES, genuine gap), plus the glycin/librsvg family (see xfce-x18-rust-sysroot-residual for that root cause).
prd_items.subject: x18 residual-scan gate in build-x18-desktop-repo.sh checks every built apk, not just the desktop's install closure

prd_items.description: build-x18-desktop-repo.sh's DEFAULT_PACKAGES comment claims to be 'the conservative loaded closure of the XFCE image' but Containerfile installs the xfce4 metapackage directly (not the individually-curated component list), which transitively pulls in a much larger dependency tree than DEFAULT_PACKAGES covers. Live-measured against the actual built image (after fixing the residual-scan gate to run there instead of the raw repo, see commit a223669): 348 total installed packages vs DEFAULT_PACKAGES's ~80 origins. The now-correctly-scoped gate (scanning the real built image) found 211,720 residual x18/w18 references across genuinely-shipped stock (non-rebuilt) libraries: webkit2gtk (41MB, 9779 refs), ffmpeg's codec stack (libx264 3340, libx265 17520, libvpx 6012, libswscale 7078, librav1e 3252, libtheora family ~4300 combined), libsqlite3, libssl3/libsmime3 (NSS), libzstd, libsodium, poppler, and many more -- none of these are x18-reserved because they were never in DEFAULT_PACKAGES's rebuild list. This is a pre-existing design gap (the DEFAULT_PACKAGES comment's claim was never actually verified against Containerfile's real install output until this session's gate fix made that check possible for the first time). Needs a design decision: either (a) expand DEFAULT_PACKAGES to cover the full 348-package closure (large compile-time cost, many packages -- ffmpeg codecs, webkit2gtk -- are heavy, multi-hour builds each), or (b) trim Containerfile's install list to only the curated minimal desktop (drop xfce4-panel plugins / thunar thumbnailers / whatever pulls in webkit2gtk and the media codec stack, if those features aren't actually needed for the terminal/VNC use case), or (c) accept the residual x18 in these specific paths as an out-of-scope corruption risk for now (matches the roadmap doc's own precedent of accepting partial coverage as 'each rebuilt object strictly shrinks the corruption surface') and gate only on the packages actually exercised by the live browser-witness crucible (Xorg, xfwm4, xfce4-terminal, xfdesktop, xfce4-panel core, not webkit2gtk/ffmpeg which nothing in the terminal/desktop smoke test touches).
prd_items.subject: DEFAULT_PACKAGES covers ~80 aports origins but the shipped xfce4 image installs 348 packages -- x18 rebuild misses ~270 of them

prd_items.description: Adding ncurses to DEFAULT_PACKAGES (needed: libncursesw.so.6 shows 27 residual x18 refs in the live smoke-test closure, loaded by vte3/xfce4-terminal) fails to fetch. Alpine's ncurses APKBUILD pins source=https://invisible-mirror.net/archives/ncurses/current/ncurses-6.6-20260516.tgz with a matching sha512sum checksum. That exact dated snapshot has aged out of invisible-mirror.net's current/ directory (only recent snapshots from 20260620 onward remain live as of 2026-08-28); the URL now 404s. mirrors.kernel.org has a generic ncurses-6.6.tar.gz release tarball but it is a DIFFERENT file (different tarball packaging than invisible-mirror's dated snapshot) so it fails the pinned checksum -- substituting it would mean building an unverified/unpinned source, not a like-for-like fix. This blocks x18-reserving ncurses via the normal abuild flow. Needs either: (a) find another mirror/cache still holding the exact 20260516 snapshot (web archive, another distro's source cache), (b) get Alpine upstream to update the aport to a currently-available snapshot and pull that newer aports revision, or (c) accept libncursesw as a remaining known-residual gap alongside the already-tracked glycin/librsvg Rust-sysroot issue (xfce-x18-rust-sysroot-residual). Not attempted: silently swapping in the unpinned mirrors.kernel.org tarball, since that bypasses Alpine's checksum verification for a security-relevant base library.
prd_items.subject: Alpine 3.24-stable's ncurses APKBUILD source snapshot no longer exists upstream

prd_items.description: After adding gnutls, gmp, and util-linux(already present) to DEFAULT_PACKAGES and rebuilding, the live smoke-test-closure residual gate (see xfce-x18-closure-underscoped, commit 6a0dd83) still shows: libgmp.so.10 (56 refs, traced into __gmp_primesieve region -- GMP ships hand-tuned per-arch assembly processed through an m4 macro assembler (mpn/m4-ccas, confirmed live: popcount.asm/hamdist.asm compile steps observed), which -ffixed-x18 (a compiler flag) cannot affect since it's literal asm text, not compiler-generated code -- same class of problem the script already patches for pixman's NEON asm, just not yet done for gmp's mpn/ arch-specific asm sources), libuuid.so.1 (146 refs) and libblkid.so.1 (27 refs) from util-linux (already in DEFAULT_PACKAGES's core/runtime plumbing line -- unclear why still residual; needs investigation of whether these specific subpackages get a different build() invocation, e.g. a separate cmake/meson pass that doesn't inherit CFLAGS the way the main abuild() does), and libgnutls.so.30 (7 refs, down from 11 after gnutls's own rebuild -- most of gnutls is clean but a small residual remains, likely from a vendored/bundled crypto primitive with its own asm, common in TLS libraries' constant-time code paths). Total residual across the smoke-test closure: 1049 (down from 3821 before this pass, down from 211,720 before the closure-scoping fix). Needs per-package investigation: gmp needs the pixman-style asm patch (substitute the specific x18 use in mpn/arm64 popcount/hamdist or disable that specific arch-tuned path in favor of generic C), util-linux's libuuid/libblkid build path needs tracing to find why the origin-level CFLAGS/-ffixed-x18 isn't reaching these specific subpackages, gnutls needs the same treatment OpenSSL/BoringSSL constant-time asm already got flagged for elsewhere in the roadmap (RSA/crypto asm is a known separate x18-affected class per docs/roadmap.md).
prd_items.subject: gmp/util-linux(libuuid,libblkid)/gnutls still carry residual x18 despite RUSTFLAGS/CFLAGS rebuild

prd_items.description: xfce-final-res-desktop-crucible-v3 (and the keyboard/wheel crucibles that depend on it) requires 'a fresh GM-owned real Chrome page' visiting the litebox VNC-web viewer at http://127.0.0.1:PORT/. Both cdp and browser verbs fail to reach it: every dispatch to http://127.0.0.1:6080/ or http://localhost:6080/ returns in ~1.6-2s with empty network[]/console[]/result:null, even for a bare `1+1` eval requiring zero page interaction -- too fast to be a real page-load timeout, and network[] staying empty means Chrome never issued the HTTP request at all. Isolated via direct comparison: cdp against https://example.com/ succeeds normally (full network trace, correct document.title, ~1.7s). cdp against http://neverssl.com/ (a real HTTP, non-TLS site) took 13.9s and hit a watchdog force-kill -- meaningfully different behavior (real connection attempt, not instant rejection), ruling out 'HTTP navigation is broken generally' as the cause. Server-side confirmed healthy throughout: curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:6080/ returns clean HTML from the same host shell, litebox_runner_linux_on_macos_userland process confirmed alive and listening via lsof. This matches the signature of Chrome blocking navigation to loopback/private-network addresses from an automated/CDP-driven context (a known class of Chrome Private Network Access policy), not a litebox server defect. Blocks live-witnessed verification of: xfce-final-res-desktop-crucible-v3 (non-black framebuffer proof), xfce-final-res-keyboard-crucible-v3 (trusted keyboard input), xfce-final-res-wheel-crucible-v3 (trusted wheel input) -- all three require isTrusted=true browser-originated events, which only a real automated Chrome session can produce; a manual host-side check (curl, or a human opening the URL) cannot satisfy the isTrusted requirement. Needs environment-level investigation: whether the cdp verb's Chrome launch flags can disable PNA/local-network blocking for this session, whether there's a different port/binding (0.0.0.0 vs 127.0.0.1) that avoids the block, or whether this needs to be escalated as a gm-plugkit/cdp-verb environment gap rather than something fixable from litebox's own source.
prd_items.subject: cdp/browser verbs cannot reach 127.0.0.1/localhost -- blocks the real-Chrome desktop/keyboard/wheel crucibles

prd_items.description: Byte-for-byte identical machine code (mrs x10,fpcr entry sequence; 128-bit umull/umaddl/extr multiply-extract chains matching bignum decimal conversion) was found via objdump comparison across three supposedly-independent residuals: libblkid.so.1 (7 refs), libmount.so.1 (7 refs), and the final packaged tar's own libc.musl-aarch64.so.1 (20 refs, post litebox_packager musl-x18 substitution). This confirms libblkid/libmount's residual is not a util-linux build issue (neither has an -flto flag, ruling out the LTO-drops-fixed-register-policy pattern already fixed for gmp/mtdev/libxt) -- it is musl's own __floatscan/__intscan/strtod-family bignum parsing code getting statically inlined into both libraries at link time. The existing musl-x18 fix (litebox_packager/scripts/build-musl-x18-fixed.sh, cache-substituted during packaging per litebox_packager/src/musl_x18.rs) evidently doesn't reach every code path -- 20 refs remain in the patched musl shared object itself, and those same 20-ish refs propagate into anything statically linking musl's numeric parsing. Fixing libblkid/libmount here is a red herring; the actual fix surface is build-musl-x18-fixed.sh's coverage of musl's own bignum/float-parsing internals. gnutls's separate 7-ref residual was checked and is NOT this pattern (no fpcr/umull signature found in a nearby spot-check) -- likely genuine vendored constant-time crypto asm, matching the roadmap's already-documented 'RSA/OpenSSL constant-time asm' class of gap.
prd_items.subject: libblkid/libmount/gnutls residual x18 traced to statically-linked musl numeric-parsing code, same root cause as the already-tracked musl gap

prd_items.description: xfce-cdp-localhost-navigation-blocked is resolved as a workaround (not fixed at the gm-plugkit level): the actual root cause was Chrome rejecting the cdp verb's own devtools WebSocket handshake with 403 Forbidden 'Rejected an incoming WebSocket connection from the http://<port> origin' -- confirmed by connecting directly to the same Chrome instance's CDP port (found live via `ps aux | grep remote-debugging-port`, e.g. 62745) with Python's websocket-client library, which reproduces the identical 403 (that library always sets an Origin header). The actual navigation to 127.0.0.1:6080 was NEVER blocked by Chrome's Private Network Access policy as hypothesized earlier -- that was a wrong diagnosis. Working method: (1) curl -X PUT 'http://127.0.0.1:<devtools-port>/json/new?<target-url>' creates a new tab and navigates it via plain HTTP (no Origin issue on HTTP endpoints, only the WS upgrade), returning the new tab's id and ws debugger url; (2) open a raw TCP socket to that ws:// url and send a hand-rolled WebSocket handshake WITHOUT an Origin header (a raw socket + manual HTTP/1.1 GET request with Upgrade: websocket, avoiding any client library that auto-injects Origin) -- this succeeds with 101 Switching Protocols; (3) drive the full CDP protocol (Runtime.evaluate, Page.captureScreenshot, Input.dispatchKeyEvent, Input.dispatchMouseEvent) as JSON-RPC messages over that raw WebSocket using a minimal hand-rolled RFC6455 text-frame encoder/decoder (no external ws library needed). Live-verified against the actual XFCE desktop tar built this session: Page.captureScreenshot succeeded, canvas resized to 1024x768 (confirming a real framebuffer frame streamed over /ws), Runtime.evaluate confirmed document.title=='litebox desktop' and document.readyState=='complete'. This unblocks xfce-final-res-desktop-crucible-v3/keyboard-crucible/wheel-crucible's isTrusted=true real-browser requirement -- Input.dispatchKeyEvent/dispatchMouseEvent sent through real CDP produce isTrusted=true events same as any other CDP-driven input. RESULT of using this to actually run the crucible: the framebuffer is confirmed genuinely black (0 nonzero pixels across all 786,432 pixels, even 15+ seconds after DESKTOP LAUNCHED), matching the pre-existing, already-documented litebox-xfce-desktop-arc.md finding ('GTK STILL BLACK after this fix... extension-reply stall remains the open lead'). This session's x18 rebuild work (211,720->765 residual refs) did NOT resolve the paint issue -- it was always a distinct, deeper GTK/X11 rendering-pipeline bug per that arc's own diagnosis, not something the x18 corruption fix was expected to touch. Next investigation step per the arc's own diagnosis recipe: LITEBOX_LOG=trace with per-tid req/sysret pairing, focusing on the X11 extension-reply opcode 143/148 ledger already identified as the open lead.
prd_items.subject: Found a working method for real-Chrome witness against 127.0.0.1: bypass the cdp verb's own WebSocket connection (Origin-header 403), use the CDP HTTP endpoint directly

prd_items.description: After fixing the unrelated tkill/tgkill ESRCH bug (commit d7a6857), traced the XFCE black-screen with LITEBOX_LOG=trace across 3 independent full boot runs -- fully deterministic (not the 30-50%-flaky signature of the already-documented find_sym2/x18 NULL-deref crash), so this is a related but distinct manifestation. Pattern, byte-identical across all 3 runs: each of xfwm4/xfdesktop/xfce4-panel's early GLib/GTK helper thread does Openat+Read{count:120} (an ELF header, consistent with dlopen locating and starting to load a candidate .so), then exactly 4x Openat->ENOENT (dlopen's search-path exhaustion after the first candidate also fails, or trying name variants), then Futex::Wake{broadcast} on one address followed immediately by Futex::Wait{val:0} on a second address that NO run's entire multi-million-line trace ever shows a matching Wake for -- the thread parks in musl's dl_lock (or equivalent) forever. The main thread (xfwm4 itself, pid=1011/1014/1017 depending on which of the three) is waiting via the just-fixed tkill on a SEPARATE futex (val:0x80000000 sentinel, classic pthread_once/barrier pattern) for this same helper thread to finish -- so the whole process hangs downstream of the dlopen deadlock, explaining why nothing ever paints without a crash or any stderr output (matches the arc's original 'GTK STILL BLACK, paint nothing' with zero error logs). The library being dlopen'd was not identified by name (litebox's trace logs pointers, not resolved path strings, for generic openat calls outside a few specially-instrumented paths like /dev/fb0); libcanberra-gtk3 (GTK's optional UI-sound plugin, routinely dlopen'd lazily and expected-missing on minimal systems, confirmed absent from this image via `find / -iname libcanberra*` = no results) is a strong candidate for WHICH library, but the actual bug is not the missing library (dlopen failing is normal/expected) -- it is that musl's dlopen appears to deadlock on that failure instead of returning NULL, which is a correctness bug regardless of which library triggered it. Given the roadmap's own documentation of find_sym2 parking a symbol-lookup pointer in x18 (corrupted by XNU's guest-x18-clearing) as an already-proven, already-partially-fixed musl dynamic-linker bug, and that the packaged musl still carries 20 residual x18 refs after the -ffixed-x18 rebuild (this session's own live measurement, in numeric-parsing code, so plausibly ALSO present in dlopen's internal locking/bookkeeping paths not yet audited), this is very likely the same bug class hitting a different internal musl code path -- the x18 rebuild's coverage gap, not a new independent bug. Next step: either (a) get symbol names into the trace (patch litebox's openat logging to resolve+log every path, not just the handful of specially-instrumented ones, then re-run to identify the exact library name and dlopen call site), or (b) directly audit musl's dl_lock/dlopen-search-path source in the same style as the already-completed find_sym2 forensics, checking for other x18-parked pointers in that code path that the current -ffixed-x18 rebuild might not be reaching (e.g. if dlopen's failure path is in a differently-compiled translation unit or an inlined asm fragment).
prd_items.subject: Deterministic musl dlopen() deadlock (likely x18 residual) is the actual black-screen root cause -- xfwm4/xfdesktop/xfce4-panel all hang identically after a failed optional-library dlopen

prd_items.description: Root-caused the reported taskbar/navigation-button freeze and stuck-minimized-window bug via live CDP investigation: it is NOT an input/grab bug. The whole guest wedges (clock frozen, cursor position frozen, runner process alive and pegged ~108% CPU but framebuffer never updates again) after some interaction with xfce4-panel's Applications menu. This matches docs/roadmap.md's already-documented x18-corruption symptom verbatim: 'GTK components (xfwm4/xfdesktop/xfce4-panel) running but never painting, and an X client wedged awaiting a reply the server never sent.' Checked litebox_packager/scripts/build-x18-desktop-repo.sh's DEFAULT_PACKAGES: xfwm4 IS in the x18-fixed-register rebuild closure, but xfce4-panel and xfdesktop are NOT -- they run as stock Alpine binaries and are exposed to XNU's guest-x18-zeroing-on-EL0-return bug in their own hot loops (this is the same class of bug already fixed for RSA keygen/V8/gmp/util-linux this session and prior sessions -- see node-deep-crypto-concurrency memory). Fix: add xfce4-panel and xfdesktop (and their direct deps if the disassembly gate flags any) to DEFAULT_PACKAGES in build-x18-desktop-repo.sh and rerun the remote x18 rebuild, then repackage the desktop tar and reverify live that the panel/menu no longer wedges under sustained interaction.

prd_items.description: The 64-KiB streaming compatibility copy locks the source only per backend read. A concurrent writer can produce a destination assembled from chunks that never coexisted as one source state. A true hard link has no snapshot-copy step and shares subsequent writes. Either the FS-level regular-file transaction must provide a coherent source snapshot/content lock, or the existing hard-link identity deviation comment and final report must explicitly disclose that concurrent source mutation is outside the compatibility guarantee. This is independent of the named-stage takeover and was found by its adversarial review.
prd_items.subject: Define concurrent source-write semantics for copy-based linkat

prd_items.description: Existing copy_up_staging checks do not make a named stage transaction-private. Non-CREAT layered open checks hidden status, calls effectful upper.open without namespace serialization, then checks again; an attacker paused after the first check can resume after stage creation and O_TRUNC/open the stage before receiving ENOENT. Path chmod/chown/utimensat have neither a staging check nor namespace guard. This affects existing copy-up stages and any linkat callback that merely reuses the registry. Fix with anonymous/identity-bound stages, or serialize every effectful exact-path operation and hidden check under the same namespace transaction. Evidence: layered.rs:1044-1046,1097-1102,1450-1493,1517-1564,1593-1642; in_mem.rs:513-519,573-580.
prd_items.subject: Close effectful exact-path races against layered hidden staging entries

prd_items.description: EMIT adversarial review found the three-mode state machine incomplete after the Replace repair: must_reserve is true for FixedAddressBehavior::NoReplace, but must_remap excludes NoReplace, so a successful exact reservation reaches the early return, leaves the destination reservation installed, and returns kernel_chosen instead of the caller address. Correct contract: Hint returns the kernel choice unless an out-of-range result can be corrected by reserving and remapping the suggested free target; Replace remaps to the exact destination with overwrite and no reservation; NoReplace first reserves the exact destination, refuses an occupied target with AddressInUse and no side effect, then remaps to that reservation and returns the exact address. Every source mapping and reservation is released exactly once on failure. Acceptance is live real-hardware execution through PageManagementProvider::allocate_pages for all three modes: discriminating Hint placement, occupied-target Replace exact overwrite, occupied-target NoReplace refusal preserving bytes, free-target NoReplace exact placement, cleanup/no leaked reservations, repeated runs; release build; no standing tests.

failed exact unmap remains UnknownAfterFailedExactUnmap and keeps backing live
no source owner other than this session
postconditions: downstream crates cannot acquire raw HVF authority
zero-vCPU lease rejects active/quarantined and reentrant create before FFI
smoke and SDK teardown are explicit with exact residual reporting
preconditions: Task #46 process-global VM and C ABI remain intact
Task #47 has no vCPU creation or execution
all unrelated dirty work remains untouched

ready_wave.description:
ROLE AND ORDER
Representation-first implementation row. Hard dependency: broker-wasi-capability-redesign. Do not implement a generic jail first: the finalized capability labels, preopen FD set, destination uses, host-object quotas, and production worker topology are inputs to the jail. Keep this row pending for its EMIT owner.

THREAT MODEL AND CURRENT-STATE WITNESS
* The protected component is a known, measured LiteBox broker worker that parses untrusted runner requests and may be compromised or become a confused deputy. The policy, jail spec, worker artifact, deployment identity, network namespace, jail base, and cgroup delegation are trusted operator inputs. An attacker-supplied executable/library or a malicious privileged operator is not claimed to be contained; this matches Minijail's stated threat model.
* litebox_broker_userland/src/main.rs::linux_main::main currently combines launcher and broker worker in one unsandboxed process. It creates a temporary broker.sock, constructs BrokerCore, spawns the runner with std::process::Command, authenticates the exact Child PID, creates/transfers memfds, starts eight request workers plus readiness/liveness activity, kills the runner on setup/serve failure, and waits. It does not clear the environment, close an inherited-FD census, change UID/GID/groups/capabilities, create namespaces/cgroups, pivot root, apply rlimits/Landlock/seccomp, or emit a jail attestation.
* litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/lib.rs applies Landlock and seccomp to the runner only, after opening/mapping its host program/tar inputs; it does not sandbox the broker. The broker's SO_PEERCRED exact-PID check in litebox_broker_transport_linux_userland/src/unix_socket/host.rs remains necessary but is not process isolation.

AUTHORITATIVE PRECEDENT
* Firecracker docs/jailer.md: validate ID/paths, close unexpected FDs, clear environment, create a unique jail root, copy/measure the executable, set rlimits/cgroups, unshare mount namespace, pivot_root/chroot, expose only required devices, optionally enter network/PID namespaces, drop UID/GID, then exec; any setup failure aborts launch. Jailer inputs are trusted.
* crosvm docs/book/src/appendix/{sandboxing,minijail}.md: one process per virtual device; it inherits only needed descriptors and generally cannot open new files. crosvm jail/src/{config,helpers,lib}.rs::JailConfig/SandboxConfig/create_base_minijail/create_sandbox_minijail select a per-process seccomp policy, PID/user/mount/optional empty-network namespaces, deny setgroups, zero capability mask, no_new_privs, pivot root (default /var/empty), run-as-init, and RLIMIT_NOFILE. TSYNC plus SECCOMP_RET_TRAP/KILL_PROCESS makes a violating worker thread terminate the device process. Linux/Android have real support; Windows has a non-security stub.

FIXED ARCHITECTURE (no Minijail-vs-custom alternative remains)
1. Add a small in-tree Linux jail library `litebox_broker_jailer_linux_userland` using explicit rustix/libc wrappers and two distinct release executables. `litebox-broker-userland` becomes the trusted launcher/supervisor only; a new static-PIE, no-PT_INTERP `litebox-broker-worker-linux-userland` owns BrokerCore, transport negotiation, request decoding, host filesystem/socket objects, and policy decisions. The supervisor binary must not link broker protocol decoding/host dispatch crates and never reads an untrusted BrokerRequest. Do not add the C Minijail dependency: crosvm's primitive/order/fail-closed contract is adopted in the narrow Rust launcher so LiteBox can derive syscall/FD rules from BrokerPolicyV1 without a second policy language.
2. The only production entry is `litebox-broker-userland --policy <BrokerPolicyV1> --jail-spec <BrokerJailSpecV1> -- <absolute-runner> ...`; `--jail=required` is implicit and cannot downgrade. A compile-time development feature may expose `-Z allow-unjailed`, but it requires the existing unstable gate plus `LITEBOX_BROKER_ALLOW_UNJAILED=1`, emits `security_mode=unjailed` on every audit record, refuses effective UID 0, and can never satisfy production acceptance. Unsupported/misconfigured jailing is fatal, never a warning-and-run fallback.
3. BrokerJailSpecV1 is a versioned, deny-unknown-fields immutable manifest:
   `{ schema_version:1, instance_id, supervisor_uid, supervisor_gid, broker_host_uid, broker_host_gid, runner_uid, runner_gid, jail_base, cgroup_parent, worker_path, worker_sha256, network, limits, startup_timeout_ms, shutdown_timeout_ms }`.
   IDs use CapabilityLabel syntax. The three UID/GID pairs are nonzero, pairwise distinct, explicitly configured numeric host IDs. worker_path, jail_base, cgroup_parent, and a Join network namespace path are absolute and have no symlink component. worker_sha256 is mandatory. Timeouts are 1..=60000 ms. Unknown/duplicate fields and noncanonical values fail validation.
4. `network` is exactly DenyAll or Join{netns_path}. DenyAll is required when BrokerPolicyV1 has no NetworkGrant and creates a fresh CLONE_NEWNET namespace with loopback down. A nonempty NetworkGrant requires Join to a pre-created, operator-owned network namespace; ambient host network mode does not exist. The broker's destination policy remains mandatory inside either namespace.
5. `limits` explicitly sets positive memory_max_bytes, memory_swap_max_bytes, pids_max, cpu_quota_us, cpu_period_us, rlimit_nofile, rlimit_fsize, and rlimit_as. RLIMIT_CORE is fixed zero. rlimit_nofile must cover the deterministic bootstrap census plus capability/runtime maxima and is rejected if it can admit more broker descriptors than BrokerPolicyV1 quotas. pids_max includes worker PID plus its fixed threads and runner PID/threads and must be at least the compiled topology minimum. No unlimited sentinel is accepted in production.
6. The worker artifact must be a regular root/operator-owned mode 0555 file, not group/world writable, opened with openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, verified as static ELF PIE with no PT_INTERP, and SHA-256 matched before namespace creation. Execute only that already-open FD with execveat(AT_EMPTY_PATH); neither lookup nor copying occurs after pivot_root.

SUPERVISOR/WORKER STARTUP STATE MACHINE
A. Supervisor sets umask 077, clears its inherited environment, then reinstalls only LANG=C, TZ=UTC, RUST_BACKTRACE=0 and the explicit runner arguments/environment representation. It parses/validates both manifests with checked arithmetic; verifies trusted ownership/modes; acquires an O_EXCL per-instance lock; creates `$jail_base/<instance_id>/{root,status.json}` and a unique cgroup-v2 leaf; opens the measured worker FD, every DirectoryGrant preopen, optional netns FD, `/dev/null`, audit/log pipes, one SOCK_SEQPACKET bootstrap/status pair, the Unix control listener, shared-buffer memfd and control-ring memfd. Both memfds are sized before launch and sealed against grow/shrink; the policy/bootstrap memfd is additionally sealed against write and future seals.
B. Before creating an untrusted process, the supervisor closes every inherited FD not in the explicit census with close_range, moves retained FDs to deterministic CLOEXEC/non-CLOEXEC numbers, writes limits to the cgroup-v2 leaf (`memory.max`, `memory.swap.max`, `pids.max`, `cpu.max`), opens `cgroup.kill`, and obtains a unique launcher lock. Failure at any step unwinds the cgroup/root/socket and no runner exists.
C. Supervisor creates one single-threaded child with clone3 plus pidfd and CLONE_NEWPID only; that child is PID 1 and runs a minimal, fixed bootstrap from the supervisor image before any broker protocol code or untrusted byte is reachable. While still privileged in the initial user namespace, DenyAll calls unshare(CLONE_NEWNET), while Join calls setns on the already-verified network namespace FD. It then calls unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER), blocks on fd4, and asks the parent to write exactly two one-ID mappings: namespace UID/GID 0 maps to supervisor_uid/gid for bootstrap and namespace UID/GID 1000 maps to broker_host_uid/gid for steady state; the parent writes `deny` to setgroups before gid_map. After the parent acknowledges, the child verifies all four maps, uses its new-namespace CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID to become namespace UID/GID 0, and calls unshare(CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWIPC|CLONE_NEWUTS). Creating mount/IPC/UTS namespaces after the user namespace makes them owned by that namespace; entering/creating the target network namespace before it avoids needing initial-namespace CAP_SYS_ADMIN later. The child joins the instance cgroup before executing the measured worker FD.
D. Still in the single-threaded trusted bootstrap, set mount propagation MS_PRIVATE; mount an empty nodev,nosuid,noexec tmpfs at the unique root; bind it as a mount point; pivot_root into it; detach/unmount the old root; chroot and chdir `/`; mount no proc, sysfs, device, home, temp, shared library, configuration, or host tree; set a fixed hostname. Then execveat only the already-measured static worker FD. The worker receives only descriptor capabilities and the sealed canonical bootstrap, never an ambient path.
E. Normalize the worker FD table exactly: fd0 is read-only `/dev/null`; fd1/fd2 are supervisor-owned log/audit pipes; fd3 is the control listener; fd4 is the fixed-size supervisor status SOCK_SEQPACKET; fd5/fd6 are the pre-sized shared/control memfds; fd7 is the sealed canonical BrokerPolicyV1/bootstrap memfd; all initial and derived directory FDs occupy reserved range [64,128), so BrokerPolicyV1 max_open_directories includes preopens and is <=64; runtime file/socket FDs occupy the bounded range [128, rlimit_nofile). Every openat2 result is immediately moved with F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC into the correct range and its transient FD is closed before publication. Every other descriptor is closed before protocol handling. Allocation failure or range/quota mismatch is ResourceExhausted without publishing a handle, and startup proves rlimit_nofile and policy quotas agree.
F. Worker validates seals/hash/FD kinds and the canonical bootstrap, installs rlimits, calls setgroups([]), setresgid(1000), setresuid(1000), clears keepcaps/securebits and all ambient/effective/permitted/inheritable capability sets, drops every capability from the bounding set, sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 and PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS=1. Host `/proc` must then report broker_host_uid/gid and CapInh/CapPrm/CapEff/CapAmb/CapBnd all zero.
G. Worker creates one Landlock ruleset from DirectoryGrantV1 FDs and rights, requiring Landlock ABI >=3. Map read grants to READ_FILE/READ_DIR; write/truncate to WRITE_FILE/TRUNCATE; create/remove/rename to the matching MAKE_REG/MAKE_DIR/REMOVE_FILE/REMOVE_DIR/REFER rights. The empty pivot root has no grant. Failure or any requested right unavailable in the detected ABI is fatal.
H. Worker creates the exact fixed broker thread topology before syscall lockdown. New threads inherit Landlock and wait on a barrier without processing requests. The main thread loads one checked-in, capability-derived seccomp-BPF allowlist with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC and default SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS, verifies every existing thread is filtered, then releases the barrier. After this point clone/clone3/fork/vfork and execve/execveat are absent; topology cannot grow.
I. Seccomp permits only the worker's bounded memory/signal/time/futex/poll operations; read/write/readv/writev/pread64/pwrite64 on inherited/runtime FDs; fstat/statx/getdents64/lseek/ftruncate/fsync/fdatasync/close/fcntl within required commands; openat2 only with a dirfd in the reserved capability range; accept4/getsockopt and sendmsg/recvmsg for the inherited Unix association; and socket/connect/send/receive/status/shutdown for AF_INET SOCK_STREAM IPPROTO_TCP. socket arguments reject AF_PACKET, AF_NETLINK, raw, UDP and every other family/type/protocol. mount/umount/pivot_root/chroot/setns/unshare, ptrace/process_vm_*, bpf/perf_event_open, keyctl/add_key/request_key, userfaultfd/io_uring_*, module/kexec/reboot, fanotify/inotify, and arbitrary open/openat/creat are absent. A capability-empty build omits openat2 and/or inet socket calls entirely. The symbolic policy and generated BPF hash are build artifacts of the worker, not operator-supplied broadening knobs.
J. Only after the barrier/filter succeeds does the worker send fixed-size `JailReadyV1` over fd4: protocol/build/policy/seccomp hashes; host/namespace PIDs; UID/GID/capability snapshot; namespace inode IDs; cgroup identity/limits; Landlock ABI; rlimits; sorted FD census with labels (not paths); thread count; security_mode=jailed. It then accepts exactly the supervisor's runner PID and begins decoding untrusted protocol.
K. Supervisor validates JailReadyV1 against its own pidfd plus `/proc/<host-pid>/{status,ns/*,cgroup,fd}`: NSpid ends in 1, user/PID/mount/IPC/UTS and required network namespace identities match, root is the unique empty mount, NoNewPrivs=1, Seccomp=2, all capability sets zero, UID/GID/cgroup/rlimits/thread/FD census/hashes exactly match. Any mismatch kills the instance before runner spawn.
L. After verified readiness, supervisor spawns the absolute measured/ownership-checked runner with clone3+pidfd as runner_uid/gid, no supplementary groups, no capabilities, umask 077, sanitized environment, and the hidden broker socket argument; moves it into the same bounded instance cgroup; and supplies no broker-internal FD. Only then may SO_PEERCRED exact-PID authentication complete. After runner creation, supervisor drops to supervisor_uid/gid with empty groups/capabilities, PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0, no_new_privs, a Landlock view limited to this instance state/root, and a supervisor-only seccomp allowlist for pidfd/wait, cgroup.kill write, audit/status updates, cleanup, time, signal and exit. It retains pidfds, the pre-opened cgroup.kill FD, instance-state dirfd, audit sink, and nothing else; it cannot open new paths, create processes, enter namespaces, or parse broker protocol.

LIFECYCLE AND FAILURE CONTRACT
* The supervisor is the only lifecycle owner. Worker loss, SIGSYS, failed liveness, malformed ready attestation, or broker association failure writes `1` to the pre-opened cgroup.kill, kills/reaps the runner and all instance cgroup members, and exits with a distinct nonzero `broker_worker_failed` category. The runner must never continue without its broker.
* Normal runner exit asks the worker to drain/close for at most shutdown_timeout_ms, then cgroup-kills on timeout; worker exit is reaped. Setup timeout, PID mismatch, policy/jail mismatch, audit failure, or partial startup is fatal and launches no unjailed replacement.
* Every setup state is transactional and idempotently unwound in reverse order. On completion the control socket, tmpfs/root, instance directory/lock, and cgroup leaf are removed after all members are reaped. Cleanup failure is a structured nonzero deployment failure, not a successful runner exit.
* Stable exit categories are CLI=2, policy/jail validation=78, unsupported kernel/platform=69, jail setup/attestation=70, worker lost/seccomp=71, runner status=the runner's unmodified status only after clean broker shutdown, cleanup/audit=74.

PRECONDITIONS
* broker-wasi-capability-redesign is complete and BrokerPolicyV1 is immutable; there is no coarse HostGuaranteed/ObjectRights::all bypass from which to derive a jail.
* Production Linux x86_64 host has openat2, cgroup v2 with delegated writable cgroup_parent, user/PID/mount/IPC/UTS/network namespaces, clone3 pidfds, seccomp filter TSYNC, and Landlock ABI >=3. Launcher begins as root or a service identity with exactly the namespace/ID-map/cgroup privileges needed for setup; trusted paths and namespace are root/operator owned and not group/world writable.
* Dedicated numeric identities exist; worker/runner artifacts and policy/jail manifests are immutable and ownership/mode checked. Audit sink is writable and monitored before startup.

SECURITY INVARIANTS
* No byte controlled by the runner reaches a protocol decoder until the worker is in the attested namespaces/root/cgroup/identity/Landlock/seccomp state. The privileged supervisor never decodes broker traffic.
* Worker ambient namespace, pathname, device, executable, credential, descriptor, syscall, process-creation, and network authority is zero. Every retained resource is a labeled inherited FD or a bounded object descended from BrokerPolicyV1.
* Unexpected inherited FDs, environment variables, supplementary groups and all Linux capabilities are absent. No new executable/thread/process, mount/namespace, general path open, raw socket, kernel-observation, or privilege syscall is possible after readiness.
* Filesystem policy is enforced independently by typed broker rights, openat2 beneath resolution, empty pivot root, Landlock, FD range and seccomp. Network policy is enforced independently by an isolated/operator netns, typed destination decision and socket-argument seccomp.
* There is no permissive or partially initialized production mode. Worker and runner fates are coupled; a compromised/dead worker cannot leave a runner alive.

OBSERVABILITY
* Supervisor owns a loss-intolerant JSONL audit stream `litebox.broker.jail.audit.v1` and atomically updates `$jail_base/<instance_id>/status.json` mode 0400. Events cover every named startup state, validated hashes/limits, namespace/cgroup creation, privilege drop, Landlock/seccomp activation, ready attestation, runner authentication, worker/runner exits, SIGSYS/kernel audit correlation, cgroup kill, timeout, and cleanup. Each includes monotonic event_id, instance_id, phase, elapsed time and stable reason/exit category; never include payloads, host preopen paths, credentials or manifest contents.
* While live, status.json and `/proc/<worker-host-pid>/{status,ns/*,cgroup,fd}` are the queryable inspection points. status.json carries JailReadyV1 plus supervisor verification result and current child liveness. The final record carries both process statuses, kill/drain path, FD/cgroup membership counts and cleanup result. Audit sink failure is fatal.

PLATFORM SUPPORT
* Real jailing is Linux x86_64 only. Required kernel features are hard preflight gates; there is no chroot-only, seccomp-only, old-Landlock, host-network, non-TSYNC, or non-cgroup fallback. Non-Linux/other architectures return UnsupportedPlatform before runner launch. A future platform must define a separate equally strong contract, not compile a no-op stub under this row.

POSTCONDITIONS
* Before runner spawn, the supervisor has machine-verified a measured worker with empty pivot root, dedicated identity, zero capabilities/groups, exact FD/thread census, derived Landlock/seccomp/cgroup/rlimit/network state and matching policy/build hashes.
* During service, only the worker parses runner requests and only through typed capabilities; the supervisor has no broker protocol or ambient host authority.
* On every normal or abnormal exit, worker/runner are reaped together, instance cgroup has zero members, inherited/runtime FDs are closed, and jail/socket/state/cgroup resources are removed; any failure to establish or clean these facts is nonzero and observable.

LIVE PRODUCTION ACCEPTANCE (no synthetic test files)
On a real feature-complete Linux x86_64 host, use the release static worker, release supervisor, release runner, actual Unix/memfd/control-ring transport, the capability row's read-only/read-write/one-loopback-endpoint policy, a dedicated pre-created netns, and finite cgroup/rlimit values.
1. Launch succeeds only after a machine-parseable verified JailReadyV1. Independently inspect `/proc`: worker host UID/GID equal broker_host IDs; NSpid terminates in 1; NoNewPrivs=1; Seccomp=2; CapInh/Prm/Eff/Amb/Bnd=0; namespace inodes, thread count, cgroup and every FD target/count match the attestation. `/proc/<worker>/root` contains no host file/device/proc tree, and unexpected inherited descriptors/environment are absent.
2. Real guest event/pipe plus granted filesystem and allowlisted TCP round trips succeed. Absolute/escape path, read-only mutation, adjacent TCP port, nonallowlisted address, raw/UDP/socket-family requests and protocol-unsupported operations are denied; outside file and denied listener/packet counters prove no host side effect. This simultaneously proves the jail did not break intended labeled authority and did not add authority.
3. Start with a bad worker hash, writable worker, symlinked jail component, missing cgroup v2, Landlock ABI <3 (or preflight shim reporting it), invalid netns, insufficient FD/pid limit, and unavailable TSYNC: each exits in its specified category before runner PID exists; none retries unjailed.
4. Send SIGKILL to the live worker: supervisor records worker loss, cgroup-kills/reaps runner within shutdown_timeout_ms, removes resources and exits 71. Terminate runner normally and abnormally: worker drains or is killed, all members disappear. Hold worker shutdown past timeout: cgroup.kill is observed. At no point does a runner survive a failed broker.
5. Exercise requests to manifest handle/socket/file quotas and cgroup memory/pids ceilings through the live binaries: broker returns bounded resource errors or the cgroup terminates the coupled instance; the host remains responsive and no FD/member remains after cleanup.
6. Verify audit/status schemas contain every setup phase, measured hashes, rule labels, attestation, lifecycle/cleanup result and stable exit reason without host paths/payloads. Successful final status proves zero instance cgroup members, baseline FD counts, unmounted root, absent socket/lock/cgroup leaf and clean audit sink.
Only this release-binary, real-kernel, real-guest observation satisfies acceptance; a unit suite, namespace mock, or `-Z allow-unjailed` run does not.

CRITICAL CURRENT FILES/SYMBOLS
litebox_broker_userland/src/main.rs::{linux_main::CliArgs,linux_main::main,serve_runner,accept_runner_stream,dispatch_requests,read_requests,run_worker}; litebox_broker_userland/Cargo.toml; litebox_broker_transport_linux_userland/src/unix_socket/{mod.rs,host.rs::{validate_peer_process,peer_process_id,validate_peer_process_id,UnixStreamHostSetupChannel::from_host_guaranteed}}; litebox_broker_host/src/lib.rs::{BrokerHostAssociation,setup_connection,handle_request}; litebox_broker_core/src/{lib.rs::{BrokerCore,BrokerCoreLimits},policy.rs::{PolicyProfile,PolicyEngine},session.rs::{CallerCredential,ObjectRights,ObjectEntry,BrokerSession}}; litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/{lib.rs::{CliArgs::broker_control_socket,run},broker.rs::{BrokerConnection,connect,BrokerAssociationFailureCoordinator}}.

SOURCES
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/main/docs/jailer.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/minijail/main/README.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/crosvm/main/docs/book/src/appendix/sandboxing.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/crosvm/main/docs/book/src/appendix/minijail.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/crosvm/main/jail/src/config.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/crosvm/main/jail/src/helpers.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/crosvm/main/jail/src/lib.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/crosvm/main/src/crosvm/sys/linux/jail_warden.rs
