ready_wave.description:
ROLE AND ORDER
Representation-first implementation row. It is the first of the two broker hardening rows and has no dependency on broker-process-jailing; broker-process-jailing MUST depend on this row because the jail FD allowlist, Landlock rules, network namespace choice, rlimits, and seccomp arguments must be derived from the finalized capability set. Keep this row pending until an EMIT owner implements and witnesses the whole contract.

CURRENT-STATE WITNESS (corrects the roadmap premise)
* litebox_broker_userland/src/main.rs::linux_main::main creates a temporary Unix listener, constructs PolicyEngine::with_host_guaranteed_rights(ObjectRights::all()), spawns exactly the configured runner, and validates the accepted peer PID.
* litebox_broker_transport_linux_userland/src/unix_socket/host.rs::validate_peer_process uses Linux SO_PEERCRED; UnixStreamHostSetupChannel::from_host_guaranteed converts that deployment proof into PeerCredential::HostGuaranteed.
* litebox_broker_host/src/lib.rs::setup_connection maps that to CallerCredential::HostGuaranteed. BrokerHostAssociation::execute_request/handle_request then dispatch event/pipe operations. handle_request deliberately returns UnsupportedOperation for every SocketRequest.
* litebox_broker_core/src/policy.rs::PolicyEngine::principal_object_rights supplies one coarse ObjectRights bitset per CallerCredential. litebox_broker_core/src/session.rs::ObjectRights contains only WAIT and WRITE and the same bitset is stamped onto every newly-created object reference.
* litebox_broker_protocol/src/message.rs and socket.rs already encode typed IPv4/TCP create/connect/send/receive/shutdown/status requests, but litebox_broker_local has no socket adapter, BrokerControl in litebox/src/broker/mod.rs has no socket methods, and ObjectEntry has no socket object.
* There is no broker filesystem request, local adapter, host handler, core object, or policy decision today. The runner constructs its guest filesystem locally from in-memory/tar layers in litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/lib.rs. This row is therefore a greenfield broker filesystem capability surface plus completion/redesign of the reserved TCP surface, not a refactor of an existing broker filesystem path.

AUTHORITATIVE PRECEDENT
* WASI filesystem 0.2.8 types.wit: all paths are relative to a base directory descriptor; absolute paths, .. or symlink traversal outside that base fail not-permitted; descriptor flags separate read, write, and mutate-directory; open-at derives a descriptor and cannot grant mutation through a read-only base.
* WASI sockets 0.2.8 network.wit/tcp.wit: network is an opaque resource; start-bind/start-connect require a borrowed network resource; access-denied is a first-class failure.
* Wasmtime main crates/wasi/src/ctx.rs and sockets/mod.rs: no preopens and all socket addresses denied by default; preopened_dir binds host and guest paths with FsPerms; socket_addr_check receives (SocketAddr, SocketAddrUse), defaults false, and maps denial to PermissionDenied. SocketAddrUse distinguishes TcpBind/TcpListen/TcpAccept/TcpConnect and UDP uses.

REPRESENTATION CONTRACT
1. Replace PolicyProfile's deployment-wide ObjectRights grant with one immutable, versioned, deny-unknown-fields BrokerPolicyV1 loaded and fully validated before the runner is launched:
   BrokerPolicyV1 { schema_version: 1, principal: PrincipalPolicyV1, limits: AuthorityLimitsV1 }.
   The initial production topology has exactly one principal because the broker launches and PID-binds exactly one runner. PrincipalPolicyV1 contains: a stable principal label, explicit event/pipe creation grants, directory_preopens: Vec<DirectoryGrantV1>, and networks: Vec<NetworkGrantV1>. No omitted grant is implied.
2. CapabilityLabel and rule IDs are operator-visible ASCII `[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`, unique within their namespace, and contain no path, credential, hostname, or secret. Reject duplicate labels/rule IDs, unknown fields, zero/overflowing limits, non-UTF-8 manifest strings, non-absolute host/guest roots, non-normalized guest roots, duplicate or ancestor/descendant-overlapping guest roots, more than 64 preopens, more than 64 network grants, or more than 1024 destination rules per network grant. AuthorityLimitsV1 explicitly and positively bounds max_live_handles, max_open_directories (including initial preopens), max_open_files, max_open_sockets, and max_total_file_bytes_in_flight; max_open_directories is at most 64 and at least the preopen count, and checked arithmetic proves every configured object/FD ceiling fits the later deterministic FD ranges and RLIMIT_NOFILE.
3. DirectoryGrantV1 is `{ label, host_path, guest_path, rights }`. The supervisor opens host_path exactly once before any jail is entered as a directory FD with O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC; it never sends host_path to the runner. guest_path is the absolute, normalized mount name exported to the runner. Directory rights are the closed least-privilege labels STAT, READ_DIR, OPEN_READ, OPEN_WRITE, CREATE_FILE, CREATE_DIR, REMOVE_FILE, REMOVE_DIR, RENAME_SOURCE, RENAME_TARGET, and READ_LINK. File rights are the closed labels STAT, READ, WRITE, SET_SIZE, and SYNC. A derived file/directory handle carries only the requested subset authorized by its parent; rights can be attenuated but never amplified.
4. Every broker reference stores a tagged ObjectAuthority, not an untyped shared bitset: Event(EventRights), PipeReader(PipeRights), PipeWriter(PipeRights), Directory(DirectoryRights), File(FileRights), Network(NetworkRights), Socket(SocketRights). Event rights are WAIT/ADD/CONSUME; reader endpoints are WAIT/READ; writer endpoints are WAIT/WRITE. Network v1 has TCP_CONNECT only. A connected socket has WAIT/STATUS/SEND/RECEIVE/SHUTDOWN. The kind tag makes using directory bits as socket bits unrepresentable. Every reference also stores session_id and CapabilityLabel; handles remain broker-minted and session-scoped.
5. Negotiation exports a bounded list of broker-minted initial capability descriptors `{handle, kind, label, guest_path?, rights}` only after peer authentication. The runner cannot supply an initial handle. ConnectSocketRequest gains an explicit network_capability handle. Every path operation starts from an explicit directory handle. Broker protocol version is bumped atomically across protocol/wire/local/host; old peers receive UnsupportedVersion before shared-memory activation.
6. Filesystem v1 wire/local/host/core surface is explicit and closed: Directory requests OpenAt, StatAt, ReadDirectory, CreateDirectoryAt, RemoveDirectoryAt, UnlinkFileAt, RenameAt, and ReadlinkAt; File requests ReadAt, WriteAt, Stat, SetSize, and Sync. OpenAt carries path flags, CREATE/EXCLUSIVE/TRUNCATE/DIRECTORY flags, and requested tagged rights. Data uses the existing bounded shared-buffer leases. Hard-link and symlink creation are intentionally UnsupportedOperation in v1; they are not silently passed through.
7. Broker-relative paths are UTF-8, at most 4096 bytes, use `/`, and contain no empty, `.` or `..` component and no leading `/`; the base itself is addressed by its existing handle, not by `.`. Final symlink following is opt-in. Every descendant resolution uses Linux openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, O_NOFOLLOW when final-follow is absent, and the original/derived directory FD; lexical canonicalization is never an authorization decision. Internal symlinks may resolve only while the kernel proves the result remains beneath the preopen. No fallback path walker is permitted.
8. NetworkGrantV1 is `{ label, uses, rules }`; v1 accepts only TCP_CONNECT and numeric IPv4 SocketAddressV4. DestinationRuleV1 is an ordered `{ id, action: allow|deny, cidr, inclusive_port_ranges }`; first match wins and the implicit terminal rule is deny. CIDRs and port ranges are canonicalized and validated at load time. DNS, IPv6, bind, listen, accept, UDP, raw sockets, and reconnect are explicitly unsupported in v1 and fail before a host syscall.
9. The per-destination seam is the total, in-process SocketPolicy hook `authorize(SocketPolicyContext) -> SocketPolicyDecision`, where context carries principal label, network capability label, NetworkUse::TcpConnect, protocol/family, and the exact canonical numeric destination; decision is Allow{rule_id} or Deny{rule_id_or_default, reason}. Production installs the immutable manifest evaluator; default construction installs DenyAll. The hook runs after handle/kind/rights validation and immediately before the one nonblocking host connect syscall. A denial performs no socket syscall, leaves the socket Unconnected, and returns ErrorCode::PolicyDenied. SocketError is reserved for host/network outcomes; remove the duplicate SocketError::PolicyDenied meaning. A hook panic is caught before connect and fatally fails that association with Internal, so no allow can be synthesized from policy failure.
10. On allowed connect, the socket object records the authorizing network capability identity and exact remote endpoint before exposing Connected/Connecting. Subsequent send/receive authority comes only from that connected socket; it cannot change destination. If DNS is ever added, the invariant already fixes its shape: name lookup is a separate denied-by-default capability and every resolved numeric address must be checked after resolution and before connect; a hostname check alone can never authorize an IP.
11. litebox_broker_local gains directory/file/socket typed adapters; litebox/src/broker/mod.rs::BrokerControl and BrokerLocalControl gain the matching bounded calls. The runner mounts one broker-backed filesystem at each exported guest_path and routes broker-backed TCP sockets through the negotiated Network capability. Host paths and policy internals never cross the local boundary.

PRECONDITIONS
* The accepted connection has already passed validate_peer_process against the exact Child PID and setup_connection has produced HostGuaranteed; an unauthenticated/unknown credential receives no capabilities.
* BrokerPolicyV1 is a regular, no-symlink operator input whose file and parent components are owned by root or the invoking deployment identity and are not group/world writable. All preopen roots are opened successfully before runner launch.
* Linux openat2 is available whenever directory_preopens is non-empty. Missing openat2 is a startup UnsupportedPlatform failure, never a racy userspace fallback.
* Capability and FD limits are internally consistent and fit BrokerCoreLimits and the later jail's computed RLIMIT_NOFILE.

INVARIANTS
* Default is zero ambient filesystem/network authority. Authority exists only as a session-owned, kind-tagged broker handle descended from a manifest grant.
* Principal authentication, capability selection, rights checks, path confinement, and destination decision all precede the host side effect. Denial is side-effect-free.
* Handle guessing, reuse after close, cross-session use, and wrong-kind use reveal no other session state and cannot reach a host object.
* Rights are monotone decreasing across derivation; close/session teardown releases the host FD/socket and all quota charges exactly once.
* An absolute path, malformed path, symlink/magic-link escape, or destination without an Allow match cannot reach an ambient host path/network syscall.
* Existing event/pipe behavior is available only when the manifest explicitly grants its object class; there is no compatibility `ObjectRights::all()` bypass.
* Every request and response remains bounded by manifest limits, wire bounds, shared-buffer bounds, and checked arithmetic.

FAILURE BEHAVIOR
* CLI/schema/ownership/duplicate/limit/preopen validation fails before runner spawn, emits one structured `policy_load_failed` reason, and exits nonzero; no permissive policy is substituted.
* Unknown, stale, foreign-session, or wrong-kind handles return UnknownObject. A known same-session handle missing the required tagged right returns InvalidRights. Explicit path/destination policy denial returns PolicyDenied. Malformed or oversized wire/path input aborts the association as MalformedRequest. Host filesystem and network failures use closed FilesystemError and SocketError enums, never raw errno passthrough.
* Failed open/create/connect never installs a handle, consumes quota, truncates a file, or changes socket state. Partial data operations report the exact completed byte count under existing shared-buffer lease rules.
* Policy hook panic/internal invariant failure occurs before the host action and aborts the association; the userland supervisor then treats broker loss as fatal to its runner.

OBSERVABILITY
* A dedicated inherited audit FD emits newline-delimited JSON schema `litebox.broker.audit.v1`; stderr is the human fallback. Startup records policy SHA-256, counts/limits, principal/capability labels, and opened preopen identities without host paths. Every authority-creating decision (initial export, OpenAt/create/rename/remove, socket connect) records monotonic decision_id, instance/session/request IDs, principal label, capability label, operation, allow/deny, rule ID/reason, duration, and protocol error. Relative paths are not logged; record length plus HMAC-SHA-256 under a fresh 256-bit per-instance key sampled with getrandom before runner launch, carried only in the sealed bootstrap, never emitted, and zeroized at teardown. Numeric network endpoint is logged because it is the authorization subject. Never log payload bytes, host paths, credentials, or manifest contents.
* Periodic/final audit snapshots expose allow_total, deny_total by reason, policy_error_total, live_handles, open_files, open_sockets, and quota high-water marks. A clean session-final snapshot must return all live/open counters to baseline. Audit write failure fails the association in production mode rather than running unobserved.

PLATFORM SUPPORT
* Production wiring is Linux x86_64, matching litebox_runner_linux_userland's cfg. Protocol/core representations remain no_std/portable. On non-Linux, or on Linux without required openat2 when preopens exist, startup returns UnsupportedPlatform and never silently runs with ambient access.
* v1 supports broker-backed numeric IPv4 TCP client streams and the listed filesystem operations only; every other family/protocol/operation is a closed UnsupportedOperation before host action.

POSTCONDITIONS
* A successfully negotiated session exposes exactly the manifest's initial labeled capabilities and no host path; every derived object can be traced to one initial grant and has no stronger rights.
* Real guest filesystem/TCP operations traverse local -> wire -> host -> policy -> confined host object and return stable broker errors; event/pipe compatibility also traverses explicit grants.
* Session/process teardown leaves no live broker reference, FD/socket, shared-buffer lease, or quota charge.

LIVE PRODUCTION ACCEPTANCE (no synthetic test files)
On a real Linux x86_64 host, launch the release litebox-broker-userland and release litebox_runner_linux_userland through their production Unix/memfd/control-ring path with one BrokerPolicyV1. The manifest grants: event/pipe; a read-only preopen mounted at `/cap/ro`; a read-write preopen mounted at `/cap/rw`; and TCP_CONNECT only to one loopback server address/port.
1. A real guest reads an allowed file, writes/creates only under `/cap/rw`, and receives permission denial for write under `/cap/ro`, an absolute path, `..`, a same-name path outside a grant, and internal symlinks escaping the root. The outside sentinel remains byte-identical.
2. The guest completes connect/send/receive against the allowlisted loopback listener. An adjacent port and a non-allowlisted address return policy denial, and listener/packet counters prove no connect syscall/SYN reached either denied endpoint.
3. A stale/guessed/cross-session/wrong-kind handle returns UnknownObject; requesting a stronger derived right returns InvalidRights; broker/runner remain healthy after recoverable denials.
4. Existing event and pipe operations still complete only with their explicit manifest grants; removing either grant makes creation PolicyDenied.
5. Audit JSONL is machine-parseable, ties every allow/deny to policy hash, labels, request and rule/reason, contains no host path/payload, and final live/open counters return to baseline. `/proc/<broker-pid>/fd` returns to its startup census after session teardown.
Acceptance is the observed production binary/transport/guest behavior and host sentinel/network state, not a unit or synthetic test suite.

CRITICAL CURRENT FILES/SYMBOLS
litebox_broker_userland/src/main.rs::{linux_main::main,serve_runner,accept_runner_stream,dispatch_requests,run_worker}; litebox_broker_transport_linux_userland/src/unix_socket/host.rs::{validate_peer_process,peer_process_id,UnixStreamHostSetupChannel::from_host_guaranteed}; litebox_broker_host/src/lib.rs::{setup_connection,BrokerHostAssociation::execute_request,handle_request}; litebox_broker_core/src/policy.rs::{PolicyProfile,PolicyEngine,PolicyEngine::principal_object_rights}; litebox_broker_core/src/session.rs::{CallerCredential,ObjectRights,ObjectReference,ObjectEntry,BrokerSession::create_object_reference,BrokerSession::authorize_use_object}; litebox_broker_core/src/lib.rs::{BrokerCore,BrokerCoreLimits}; litebox_broker_protocol/src/message.rs::{BrokerOperation,SocketRequest,BrokerResult}; litebox_broker_protocol/src/socket.rs::{CreateSocketRequest,ConnectSocketRequest,SocketConnectionStatus,SocketError}; litebox_broker_local/src/lib.rs::BrokerLocal; litebox/src/broker/mod.rs::{BrokerControl,BrokerLocalControl}; litebox_runner_linux_userland/src/{lib.rs::run,broker.rs::connect}.

ready_wave.description: User-requested (2026-08-10), split from the combined 'interactive keyboard input' request since this half is Windows-only and cannot be hardware-verified on this session's Apple Silicon macOS machine (no Windows host available). Explored: litebox_shim_windows/src/syscalls/condrv.rs (the ConDrv/console-driver IOCTL handler) only recognizes the LaunchServer handshake IOCTL (lines 303-362) and returns NOT_SUPPORTED for everything else, including any real input-delivery or cursor-position-report (CPR) IOCTLs. A TODO(condrv-shared-console) at litebox_shim_windows/src/lib.rs:619-621 already flags moving console ownership to shared/broker state as unfinished. No hits anywhere in the repo for 'cooked', 'CPR', 'ConPTY', or CreatePseudoConsole -- this is a clean-slate implementation, not a targeted bug fix. Needs a real Windows host to implement and verify against real console API behavior (ReadConsoleInput, cooked vs raw mode line editing, ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT/ENABLE_LINE_INPUT flags, and CPR escape-sequence replies for cursor-position queries) -- deferred from this pass, same reasoning already applied to the Windows CI job investigation and the Windows-only items in this same request batch.
